rec.title: Exposés de post-doctorants
rec.speaker: Felipe Gambardella, Lyuhui Wu, Lucas Mann
rec.abstract:
14h00-14h40: Felipe Gambardella
Title: Some diophantine and cohomological aspects of fields
Abstract: Over the years, cohomological tools such as Galois cohomology or the Brauer—Manin obstruction have shown to be fruitful in the study rational points and others Diophantine properties. Conversely, Diophantine features such as Tsen's C_1 property or the property of being PAC determine the cohomology of a field partially. In spite of the positive results, the precise relationship between Cohomology and Diophantine properties is not fully understood. In this talk, I will present some Diophantine and Cohomological invariants with a particular focus on their interaction and the variety of tools appearing in their computation.
14h45-14:25: Lyuhui Wu
Title: Theory of non-archimedean plurisubharmonic functions
Abstract: Understanding the asymptotic behavior of Kähler metrics along degenerating families of complex projective manifolds is a fundamental problem in complex geometry. Non-archimedean pluripotential theory, that is, the theory of plurisubharmonic functions in the non-archimedean setting, provides a powerful framework for investigating this problem. In this talk, I will give an overview of non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and discuss some of its applications to complex geometry.
15h30-16h10: Lucas Mann
Title: Six-functor formalisms and representation theory
Abstract: Six-functor formalisms are a powerful tool to capture the formal properties of a cohomology theory. In recent years, the development of abstract six-functor formalisms has shown that they capture a surprising amount of constructions and results, including well-known finiteness conditions and dualities. Even more, six-functor formalisms can be applied in places outside traditional cohomology theories, for example in representation theory. In this talk I will survey the theory of six-functor formalisms and discuss its applications to representations and the local Langlands program.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Propagation d’états cohérents en temps long et application à des estimées de propagateurs
rec.speaker: Roméo Taboada
rec.abstract:
Dans cette thèse, nous présenterons des asympotiques d'états cohérents propagés par une équation de Schrödinger associée à un Hamiltonien donné. Ces résultats étendent ceux obtenus par Combescure et Robert, dans lesquels un état cohérent propagé est approché dans la limite $h\to 0$ par des paquets gaussiens déformés dits états cohérents comprimés. Cette description reste valide pour des temps $t$ pouvant tendre vers l'infini quand $h\to 0$, dans le régime $|t|\leq |\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ où $\lambda_0$ est l'exposant de Lyapunov maximal de la dynamique classique. L'échec de cette approximation au temps $|\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ est relié à la flexion des paquets d'ondes évolués : une fois étalés à l'échelle $h^{1/3}$, les états comprimés ne founissent plus une description appropriée. Pour obtenir une représentation valide jusqu'à des temps $|t|\leq C|\log h|$ avec un plus grand $C$ (par exemple jusqu'au temps d'Ehrenfest $|\log h|/(2\lambda_0)$ où un étalement à des échelles macroscopiques est autorisé), on ajoute des hypothèses sur le flot $\Phi_t$ associé à la dynamique classique, imposant des contraintes sur les directions d'élongation. La description obtenue met en évidence que les états propagés ne doivent plus être considérés comme microlocalisés en un point mais plutôt le long d'une sous-variété isotrope (correspondant à des directions instables).
Ces résultats seront ensuite appliqués à l'étude de l'équation des ondes amorties sur une variété Anosov, on expliquera comment une telle asymptotique d'états cohérents propagés peut être utilisée pour obtenir des estimées de propagateurs, permettant d'obtenir un trou spectral et des estimées de résolvante pour l'opérateur associé, et ainsi de montrer la décroissance exponentielle de l'énergie des solutions.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L8

rec.title: Scattering and smoothing for the two-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
rec.speaker: Muyuan Lyu
rec.abstract:
Scattering theory describes the large-time behavior of nonlinear evolution equations through comparison with a linear flow. This raises a further question: can the nonlinear correction to the asymptotic state be smoother than the initial data?
I will begin with an introduction to scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, highlighting several developments that motivate this question. I will then present a deterministic smoothing result for the two-dimensional cubic equation. Assuming that a solution scatters in the harmonic Sobolev space (\mathcal H^s), with (s>0), the difference between its scattering state and its initial datum belongs to (\mathcal H^{s+\sigma}) for every (0<\sigma<\min{2s,1}). The proof combines the lens transform, which turns the large-time problem into a finite-time endpoint problem, with bilinear Strichartz estimates and harmonic spectral analysis. The emphasis will be on the mechanism behind the regularity gain. The talk is intended for graduate students in analysis, with no prior familiarity with nonlinear scattering required.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Matrix entries, unipotents and linearity of amalgams
rec.speaker: Konstantin Tsouvalas
rec.abstract: n this talk, we consider the question of whether amalgams of linear groups are still linear. By analyzing matrix entries and unipotent elements, we will discuss linearity for specific algebraic "doubles" and obtain new examples of finitely generated, residually finite, non-linear groups. This includes new examples of linear groups constructed by combining together precompact groups and lattices in real semisimple Lie groups. This is joint work with Sami Douba.

rec.title: Autour des ensembles limites de groupes non Zariski-denses
rec.speaker: Blandine Galiay
rec.abstract:
Étant donné un groupe de Lie semisimple réel G et un sous-groupe discret Gamma de G, l'ensemble limite de Gamma dans le bord de Fürstenberg de G est l'ensemble des limites de suites divergentes dans Gamma. Comme un tel ensemble est Gamma-invariant, si Gamma est Zariski-dense, alors son ensemble limite l'est (voir par exemple [Benoist, '97]). La réciproque de cette implication ne paraît pas évidente, étant donnée la nature essentiellement dynamique (et non algébrique) de l'ensemble limite. Lorsque G est de rang 1, il est connu que la réciproque est vraie. Dans une collaboration avec Sami Douba et Joaquin Lema, nous démontrons que ce n'est plus le cas lorsque G est de rang supérieur. Nous cherchons alors quelles conditions algébriques, dynamiques ou géométriques imposer sur l'ensemble limite d'un groupe, pour pouvoir capter sa Zariski-densité. Dans cet exposé, j'expliquerai la construction de sous-groupes non Zariski-denses avec un ensemble limite Zariski-dense, dans le cas où G=SL(3, R). Dans un second temps, j'expliquerai pourquoi, sous certaines hypothèses de sous-algébricité/transversalité, on peut déduire la Zariski-densité d'un sous-groupe de G de celle de son ensemble limite.
Café culturel 13h05 par Nicolas Tholozan.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 2L8

rec.title: Training deep Transformers: mean-field models and convergence analysis
rec.speaker: Raphael Barboni
rec.abstract:
Transformers have become the dominant architecture in modern machine learning, yet the theoretical understanding of their training dynamics remains limited, especially for deep architectures with many layers and Attention heads. I will present a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing gradient-based training of Transformers in the overparameterized regime, where depth, width and context length tend to infinity. This mean-field model features two types of measure representations: token distributions evolving through layers (measures over the token space), and Attention parameters at each layer (measures over the parameter space). Our contributions are twofold: (i) We prove the well-posedness of gradient flow curves in a conditional Wasserstein metric space, establishing a rigorous foundation for gradient-based Transformer training. (ii) We prove convergence of gradient flow towards global minima when the initial training risk is sufficiently low. A key technical contribution is providing necessary and sufficient conditions for injectivity of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) for Attention mechanisms: we show that NTK injectivity is equivalent to linear independence of log-sum-exp functions modulo affine functions, a condition satisfied by diverse token distributions, including discrete distributions, uniform distributions, and Gaussian mixtures.
These results builds on joint works with M. de Hoop, T. Furuya, G. Peyré and F.-X. Vialard.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Cavu theorems or ‘How to get away with « délit d’initié »’.
rec.speaker: Victor Turmel
rec.abstract:
Le séminaire des doctorants se propose de fournir aux doctorants une occasion de s'ouvrir aux autres domaines des mathématiques que le leur. A chaque séance, un intervenant réalise un exposé sur un fait standard de leur domaine d'étude, de niveau adapté à l'ensemble des doctorants.
Le but de cette présentation est d’introduire les outils développés en théorie des jeux, qui est l’étude mathématique des comportements stratégiques. En particulier, on s’intéressera aux jeux répétés avec asymétrie d’information, qui mettent en évidence les enjeux spécifiques de la discipline. On démontre le théorème clef de cette classe de jeux (le théorème du « cavu »), qui explique comment exploiter l’ignorance d’un adversaire, sans que ladite exploitation n’informe l’adversaire. Ce théorème est une porte d’entrée vers les jeux différentiels, qui forment un trait d’union entre théorie des jeux et certaines équations de type Hamilton Jacobi.
----
The PhD students seminar aims to provide PhD students with an opportunity to explore other areas of mathematics beyond their own. At each session, a speaker gives a presentation on a standard topic in their field of study, at a level suitable for all phd students.
he aim of this talk is to introduce the tools developed in game theory, the mathematical study of strategic behaviour. We focus on repeated games with asymmetric information, which bring out the issues specific to the field. We prove the key theorem for this class of games, the “cav u” theorem. It explains how to exploit an opponent’s ignorance without that exploitation revealing information to the opponent. This theorem is a gateway to differential games, which link game theory and Hamilton–Jacobi equations.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 2L8

rec.title: Homotopy reconstruction: how we expanded on the seminal results of Niyogi, Smale, and Weinberger
rec.speaker: Hana Dal Poz Kouřimská
rec.abstract:
In this talk I will walk you through how we extended and strengthened the seminal work by Niyogi, Smale, and Weinberger on the learning of the homotopy type from a sample of an underlying space. In their work, Niyogi, Smale, and Weinberger studied samples of \(C^2\) manifolds with positive reach embedded in \(\mathbb{R}^d\). We extend their results in the following ways:
First, we consider both manifolds of positive reach --- a more general setting than \(C^2\) manifolds --- and sets of positive reach embedded in \(\mathbb{R}^d\). The sample P of such a set S does not have to lie directly on it. Instead, we assume that the two one-sided Hausdorff distances --- ε and δ --- between P and S are bounded. We provide explicit --- and tight --- bounds in terms of ε and δ, that guarantee that there exists a parameter r such that the union of balls of radius r centred at the sample P deformation-retracts to S. If time allows we will consider homotopy learning in a significantly more general setting --- we investigate sets of positive reach and submanifolds of positive reach embedded in a Riemannian manifold with bounded sectional curvature. To this end we introduce a new version of the reach in the Riemannian setting inspired by the cut locus. Yet again, we provide tight bounds on ε and δ for both cases (submanifolds as well as sets of positive reach), exhibiting the tightness by an explicit construction.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, online

rec.title: On the well-posedness of a Cauchy problem for an operator associated with a geometric brownian motion
rec.speaker: Moustapha Agne
rec.abstract: This talk is about an initial value problem of the Schrodinger type but instead of the Laplacian we consider a differential operator which is the infinitesimal generator of a geometric brownian motion. We aim at establishing the well-posedness for an $L^2$ initial data. We present Strichartz estimates of the eventual solution in weighted $L^p$-spaces. The following part of the talk is dedicated to the proof of the well-posedness issue.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 0A2

rec.title: Quadratic terms, Lie brackets and local controllability
rec.speaker: Karine Beauchard
rec.abstract:
We study the small-time local controllability, in the vicinity of an equilibrium, of a nonlinear scalar-input system. A natural strategy consists in proving the controllability of the linearized system at the equilibrium and conclude with a local inversion argument. When this linearized system is not controllable, it is necessary to study the quadratic term.
In this talk, we link several recent results on this subject. We also propose a unified methodology to prove quadratic obstructions to local controllability, that relies on systematic drift estimates.
For finite-dimensional control systems, quadratic terms only generate obstructions to controllability: they introduce coercive drifts in the dynamics, quantified by negative integer Sobolev norms of the control, linked to Lie brackets.
In infinite dimension, the same obstructions persist, but two new behaviors occur. First, quadratic obstructions can be due to drifts quantified by other norms (for instance fractional Sobolev norms); their geometric interpretation is challenging. Second, and more strikingly, small-time local controllability can sometimes be recovered from the quadratic expansion.
The tools developed for these studies are also used to understand the influence of higher order terms on the small-time local controllability, for single or multi-input systems, and in other research areas.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L8

rec.title: Sur le théorème de Kaluza
rec.speaker: Philippe Marchal
rec.abstract: Soit une $f(x)$ une série entière à coefficients positifs telle que $f(x)>0$. Un théorème dû à Kaluza (1928) montre que si la suite des coefficients est log-convexe, alors la série entière $1/f$ a tous ses coefficients négatifs, à part le coefficient constant. Nous montrons que cette condition de log-convexité n'est pas nécessaire et exhibons des contre-exemples en utilisant les processus de renouvellement discrets.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Importance Sampling
rec.speaker: Simon Coste
rec.abstract: Importance sampling is a technique for estimating integrals of the form E[φ(X)], where X has a density g that may be difficult to sample from or otherwise handle. The simplest Monte Carlo method would consist of generating i.i.d. samples X_1,...,X_n from g and averaging the values φ(X_i). By contrast, Importance Sampling (IS) consists of using samples Y_1,...,Y_n from another density, say f, and averaging the reweighted values φ(Y_i) * g(Y_i)/f(Y_i). This works provided that f is positive when g is positive, but there is no free lunch: the price to pay can be high variance and poor accuracy. In this expository talk, I will (1) explain when and how to use IS, with practical examples from chemistry and combinatorics; (2) explain how to measure the accuracy of IS and determine the sample size n needed for an accurate estimation of E[φ(X)], locally for a specific φ; and (3) explain how to measure this accuracy globally using Wasserstein distances, even in infinite dimensions for stochastic diffusions, where "importance sampling" is known under the name of "Girsanov theorem".
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Les relocalisations préférentielles améliorent la survie
rec.speaker: Jean Bertoin
rec.abstract:
Nous étudions une modification de l’évolution d’une chaîne de Markov sous-stochastique qui consiste en des relocalisations aléatoires en des états visités précédemment, et son impact sur la survie.
Le résultat central est que de telles relocalisations préférentielles augmentent le taux de persistance, c’est-à-dire que la probabilité de survie décroît plus lentement que pour la chaîne de référence dépourvue de relocalisations, et que cette amélioration est stricte sous des hypothèses très générales. Nous établissons des minorations explicites du rapport des taux de persistance lorsque la loi de relocalisation est fortement dispersée. L’analyse repose sur les propriétés ergodiques de chaînes dites à connexions complètes, ainsi que sur une approche de Feynman--Kac pour estimer la persistance.
Travail en collaboration avec Martin Minchev
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Uncertainty and unique continuation for dispersive PDEs at two time points
rec.speaker: Diego Fiorletta
rec.abstract:
Imposing too strong simultaneous decay or localization constraints on a function and its Fourier transform causes the function to vanish identically (Uncertainty Principle). The same applies to a solution to some dispersive evolutionary PDE if similar constraints are imposed on its profile at two different time points.
In the first part of the talk, I will introduce a manifestation of the Uncertainty Principle, the Benedicks-Amrein-Berthier Theorem. The $L^2$ norm on $\mathbb{R}^n$ of a function is controlled by the sum of the $L^2$ norms of the function and its Fourier transform observed outside sets of finite Lebesgue measure (Amrein-Berthier). In particular, no non-zero function supported on a set of finite Lebesgue measure can have a Fourier transform with the same property (Benedicks).
In the second part I will show how the above statements translate into qualitative and even quantitative unique continuation results when the Fourier transform is replaced by the propagator, evaluated at a non-zero time T, associated to some dispersive PDE, in particular considering linear and non-linear instances of the Schr\"odinger equation.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: On the Euler characteristic and simplicial volume of convex projective manifolds
rec.speaker: Grazia Rago
rec.abstract:
A famous conjecture of Gromov states that, for a closed oriented aspherical manifold, the vanishing of the simplicial volume implies the vanishing of the Euler characteristic.
In this talk, we prove this conjecture for closed oriented real convex projective manifolds by explicitly constructing a bounded cocycle representing their Euler class.
The talk is based on joint work with Michelle Bucher and Stefano Francaviglia.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, Salle 2L8

rec.title: Universal minimal flow of the automorphism group of the regular tree of infinite valency
rec.speaker: Flore Le Roux
rec.abstract: The universal minimal flow of a topological group is "the biggest" compact space on which the group acts continuously and minimally. It thus captures a lot of information about the topological dynamics of the group. In this talk, I will determine that space in the case of the group of automorphisms of the regular simplicial tree of infinite valency.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, Salle 2L8

rec.title: Équations de Painlevé : fonctions spéciales, séries divergentes et résurgence
rec.speaker: Mohamad Alamaddine
rec.abstract:
Les équations de Painlevé sont des équations différentielles non linéaires qui interviennent aujourd’hui dans des domaines variés. Après une introduction à ces équations et à leurs applications, je présenterai leurs solutions formelles en présence d’un petit paramètre et expliquerai comment la résurgence permet d’aborder leur divergence. L’exposé aboutira à un théorème d’existence et d’unicité de ces solutions formelles, sous des hypothèses de non-dégénérescence, accompagné de bornes factorielles sur leurs coefficients.
Aucune connaissance préalable des équations de Painlevé ou de la résurgence ne sera supposée.

rec.title: The Diederich--Fornæss index and global regularity of the $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problem
rec.speaker: Bingyuan Liu
rec.speaker_affiliation: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley.
rec.abstract:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain. The $\bar\partial$-Neumann problem is Hodge theory with boundary on $\Omega$. Its solution operator $N_q$ is globally regular, i.e., preserves $C^\infty(\overline{\Omega})$, on strongly pseudoconvex domains (Kohn), but not on the worm domains (Christ). Since the 1990s it has been conjectured that global regularity follows when the Diederich--Fornæss index of $\Omega$ equals $1$. This index is the supremum of $\eta\in(0,1]$ such that $-(-\rho)^\eta$ is plurisubharmonic near $b\Omega$ for some defining function $\rho$.
I will present joint work with Emil Straube. Suppose that, for some $1\le q_0\le n-1$, the $q_0$-sums of the Levi eigenvalues are comparable, and the index is $1$. Then $N_q$ and the Bergman projections $P_{q-1}$, for $q_0\le q\le n$, are continuous in every Sobolev space $W^s(\Omega)$. In particular, the conjecture holds in $\mathbb{C}^2$, and there having index one is preserved under biholomorphisms. The key point is that index one gives a self-bounded gradient condition, which is weak pointwise but suffices in an integrated $L^2$ form.

rec.title: Small noise limit for Entropic Variational Mean Field Games
rec.speaker: Alessandro Cosenza
rec.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: Variational mean-field games are a class of mean-field games whose equilibria can be characterized as minimizers of a global energy functional combining agents’ individual costs and collective interactions. In the classical formulation, the energy functional resembles the (Eulerian) Benamou-Brenier type formula for entropic optimal transport, with the addition of a convex term which encompasses the interaction between the agents. In analogy with entropic OT, Benamou, Carlier, Di Marino and Nenna recently proposed an equivalent (Lagrangian) entropy-minimization formulation of the problem. The aim of this talk is two-fold. First, we investigate the small-noise Gamma limit for the lagrangian entropy-minimization formulation, establishing Gamma convergence of noisy second order mean-field games towards its deterministic first order counterpart. This also translates into a dynamical proof of the convergence of entropic OT to classical OT. Secondly, we study the original Eulerian problem. We prove a first order energy expansion, which establishes a selection principle for minimizers of the deterministic problem. This is a joint work with Luca Nenna.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, Laboratoire de Mathématiques d'Orsay - Salle 3L15
rec.department: GT Transport optimal - EDP - Machine learning
rec.series_name: GT Transport optimal - EDP - Machine learning

rec.title: The stratified shape
rec.speaker: Marco Volpe
rec.abstract:
In this talk, I will try to address the question of how to do algebraic topology with stratified spaces and schemes in a meaningful way. I will begin by recalling and motivating some of the main historical attempts to approach this question, both in topology and in algebraic geometry, passing through the work of Nash, Quinn, Siebenmann, Edwards–Hastings, Deligne, and, more recently, Lurie and Barwick–Glasman–Haine. I will then propose my own answer, based on a construction I call the stratified shape.
Time permitting, I will discuss some applications of the stratified shape to proper homotopy theory (joint with Georg Lehner), homology manifolds (joint with Markus Land), and a generalization of Lurie's exodromy equivalence (joint with Peter Haine and Guglielmo Nocera).
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Accélération du cycle auto-cohérent en théorie de la fonctionnelle de la densité de Kohn-Sham appliquée à des systèmes complexes
rec.speaker: Clémentine Barat
rec.abstract: La DFT de Kohn-Sham est une méthode très utilisée en physique du solide pour la modélisation des matériaux. La résolution numérique des équations de Kohn-Sham qui lui sont associées est le plus souvent faite par des itérations auto-cohérentes (SCF). Cette thèse porte sur les stratégies de préconditionnement pour les itérations SCF en théorie de la fonctionnelle de la densité de Kohn-Sham (KSDFT). La convergence des itérations SCF est gouvernée par l'opérateur diélectrique adjoint et est ralentie lorsque celui-ci est mal conditionné, c'est-à-dire, a des valeurs propres très petites ou très grandes. Ce conditionnement peut être amélioré avec un préconditionneur, qui approxime l'opérateur diélectrique, et en particulier la susceptibilité non-interagissante qui est le terme coûteux de l'opérateur diélectrique. Trois sources spécifiques de mauvais conditionnement sont étudiées. Dans un premier temps, nous nous sommes intéressés aux problèmes de convergences liés à l'interaction Coulombienne dans les semi-conducteurs inhomogènes. Nous proposons une extension inhomogène du préconditionneur de Resta basé sur une polarisabilité locale. Ensuite, nous nous intéressons aux problèmes de convergence liés aux transitions de phase magnétiques du second ordre. Ce type de transition est associé à une valeur propre nulle de l'opérateur diélectrique et, autour de la transition, on observe des problèmes de convergence caractérisés par un plateau. En nous inspirant du modèle de Stoner, nous proposons un nouveau préconditionneur basé sur une approximation diagonale de la susceptibilité non-interagissante, qui néglige les variations inter-orbitales. Ce préconditionneur, implémenté dans Abinit et dans DFTK, permet de réduire les problèmes de convergence autour des transitions de phase ferromagnétiques. Enfin, nous traitons les problèmes de convergence liés à la présence d'orbitales localisées. En utilisant la règle d'or de Fermi, qui apparaît pour des résonances de Feshbach, nous proposons un modèle pour la susceptibilité non-interagissante. Ce modèle préliminaire est testé, avec succès, sur une impureté de manganèse dans du cuivre.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L8

rec.title: Meanfield limit with singular interactions
rec.speaker: Toan Nguyen
rec.abstract: The seminar shall present some overview on the topic of deriving the Vlasov theory from many body particle systems in the meanfield limit, focusing on singular interactions. In particular, the focus will be more on reviewing available mathematical frameworks and presenting a recent weighted energy-based approach that allows to cover the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in a joint work with P. T. Nam.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L8

rec.title: Expected Batch Optimal Transport Plans and Consequences for Flow Matching
rec.speaker: Kimia Nadjahi
rec.abstract: Solving optimal transport (OT) on random minibatches is a common surrogate for exact OT in large-scale learning. In flow matching, this surrogate is used to obtain OT-like couplings that can straighten probability paths and reduce numerical integration cost. Yet, the population-level coupling induced by repeated minibatch OT remains only partially understood. We formalize this coupling as the expected batch OT plan, obtained by averaging empirical OT plans over independent minibatches. We then establish its large-batch consistency and, in the semidiscrete case relevant to generative modeling, derive rates for both the transport-cost bias and the convergence of the expected batch OT plan to the OT plan. For flow matching, this yields a population coupling whose induced velocity field is regular enough to define a unique flow from the source to the discrete target. We finally quantify how OT batch size interacts with numerical integration in a tractable two-atom model and in synthetic and image experiments. This talk is based on a joint work with Samuel Boïté and Julie Delon:https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12174
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Lagrangian Klein bottles in S^2 x S^2
rec.speaker: Nikolas Adaloglou
rec.abstract:
The study of Lagrangian submanifolds is a central theme in symplectic geometry. In this talk, after a brief introduction on the basics of symplectic geometry, we are going to study Lagrangian submanifolds in \(S^2\times S^2\), equipped with standard symplectic forms. Our goal is to understand which symplectic forms on \(S^2\times S^2\) carry Lagrangian Klein bottles. We will focus mainly on constructing the Klein bottles, using certain techniques from the theory of Lagrangian torus fibrations. This theory effectively reduces many constructive problems into problems of classical affine geometry of the plane.
Afterwards, I will explain how to obstruct the existence of some Lagrangian Klein bottles, using pseudoholomorphic curve techniques.
Together, the obstructive part and the constructive part completely determine which symplectic forms in \(S^2\times S^2\) carry a Lagrangian Klein bottle.
Café culturel à 13h05 par Patrick Massot
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 2L8

rec.title: Long-time behavior of small solutions of NLS with non-generic potentials in 1D
rec.speaker: Neba Polneau
rec.abstract: The goal of this talk is to present an almost global result on the long-time behavior of small solutions to the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the presence of an external non-generic potential. Roughly speaking, non-generic potentials are potentials that exhibit a resonance at the bottom of the spectrum of the associated linear Schrödinger operator. These resonances make the analysis more involved, as we will see. To handle these issues, we use the distorted Fourier transform and introduce a modified eigenfunction basis tailored to the non-generic setting. We then discuss the nonlinear analysis through what we call the Nonlinear Spectral Distribution (NSD), a tempered distribution that encodes the nonlinear interactions in distorted Fourier space. Finally, we examine some nonlinear estimates specific to the non-generic setting.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Nouveaux modèles en dynamique des foules : à la frontière du calcul des variations, des lois de conservation et du transport optimal.
rec.speaker: Nicolas Masson
rec.abstract:
L’objet de cette thèse est d’étudier de nouveaux modèles macroscopiques de mouvements de foule.
La modélisation mathématique des mouvements de foules répond à des enjeux multiples, en ce qu’elle permet la meilleure compréhension de phénomènes essentiels pour la conception de bâtiments, la planification urbaine, ou encore la gestion d’événements culturels et sportifs d’envergure. Elle revêt en ce sens un intérêt substantiel qui n’a cessé de croître au cours de ces dernières décennies, lui conférant un statut de champ de recherche à part entière au croisement des mathématiques, de la physique, des sciences sociales ou encore de l’informatique.
L’objectif des travaux entrepris durant cette thèse était de développer un nouveau modèle mathématique de dynamique des foules à l’échelle macroscopique en y intégrant une notion d’inhibition. Ce nouveau modèle reprend les ingrédients principaux de celui développé par Maury, Roudneff-Chupin et Santambrogio en 2010 : la foule y est décrite par une densité - soumise à une contrainte de congestion, cherchant à se déplacer à une vitesse donnée appelée vitesse souhaitée. Cette vitesse pouvant être incompatible avec la contrainte de congestion, on fait l’hypothèse que la foule adopte une vitesse « effective », choisie de sorte à coïncider avec la vitesse souhaitée là où la foule n’atteint pas le seuil de congestion (modèle « hard ») tout en préservant la contrainte là où le seuil est saturé.
L’apport majeur de ce nouveau modèle réside dans le choix de la vitesse effective, que l’on souhaite être de nature à respecter le principe suivant : dans la région saturée, les personnes sont classées selon une hiérarchie, et les individus de priorité la plus élevée se déplacent librement, tandis que les autres adaptent leur dynamique de sorte à respecter la contrainte de congestion, sans influencer les personnes avec un plus haut degré de priorité.
Cependant, un tel modèle pose de nombreuses difficultés mathématiques, qui ont donné lieu à l’adoption de deux approches : une première dite « mécaniste », et une autre dite « sociale ». La première accepte une influence bilatérale des individus avec des niveaux de priorités distincts, tout en conférant un poids progressivement plus élevé aux personnes selon leur degré de priorité, avec un paramètre de raideur déterminant à quel point deux niveaux de priorité différents correspondent à des poids différents. En faisant dégénérer ce paramètre, on arrive à briser la symétrie d’influence et obtenir un modèle qui correspond à nos attentes. La deuxième approche, dite « sociale », intègre directement l’asymétrie d’influence entre les agents, tout en autorisant une adaptation progressive de la vitesse effective à mesure que la densité se rapproche du seuil de congestion (modèle « soft). Cette adaptation se fait également selon un paramètre de raideur, que l’on fait dégénérer afin de retrouver un modèle « hard ».
Nous présenterons les résultats obtenus en utilisant ces deux approches, commenterons le modèle obtenu avec quelques illustrations numériques, tout en mentionnant les nombreux problèmes ouverts qui subsistent.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L8

rec.title: Learning with reject option and applications
rec.speaker: Mohamed Hebiri
rec.abstract:
The reject option is an efficient technique to abstain from prediction when the uncertainty about the label is too high. This may happen, for instance, when classes overlap, images contain several objects, or the input is degraded. In this talk, I will first present learning with reject option in its classical use, and then focus on the case where the rejection rate is bounded, which turns this uncertainty into a controlled quantity. The optimal rule is then characterized and estimated by a plug-in procedure in a semi-supervised setting, where unlabeled data are enough to calibrate the rejection threshold; I will discuss distribution-free guarantees on the rejection rate as well as rates of convergence on the excess-risk highlighting when unlabeled data help.
In the second part, I will argue that the rejected set is not a failure but a signal on where to spend a scarce resource. I will illustrate this with two applications of a different nature: active learning, where rejection identifies the region in which labels should be queried, and early exiting in deep neural networks, where rejection decides which inputs deserve more computation under a fixed computational (and energy) budget. I will conclude with a brief overview of recent uses of abstention in other settings.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Prévision probabiliste par inférence conforme : application à la recharge des véhicules électriques
rec.speaker: Guillaume Principato
rec.abstract:
La thèse vise à quantifier l'incertitude des prévisions pour la recharge des véhicules électriques en adaptant les méthodes d'inférence conforme aux spécificités des données.
La démarche s'articule autour de trois caractéristiques :
(i) la structure hiérarchique des données,
(ii) l'évolution temporelle de leur distribution,
et (iii) l'évolution des infrastructures de recharge dans le temps.
Les données de recharge des VE sont structurées selon des relations d'agrégation, induisant une structure hiérarchique. Une procédure de réconciliation permet d'imposer les contraintes hiérarchiques aux prévisions pour intégrer cette information structurelle. Nous combinons la réconciliation des prévisions avec des méthodes d'inférence conforme et nous montrons que l'étape de réconciliation est bénéfique aux intervalles de prévision qui en découlent.
L'essor des véhicules électriques engendre des évolutions dans la distribution des données de recharge. Dans ce contexte, l'hypothèse sous-jacente à l'inférence conforme n'est plus vérifiée et des extensions adaptatives, mettant à jour séquentiellement les intervalles de prévision, sont alors nécessaires. Nous étudions théoriquement, à travers le prisme de l'approchabilité de Blackwell, les garanties de couverture et de longueur des intervalles produits par ces méthodes adaptatives.
Les infrastructures de recharge sont aussi amenées à évoluer dans le temps (ouvertures, maintenances et fermetures de stations). Ces transformations doivent être prises en compte dans la quantification de l'incertitude des prévisions afin de modéliser la variabilité induite sur l'ensemble de l'infrastructure de recharge. Nous exploitons la structure hiérarchique des données pour inclure la connaissancede l'état de l'infrastructure dans les prévisions et proposons des méthodes d'inférence conforme dont les objectifs de couverture sont conditionnels à l'état de l'infrastructure de recharge.

rec.title: Existence, Uniqueness, Feller Property and Dirichlet form of the Keller-Segel particle system up to blow up
rec.speaker: Yoan Tardy
rec.abstract: The Keller-Segel particle system as defined in \cite{ft} through the Dirichlet form theory (see \cite{f}) consists of N planar Brownian motions interacting through the kernel x\in \rr^2 \mapsto \theta K(x) = -\theta x/\|x\|^2, where θ>0. One particularity of this model is that collisions (i.e. overlapping of particles) occur depending on the value of θ, making the well-posedness of the particle system delicate. In this work, we propose a new notion of solution of this SDE without relying on the Dirichlet form theory and prove uniqueness in law of such solutions. The proof relies on an excursion decomposition of the particle system based on the "barycenter-radius-angle" decomposition in \cite{ft}. As additional results, we prove that the solution is strong Markov, has the Feller property and fits in the definition of solutions in the Dirichlet form sense. Finally we prove that the law of the particle system starting from a configuration where all the particles overlap is explicit.

rec.title: Introduction au Laplacien magnétique sur une variété riemanniene
rec.speaker: Ambre Chabert
rec.abstract: Je commencerai par présenter la correspondance classique-quantique via l'analyse semiclassique, dans le cadre de l'effet d'un champ magnétique sur une particule chargée évoluant dans l'espace euclidien. J'expliquerai ensuite comment l'apparition de "phase shift" non triviaux sur la fonction d'onde quantique (effet Aharonov-Bohm) motive la modélisation du magnétisme sur une variété riemanniene compacte par l'introduction de fibrés hermitiens, et la définition correspondante d'un Laplacien magnétique semiclassique. Enfin, je montrerai une illustration du principe de correspondance dans le cas d'un champs magnétique constant sur une surface hyperbolique, en montrant une transition de phase en fonction des niveaux d'énergie, via l'étude de la concentration maximale des fonctions propres (leur norme L infinie). rec.title: Opers and Non-Linear Integral Equations
rec.speaker: Giovanni Ravazzini
rec.abstract: I will introduce the relation between Hitchin integrable systems, supersymmetric gauge theories and opers on a Riemann surface. I will then show how this relation works in practice in the case of the opers on cylinder, corresponding to the Toda chain and the pure SU(N) gauge theory: I will argue how the three are naturally unified by a Non-Linear Integral Equation (NLIE). I will then move to the example of the four-punctured sphere, showing how a NLIE can be used to solve the (confluent) Heun equation and the associated Riemann-Hilbert problem. Based on [2512.18744] and work in progress with Jörg Teschner, Jonah Baerman, Guido Bonori.

rec.title:
Propriété de Markov pour le profil vertical d’arbres aléatoires étiquetés et modèles de géométrie brownienne.
(Markov property for the vertical profile of random labelled trees and models of Brownian geometry.)
rec.speaker: Alexis Metz-Donnadieu
rec.abstract:
Cette thèse porte sur l’étude de plusieurs modèles discrets et continus de géométrie aléatoire, et plus spécifiquement de modèles d’arbres étiquetés et de cartes aléatoires.
La première partie de l'exposé sera consacrée à l’étude du profil vertical de certains arbres étiquetés aléatoires. Nous expliquerons en quoi un certain processus bidimensionnel, comptant le nombre d’arêtes reliant des sommets d’étiquettes adjacentes, est markovien pour une large classe de modèles d’arbres étiquetés dont les incréments des étiquettes le long des arêtes appartiennent à {-1, 0, 1}. Nous expliquerons comment exploiter cette propriété pour obtenir de nouvelles formules d’énumération dans certaines classes combinatoires d'arbres. Nous nous interesserons également à la limite d’échelle du profil vertical des arêtes de forêts croissantes d’arbres étiquetés aléatoires. Lorsque la loi de reproduction est de variance finie, il est possible d'identifier cette limite à la dérivée et la valeur prise par la densité de la mesure d’occupation d’un super-mouvement brownien. Cela permet d’interpreter nos résultats comme un analogue discret d’une propriété de Markov récemment mise en évidence par Le Gall et Perkins pour le temps local du super-mouvement brownien.
Dans une seconde partie, nous présenterons certaines propriétés des surfaces browniennes. Ces objets sont des espaces métriques aléatoires qui apparaissant comme limite d’échelle de cartes planaires aléatoires. Dans un premier temps, nous donnerons une nouvelle construction de l’anneau brownien libre, la limite d’échelle de triangulations de Boltzmann à deux frontières. Dans un second temps, nous présenterons des résultats liés aux propriétés géométriques fines du bord des surfaces browniennes. Nous montrerons que la mesure uniforme sur le bord des surfaces browniennes est, à une constante multiplicative près, une mesure de Hausdorff associée à une fonction de jauge explicite.

rec.title: Density Functional Theory for classical particle systems
rec.speaker: Simon Le Bouëdec
rec.abstract: We develop the mathematical analysis of the Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory introduced by Manfredi [J. Plasma Phys., 86.2 (2020), 825860201] in the setting of Vlasov equations with a time-dependent exterior potential. In this context, we establish the invertibility of the potential-density mapping for the Vlasov-Poisson system on \(\mathbb{T}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d\) when the exterior potential is (real-)analytic in the space variable. We also recover a Runge-Gross type Theorem for the Vlasov-Poisson equation for smooth (real-)analytic in time exterior potential. The surjectivity of the potential-density mapping is an inverse problem for the Vlasov-Poisson equation: we find the electric field that generates a given density profile on a given time interval.

rec.title: How data geometry shapes flow-based generative models? From tessellations in semi-discrete flow matching to discretization error
rec.speaker: Samuel Hurault
rec.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: In this talk, I’ll present two works on how data geometry shapes generative flows when the velocity field / score is known exactly. With exact velocity field, a flow matching model memorizes the training set and its flow maps (almost) every Gaussian input to a training sample. The inputs mapped to the same sample form a cell. The resulting tessellation resembles the Laguerre diagram of semi-discrete optimal transport (OT). We show that the flow matching (FM) cells are open and simply connected and, under an additional assumption, homeomorphic to an open ball. A planar four-point example shows that, contrary to OT, FM cells can be nonconvex and have curved boundaries. The two tessellations also differ in which cells are unbounded and which pairs of cells share a boundary. In the second part of the talk, I’ll discuss discretization error in flow-based generative models. For Gaussian data, we derive explicit formulas showing how this error explicitly depends on the covariance spectrum and on sampling parameters. These formulas let us tune the sampler to the geometry of the data, as captured by its covariance spectrum. On real image datasets, predictions from Gaussian theory using empirical covariance spectra well capture how optimal parameters vary across datasets.

rec.title: Eisenstein sheaves, Hall categories, and Canonical bases
rec.speaker: Jiangfan YUAN
rec.abstract:
Cette thèse est consacrée à l’étude de la géométrie des champs de faisceaux cohérents sur une courbe projective lisse, des formes automorphes induites par les séries d’Eisenstein et des structures algébriques quantiques encodées par les produits de Hall. Pour une courbe projective lisse, nous considérons le champ des faisceaux cohérents sur cette courbe. L’espace des fonctions sur ce champ peut être vu comme un espace de formes automorphes non ramifiées sur le corps de fonctions de la courbe, où interviennent les modifications de Hecke. Cet espace est muni d’une structure d’algèbre de Hall, définie à partir des extensions de faisceaux cohérents. Nous étudions une catégorification de l’algèbre de Hall de la courbe ainsi que d’une certaine sous-algèbre de Hopf, appelée algèbre de Hall sphérique, qui présente une structure de type groupe quantique. Notre construction suit l’approche de Lusztig dans le cas des carquois et s’appuie sur la construction des faisceaux d’Eisenstein due à Laumon.
Nous construisons une base canonique de l’algèbre de Hall sphérique à partir des constituants simples des faisceaux d’Eisenstein, en démontrant que les éléments ainsi obtenus engendrent l’algèbre et sont linéairement indépendants. La démonstration repose sur la géométrie du champ des faisceaux cohérents et s’appuie sur des résultats et des méthodes du programme de Langlands géométrique ainsi que de la théorie des groupes quantiques.
Nous montrons que l’application de cycle caractéristique induit un isomorphisme entre le groupe de Grothendieck engendré par les classes des faisceaux d’Eisenstein et l’homologie de Borel–Moore en degré maximal du cône nilpotent global. Dans cette démonstration, nous construisons un coproduit sur l’homologie de Borel–Moore à l’aide du faisceau dit de Joyce, un objet fondamental de la théorie de Donaldson–Thomas.
Nous étudions également les propriétés catégoriques des catégories de faisceaux sur le champ des faisceaux cohérents. Nous montrons que ce champ est miraculeux. Cette propriété, qui joue un rôle important dans le programme de Langlands géométrique, donne lieu à une autoéquivalence non triviale de la catégorie des faisceaux. Cette autoéquivalence s’apparente à la dualité d’Alvis–Curtis pour les algèbres de Lie et les groupes.

Presentation of the programme
In recent years, there have been major advances using techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to show, in a rigorous way, that many classical problems in Dynamical Systems are impossible to solve. In this context, a problem that can be set in a Polish space is said to be impossible to solve if it cannot be settled using inherently countable techniques. These groundbreaking results mostly lie in Ergodic Theory, with further significant advances in Topological and Smooth Dynamical Systems.
One main goal of this program is to further enhance interactions between Descriptive Set Theory and Dynamical Systems. It brings together researchers from different fields to settle some of the most famous problems in dynamics dating to the mid-20th century.
A second main goal is to expand applications of the techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to other areas of mathematics.
Week 1
The program begins with lectures introducing the basic impossibility techniques and lectures explaining fundamental concepts in areas of potential applications.
We plan to have tutorials on:
Impossibility Results
Ergodic Theory
Symbolic Dynamics
Smooth Dynamical Systems
Additionally, there will be Research Talks and Expository Lectures (primarily in Ergodic Theory and Descriptive Set Theory).
Week 2
Research talks in Descriptive Set Theory, Ergodic Theory, Smooth and Symbolic Dynamics, as well as Expository Lectures, including on:
Impossibility Results in Ergodic theory
Complexity Theory
Flexibility and Rigidity
Moreover, we will have Problem and Discussion Sessions.

Operator algebras are self-adjoint subalgebras of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space and divide into two main classes: C∗-algebras and von Neumann algebras, according to whether one demands that they are closed in the norm topology or the weak operator topology. When one first meets these algebras, they might look quite similar, but they have different natures as exemplified by the commutative case: via the Gelfand transform, abelian C∗-algebras are algebras of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on a locally compact Hausdorff space, while abelian von Neumann algebras are essentially bounded measurable functions on a measure space. These flavours persist in general. Topological concepts such as dimension and invariants such as K-theory pervade the study of C∗-algebras, while measure-theoretic style methods are often used to study von Neumann algebras.
The long thematic program OA will focus on operator algebras and its still evolving interactions with ergodic theory, topological dynamics, discrete subgroups of semisimple Lie groups, analytic, ergodic and geometric group theory, quantum information theory and random matrices.

Summary
The program centers on the development of a unified understanding of kinetic theory in systems with long‑range interactions, with a particular emphasis on the quantum regime. Long‑range interacting quantum systems—realized experimentally in cold atoms, trapped ions, and polar molecules—exhibit rich dynamical behavior such as metastability, collisionless dynamics, anomalous transport, critical scaling, and turbulence‑like phenomena. These effects are often linked to the Vlasov equation, the collisionless kinetic equation that emerges in the thermodynamic limit. While Vlasov theory is conceptually well established in classical plasma physics, its systematic extension to quantum many‑body systems remains incomplete.
A key scientific motivation of the program is that different communities—mathematical physics, quantum many‑body theory, and AMO physics—address similar non‑equilibrium long‑range phenomena using different methods, preventing the emergence of a unified framework. The program aims to bridge these approaches and clarify conceptual connections between classical and quantum kinetic theories.
The scientific agenda spans several interconnected themes. One major theme is the analysis of classical transport, Vlasov dynamics, and their differences from Boltzmann kinetic theory, including how turbulence, chaos, and long‑range correlations emerge in classical systems. Another theme concerns the quantum generalizations of Vlasov theory, focusing on rigorous derivations and effective equations for quantum gases, including mean‑field and Gross–Pitaevskii limits, and the treatment of finite‑size effects in quantum simulators.
The program will explore non‑equilibrium many‑body dynamics in quantum systems, including quantum turbulence, cascade processes, ergodicity breaking, and anomalous scaling. A related line of inquiry concerns the dynamics of quantum correlations and entanglement, the onset of quantum chaos, and the characterization of universal quasi‑static dynamics in isolated systems. Another scientific direction is the study of effective theories in quantum matter, connecting renormalisation‑group methods with kinetic descriptions and identifying the regimes where classical scaling concepts can illuminate quantum behavior.
On the mathematical side, the program emphasizes rigorous derivations of macroscopic equations from microscopic many‑body dynamics, particularly in long‑range systems, and the formulation of effective transport equations, scaling limits, and mean‑field theories. Renormalisation‑group tools are highlighted both in their rigorous and approximate forms, with the aim of connecting microscopic models to emergent large‑scale behavior in many‑body systems.
Finally, the proposal identifies a scientific need to synthesize current insights into a coherent and predictive quantum kinetic theory for long‑range interactions, and to outline a roadmap of open problems invol

Lectures of the Introductory School
Gross-Pitaevskii equation from Quantum Dynamics
Serena Cenatiempo
While the theory of quantum mechanics describes interactions between the fundamental constituents of matter at microscopic scales, these interactions can lead to fascinating effects at the macroscopic level. Understanding the emergence of these phases from the microscopic description of quantum systems is a fundamental yet highly challenging mathematical problem. In this course, we will explore this challenge in the case of the interacting Bose gas, a system whose low-temperature phases exhibit the so-called Bose-Einstein condensation phenomenon, a phase of matter in which particles remain confined purely due to quantum effects. In particular, we will discuss how the non-linear Hartree and Gross-Pitaevskii equations arise as effective descriptions for the dynamics of a large number of particles exhibiting condensation, in relevant scaling regimes. Time permitting, we will also discuss how quantum fluctuations around the condensate can be accurately described by the so-called Bogoliubov theory.
Renormalization Group for Long-Range Interactions: From the Central Limit Theorem to the O(N) Model
Nicolò Defenu
These lectures introduce the renormalization group (RG) through the lens of long-range interactions, starting from the simplest setting where the method can be carried out exactly. We first formulate the central limit theorem as an RG problem. Summing and rescaling independent random variables defines a flow in the space of probability distributions, whose fixed point for any finite-variance distribution is the Gaussian. This shows how universality emerges, since all microscopic details other than the variance are irrelevant. Relaxing the finite-variance condition reveals a broader family of fixed points, the Lévy stable distributions. For these, the exponent α of the power-law tail alone selects the fixed point, and the Gaussian is recovered for all α ≥ 2. The fixed point therefore follows from the tail, but the converse does not hold, since the Gaussian basin of attraction contains distributions with arbitrary rapidly decaying tails. We then carry these ideas over to interacting field theories by considering the O(N) model with a long-range kinetic term proportional to q^σ. In the large-N limit the theory is solvable, and the competition between the analytic q^2 and the non-analytic q^σ terms produces a threshold σ* separating long-range and short-range universality, in direct analogy with the single-variable problem. Finally, a calculation at order 1/N shows how the anomalous dimension of the short-range fixed point shifts the boundary to σ* = 2 − η_SR. It also explains why the non-analytic term is not renormalized, which fixes η_LR = 2 − σ throughout the long-range regime.

Financial support requests are closed.
Recent trends at the interface between information theory, probability, statistics and high-dimensional geometry raise new questions on the role and importance of entropy in the understanding of both asymptotic and finite range phenomena, in particular towards discrete structures and applications to areas such as quantum information, percolation and random matrices. Recent fruitful developments warrant imminent blossom of new ideas and results in this area in the near future.
Another central theme at the interface of High-Dimensional Probability and Convexity is the study of isoperimetric properties of log-concave measures (including isoperimetric-type questions related to convex bodies). This is not a mere curiosity: convexity and isoperimetry play an important role in the study of concentration of measure phenomena which is crucial for harnessing various high-dimensional effects in Probability as well as several applied fields.
The scope of the semester includes developing further connections between Information Theory and Convexity, in all of the different directions described above. The semester will aim to strengthen these powerful interdisciplinary methods, aiming towards challenging issues and applications, including the isoperimetry questions for log-concave measures, and super-concentration properties of models from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
The semester’s objective is to foster cross-fertilization between probability, analysis, information theory and convex geometry (continuous and discrete). By organizing two thematic pre-schools, we will ensure active participation by junior researchers, which should have a lasting effect on their careers, as well as influence the routes along which these research areas will be developed in the future. Our two workshops will further provide opportunities for many re- searchers from across the globe to interact and collaborate. We believe that close interactions between these disciplines are a necessary condition to address many mathematical challenges raised in the last decades, and that the timing is optimal to bring together all these powerful ideas which have been recently developed in several communities. Therefore, our proposed semester program will have a strong and lasting impact on High-Dimensional Probability, Convexity and Analysis as a whole.

rec.title: Advances in Quantum Cryptography, Paris
rec.abstract:
This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on mathematical developments in Advances in Quantum Cryptography (QCRYPTO).
September 13th to December 10th, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
** REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE **
Deadline for financial support request is March 15, 2027
Presentation of the programme
Quantum cryptography lies at the intersection of cryptography, quantum information, and computational complexity. Quantum technologies offer new cryptographic possibilities, while also changing our understanding of which security guarantees and computational tasks are achievable. Recent developments have revealed deep connections between these areas, but many fundamental questions remain open.
This programme will bring together researchers from theoretical computer science, mathematics, cryptography, and quantum information. It will explore three closely connected directions: information-theoretic foundations, including quantum communication, nonlocality, randomness, and device-independent security; complexity-theoretic foundations, including quantum proofs, verification, reductions, and computational assumptions; and computational and interactive primitives, including commitments, zero knowledge, secure computation, and protocols involving quantum devices.
Through an introductory school, seminars, focused workshops, informal discussions, and extended research visits, the programme aims to develop a common language across neighboring communities. It will provide opportunities for sustained collaboration between senior and junior researchers, encourage new research partnerships, and help identify important directions for the next stage of quantum cryptography.

rec.title: Séminaire 09/10/2026 - Gabriel Peyré and Vianney Perchet
rec.abstract:
14h15-15h15 Gabriel Peyré (ENS)
The Expressive Power of Large Language Models
Abstract: Large language models process vast sequences of input tokens by alternating between classical multi-layer perceptron layers and self-attention mechanisms. While the approximation capabilities of perceptrons are relatively well understood, those of attention mechanisms remain less explored. In this talk, I will compare the proof techniques and approximation results associated with these two types of layers, emphasizing key open questions that connect large language models with approximation theory in infinite-dimensional spaces representing input token distributions.
15h30-16h30 Vianney Perchet (Criteo et ENSAE)
AI-powered AI. Robustness, Consistency and Smoothness of Algorithms.
Abstract: AI systems no longer operate as isolated algorithms, machines, or agents; instead, they
interact with each other. An algorithm designed for a specific task might use the output or
prediction of another as its input. This has serious consequences: blindly relying on another
algorithm can be extremely helpful if it is accurate, but devastating if it is not, as a single error -
even the tiniest one - could break down the whole system. New algorithms will need to incorporate
these predictions to improve their consistency, while remaining robust against errors. We will use
simple toy examples to show how the generic framework of learning-augmented algorithms (LAA) is
perfectly suited for this challenge, highlighting the complexity of designing practical and potentially
vastly more efficient algorithms.

rec.title: Amal Omrani - Explicit Computation of Super-Hedging Prices and Strategies under Transaction Costs
rec.abstract: In markets with transaction costs, can super-hedging prices and strategies be explicitly characterized and computed directly from real market data, without relying on dual formulations? This talk presents a constructive approach based on conditional supports and dynamic programming, leading to explicit recursive formulas for super-hedging prices and strategies. The approach is illustrated using real market data.
rec.location_text: Salle Olga Ladyjenskaïa, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Ruben Haalebos - Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information
rec.abstract: We study dynamic portfolio decarbonization under incomplete information about firms' carbon intensities and the underlying transition state. The investor maximizes expected utility of terminal wealth net of a penalty on perceived cumulative financed emissions. Asset returns and carbon intensities depend on a stochastic transition factor, while the investor may need to infer the current transition state, its long-run mean and firms' carbon intensities from market observations and periodic noisy disclosures. The optimal strategy combines a Merton-type component with climate-dependent expected-return adjustments, a direct carbon intensity penalty and intertemporal hedging demands associated with stochastic carbon intensities and learning. In a numerical application, incomplete information has limited effects on welfare and target satisfaction when prior beliefs are well specified. By contrast, biased beliefs generate welfare losses in either direction but asymmetric environmental consequences: optimistic and pessimistic beliefs induce opposite portfolio tilts and therefore affect the probability of exceeding the cumulative emissions target differently.
rec.location_text: Salle Olga Ladyjenskaïa, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Élise Devey - A Frank–Wolfe-Type Algorithm for High-Dimensional Stochastic Control Problems with Non-Exchangeable Agents
rec.abstract: Abstract : This paper presents a Frank--Wolfe type algorithm for computing approximately optimal distributed stochastic controls in a large population of $N$ agents cooperating to minimize a convex cost functional. The cost includes a heterogeneous pairwise interaction term between the agents' controls, which rules out a direct treatment by the classical Mean Field Control framework. Working directly at finite $N$ rather than through a mean-field limit, we prove that the distributed controls returned by our algorithm are $N^{-1/2}$-optimal for the original problem, with an explicit rate in the number of iterations $K$ and in a measure of interaction heterogeneity, $\Delta_{\mathrm{spread}}$, that we introduce. The algorithm avoids the curse of dimensionality: at each iteration, the coupled $N$-agent problem is linearized and decomposed into $N$ independent, low-dimensional subproblems. We illustrate the approach on a linear-quadratic benchmark, for which we derive a closed-form Riccati-type characterization of the optimal control, and validate the predicted convergence rate numerically. Interaction structures of this heterogeneous, pairwise-penalized type arise naturally in applications such as electricity grid flexibility management, where local storage units are coupled through shared transmission-line capacity constraints.
rec.location_text: Salle Maurice Fréchet, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Grégoire Sempé - Marginal Propensities to Decarbonize
rec.abstract: This research project characterizes the cost-effective climate policy on households’ direct emissions. Heterogenous households abate through lumpy decisions on their durable goods holdings and their usage intensity. I study theoretically whether liquidity constraints justifies combining carbon pricing and subsidies or credit lines. I propose a quantitative heterogenous agent model to find the optimal climate policy mix.
rec.location_text: Salle Olga Ladyjenskaïa, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Marco Plazzogna - Endogenous Dynamic Networks for Heteroscedastic Outcomes
rec.abstract:
Many economic and financial systems are naturally represented as networks: the outcome of one unit may depend on those of other units through relationships that evolve over time. A central difficulty is that these relationships need not be exogenous. The network itself may react to the same shocks that affect the variables of interest, creating an endogeneity problem that cannot be addressed by treating network weights as fixed or predetermined.
We study a dynamic spatial model in which the interaction network is time-varying and generated by an auxiliary formation process. Dependence between innovations driving network formation and the structural outcome shock is explicitly incorporated through a control-function approach.
The framework is further extended to allow for conditional heteroskedasticity. In particular, we distinguish between two potentially different dynamic networks: one governing the transmission of outcomes in the conditional mean, and another governing the propagation of past shocks in the conditional variance. This makes it possible to separate network effects on the level of the process from network effects on its risk and volatility.
The resulting model provides a framework for studying systems in which both interactions and uncertainty evolve endogenously over time.
rec.location_text: Salle Olga Ladyjenskaïa, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables
rec.abstract:
La Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables aura lieu le vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à l'Institut Henri Poincaré.
Titles and Abstracts
Mini-course (2x1h) by Cédric Boutillier
Title: Scaling and local limits of random Young tableaux: a determinantal approach
Abstract: Given a partition λ of an integer n (or a Young diagram with n boxes), a standard Young tableau of shape λ is a way to fill the boxes of the Young diagram with integers from 1 to n which is injective, and increasing along rows and columns.
Standard Young tableaux are classical objects in combinatorics and representation theory. They can be interpreted as (monotone) surface above the domain delimited by their shape. A natural question is, given a large shape λ, what does a typical standard Young tableau of that shape look like?
After discussing some properties of these objects, the results of existence of limit shape of Biane using asymptotic representation theory, and the case of rectangular tableaux studied by Pittel and Romik, we will discuss an approach to limit shape using determinantal processes, by making connections with the dimer model.
If time permits, we will discuss also the local limit of these objects, describing the relative order of the numbers inside the tableau in a mesoscopic window around a given box.
This is joint work with Jacopo Borga, Valentin Féray and Pierre-Loïc Méliot.
Seminar talk (1h) by Elia Bisi (Università degli Studi di Firenze)
Title: Matrix Whittaker processes
Abstract: The log-gamma polymer is a prominent integrable model in the KPZ class: the law of its partition function is a marginal of a Whittaker measure, a positive-temperature analogue of the Schur measure. I will present a non-commutative generalisation, in which the “particles” are positive definite matrices. These evolve as interacting multiplicative random walks with inverse Wishart increments, arranged in a triangular array with push-and-block interactions. Using intertwining relations, we show that, for suitable random initial configurations, the bottom edge of the array evolves as an autonomous Markov process, with a kernel built from Whittaker functions of matrix arguments. For a singular initial state, its fixed-time law is a matrix Whittaker measure. Consequently, the matrix log-gamma polymer partition function is distributed as the first marginal of this measure.
Joint work with Jonas Arista and Neil O’Connell.
rec.location_text: Salle Yvette Cauchois, IHP - Bâtiment Perrin

rec.title: Le problème de Littlewood inverse pour les fonctions multiplicatives
rec.speaker: Péa Bazin
rec.abstract: Nous montrons que si $f$ est une fonction complètement multiplicative vérifiant $$\int_0^1 \left| \sum_{n\le x} f(n)e(\alpha n) \right|\,d\alpha \ll \log x$$ pour tout $x$, alors $f$ est exactement de la forme $\chi(n) n^{it}.$ Travail coécrit avec Oleksiy Klurman.

rec.title: Sur la probabilité qu’un entier possède un diviseur de la forme $p-1$ dans un intervalle donné
rec.speaker: Rebecca Abi Abdallah
rec.abstract: Dans cet exposé, nous étudierons la fonction qui compte les entiers naturels inférieurs ou égaux à $x$ possédant, dans un intervalle $(y,z]$, un diviseur de la forme $p-1$, où $p$ est premier. En analysant le comportement asymptotique de cette quantité dans les différents régimes de $z=z(y)$, nous mettrons en évidence une transition de phase qui révèle les dépendances entre ces événements de divisibilité en fonction de la longueur logarithmique de l’intervalle $(y,z]$. Notre résultat généralise un théorème de Ford correspondant au cas $z=x$. Ceci est un travail en collaboration avec V. Kovaleva, J. Schlitt et N. Tardy.

Cela aboutit à des problèmes de comptage intéressants. C’est un travail en collaboration avec Max Xu et Victor Wang.

rec.title: Irreducibility of random reciprocal polynomials
rec.speaker: David Hokken
rec.abstract: Let $P = a_m T^m + \sum_{j=0}^{m} a_j (T^{m-j} + T^{m+j})$ be a monic reciprocal polynomial of even degree n, with the $a_j$ drawn independently and uniformly at random from $\{1, 2, \ldots, H\}$ for some fixed integer $H \geq 35$. In joint work with Dimitris Koukoulopoulos, building on prior work of Bary-Soroker—Koukoulopoulos—Kozma, we show that $P$ is irreducible over the rationals, and has large Galois group, with probability tending to 1 as $n$ tends to infinity. This is in line with the long-held belief going back in various forms to Hilbert, Van der Waerden, Odlyzko—Poonen and Konyagin that a typical polynomial is irreducible and has Galois group as large as possible. I will discuss some recent, related developments in the field of probabilistic Galois theory before discussing aspects of the proof, which draws from classical polynomial theory, Fourier analysis, probability theory and group theory.

rec.title: Palindromes and Kloostermania
rec.speaker: Daniel Johnston
rec.abstract: Recently, there has been a surge in new results on the digital properties of numbers. In this talk, we discuss some recent results on palindromes, numbers which are the same backwards and forwards (e.g. 12321 or 7887) in a fixed base. Despite being elementary objects of study, in order to prove deep results about their multiplicative properties we need to turn to powerful estimates on exponential sums. For this talk, we focus particularly on a recent result of Bryce Kerr and myself, establishing the infinitude of square-free palindromes.

rec.title: Low Lying Zeros of Hecke $L$-Functions
rec.speaker: Ezra Waxman
rec.speaker_affiliation: Academic College of Engineering in Tel Aviv, Israël
rec.abstract: The one-level density measures the statistical distribution of zeros across a family of $L$-functions near the central point. In this talk, I will present several results concerning the one-level density for families of $L$-functions associated to CM elliptic curves of the form $y^2=x^3-dx$. The talk will moreover discuss applications to bounding the average rank of such curves (joint work with Chantal David, Lucile Devin, and Alessandro Fazzari).

rec.title: Using AI in mathematical research
rec.speaker: Andrew Pearce-Crump
rec.abstract: AI systems have recently contributed to new results across mathematics, several of them in number theory. This talk is about the everyday version: how a working mathematician can use AI for a research project. I will go back to a paper from my PhD with Chris Hughes, about the moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function at its zeros, and ask how I would have worked on it had AI been available then. The emphasis is on habits that mathematicians already have, and how they apply to mathematical research in the age of AI.

rec.abstract: In this talk I will present joint work with Bingrong Huang in which we establish an asymptotic formula for the first moment of symmetric cube central $L$-values over Hecke-Maass forms in short spectral windows. Applications include a quantitative non-vanishing result and an almost-all Lindelöf bound.

rec.title: Modular symbols in arithmetic progressions
rec.speaker: Svenja Zur Verth
rec.abstract: Motivated by conjectures of Mazur, Rubin and Stein, the distribution of modular symbols has received a lot of attention in recent years. Notably, Petridis and Risager showed that modular symbols are asymptotically normally distributed when averaged over all denominators. A natural next step is to restrict the denominators to sparser sets, such as squarefree numbers. This requires understanding modular symbols in arithmetic progressions. Using spectral methods for Eisenstein series twisted by modular symbols, we make the dependence on the modulus explicit in the first two terms of all even moments, and in the full main term of the fourth moment. As an application, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the fourth moment over squarefree denominators.

rec.title: An affirmative solution to the generalized Busemann-Petty problem with subspaces dimensions 2 and 3
rec.speaker: Cheng Lin
rec.abstract: The generalized Busemann--Petty problem asks whether two origin-symmetric convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ having larger volume of all $m$-dimensional sections necessarily have larger volume. When $m\geq 4$, this is known to be false, but the cases $m=2, 3$ for $n\geq 5$ have remained open since the 1990s. In this work, we resolve these cases. Together with the known results, the generalized Busemann--Petty problem is completely solved: the answer is affirmative for $m=1, 2, 3$, and negative for $m\geq 4$. This talk is based on the joint work with Yu-de LIU and Ge XIONG.

rec.title: IHP School: Artificial Intelligence for Mathematicians and Theoretical Physicists
rec.abstract:
Recent breakthroughs have shown that AI can now prove theorems. At the same time, many of the deepest open questions about AI are, at heart, questions of mathematics and physics: high-dimensional geometry, non-convex optimisation, the statistical mechanics of learning. AI is becoming both a tool for and a subject of research in our fields, and a working knowledge of it is fast becoming essential for every young researcher.
This one-week school, funded by Qube Research & Technologies, will introduce the fundamental concepts of modern AI. It is designed for PhD students and early-career researchers in mathematics and theoretical physics with no prior specialisation in AI. The programme combines lectures with hands-on lab sessions.

rec.title: Exact curve counting on the once-punctured torus
rec.speaker: Mingkun Liu
rec.abstract: Two closed curves on a surface are said to have the same topological type if they lie in the same mapping class group orbit. Mirzakhani first showed that, on a hyperbolic surface, the number of closed geodesics of a given topological type of length at most L is asymptotically proportional to L^{6g-6}. In this talk, we will focus on the case of the once-punctured torus. Rather than using hyperbolic length, we will count curves according to their word length. In this setting, it turns out that exact counting formulas can be obtained. This is joint work with Filippo Baroni and David Fisac.

rec.title: An Introduction to D-Modules
rec.speaker: Raoul Hallopeau
rec.abstract: The theory of D-modules had initially been developed for complex (algebraic and analytic) varieties in the 1970's, and allows for an algebraic approach of partial differential equations. There are lots of applications; for instance, in the 1980's Masaki Kashiwara and Zoghman Mebkhout have used it to generalize the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. D-modules are also an invaluable tool in less expected areas, such as Representation Theory. In more recent years, D-modules have also found applications to the world of arithmetic varieties.

rec.abstract: In this talk, I will introduce differential equations on p-adic analytic varieties. We will see how the ultrametric p-adic topology is an obstruction to a Cauchy-Lipschitz-type result. I will then show, following Scholze, how the pro-étale topology and the introduction of new numbers called "periods" provide a workaround to this issue.
