We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres.

arxiv:2611.26001.title: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
arxiv:2611.26001.summary: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo.

arxiv:2611.26028.title: On the dimension of $V$-variable fractals
arxiv:2611.26028.summary: Random recursive sets have been used to model a wide range of fractal phenomena, but they can be slow and difficult to generate. $V$-variability address this problem by allowing these sets at most $V$ distinct shapes at each level of magnification. The formulae for the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of both classes is known, and it has been conjectured that (under mild assumptions) the $V$-variable dimension converges to the random recursive dimension as $V\to\infty$.

arxiv:2611.26034.title: Stars and paths in oriented graphs
arxiv:2611.26034.summary: Let $\overrightarrow{F}$ be a fixed oriented graph. Its oriented Tur\'{a}n number, written $\exo(n,\overrightarrow{F})$, is the largest size of an $n$-vertex oriented graph with no copy of $\overrightarrow{F}$. This parameter extends the classical notion of Tur\'{a}n number to oriented graphs.
arxiv:2611.26034.authors: Xuanrui Hu, Hanyi Wang, Yuefang Sun, Bo Deng

arxiv:2611.26037.title: An improved Moore bound for girths seven and eleven
arxiv:2611.26037.summary: Let $n(d,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices of a graph of minimum degree $d$ and girth at least $g=2k+1$. A simple counting argument gives the classical lower bound $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)=1+d\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(d-1)^i$, known as the Moore bound and dating back at least to 1960. Apart from complete graphs and odd cycles, graphs attaining this lower bound can exist only for girth $5$ and degrees $3,7$ and $57$ (Hoffman and Singleton 1960; Bannai and Ito 1973; Damerell 1973).

arxiv:2611.26092.title: Control of Complex Social Systems via Committed Minorities and Opinion Broadcast
arxiv:2611.26092.summary: Complex social systems are often characterized by a deep interconnection between individuals' opinion formation and their decision-making processes. In this chapter, we show how these two dynamics can be incorporated within a unifying game-theoretic coevolutionary model for actions and opinions. We present the main theoretical results concerning the convergence of the coevolutionary model, and its recent extensions to incorporate further features of real-world social systems.
arxiv:2611.26092.authors: Roberta Raineri, Mengbin Ye, Lorenzo Zino

arxiv:2611.26093.title: Post-Hopf structures on $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and post-Lie bialgebras
arxiv:2611.26093.summary: We classify post-Hopf structures on the Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, for $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not a root of unity, proving that there are exactly three isomorphism classes. We then investigate the semiclassical limits of post-Hopf quantized universal enveloping algebras and derive a compatibility condition between the induced post-Lie product and Lie cobracket. This leads to the notion of a post-Lie bialgebra.

arxiv:2611.26110.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank III: Lattice points of the Kozlov polytope
arxiv:2611.26110.summary: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators and $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r Eg_i$ a graded free $E$-module with $\deg g_i=d_i$. Part I of this series identified the convex hull of the Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, $M$ a proper monomial submodule, as the Kozlov polytope $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$, a Minkowski sum of shifted Kozlov simplices, and described its vertices at rank two, conjecturing its facets there; Part II counted the Hilbert functions. Here we study the lattice points of the polytope.

arxiv:2611.26115.title: Rational multisections and unirationality of supersingular K3 surfaces
arxiv:2611.26115.summary: We prove that every supersingular K3 surface of Artin invariant at most nine is unirational, confirming the question of Artin, Rudakov, Shafarevich and Shioda outside the generic case of Artin invariant ten. In odd characteristic, we reduce the question to Artin invariant nine and sweep out the K3 surface by Abel--Jacobi images of rational multisections of its Artin--Tate twists which vary along the supersingular twistor line.

arxiv:2611.26130.title: Maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs with given minimum degree and edge connectivity
arxiv:2611.26130.summary: Let $G$ be a simple connected graph of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and edge connectivity $k$. Recently, in [Linear Algebra Appl. 751 (2026) 318-330], Zhao, Ye, and Fan characterized the extremal graph with maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all graphs of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and edge connectivity $k$ when $n \geq \delta^2+4\delta+3$ and $k \in \{0,1,2\}$, and proposed the corresponding problem for $3 \leq k \leq \delta-1$. In this paper, we solve the problem for the entire range $0 \leq k \leq \delta-1$ and completely remove the order restriction.

arxiv:2611.26151.title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
arxiv:2611.26151.summary: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_{\delta}$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown/Vershik/Ryzhikov/Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results.

arxiv:2611.26152.title: Orbifold Chern slopes of surfaces with negative second Segre number and big cotangent bundle
arxiv:2611.26152.summary: In this paper, we construct smooth minimal projective surfaces of general type with negative second Segre number and big cotangent bundle, and prove that every rational number in $(1,3]$ is realized as the orbifold Chern slope of a Du Val contraction of such a surface. The upper endpoint is attained by a canonical model with eighteen $A_8$ singularities and three $A_2$ singularities, which is a compact complex two-ball quotient by the equality case of the orbifold Miyaoka-Yau inequality. We also construct an explicit sequence of canonical-model orbifold Chern slopes converging to three from below.

arxiv:2611.26155.title: The $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of perfectoid THH
arxiv:2611.26155.summary: Let $R$ be a perfect $\mathbb F_p$-algebra or a nonzero $p$-torsionfree perfectoid ring and $p$ be an arbitrary prime number. We compute the $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of $\operatorname{THH}(R;\mathbb Z_p)$ for every $n\ge0$, including all homotopy groups, products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions and norms. We also compute genuine cyclotomic restriction.

arxiv:2611.26163.title: Uniform Positivity of the $F$-Signature and Pure Descent of klt Singularities
arxiv:2611.26163.summary: In this paper, we affirmatively answer the question of Carvajal-Rojas, Schwede, and Tucker on the uniform positivity of the $F$-signature, and prove a converse. Namely, given a klt type singularity, we establish uniform lower bounds on the $F$-signatures of its reductions mod $p$ for $p$ sufficiently large. Conversely, if the $F$-signatures of the reductions of a normal singularity are uniformly bounded below by a positive constant on large primes, we prove that the singularity is of klt type.

arxiv:2611.26184.title: Invariant real curves arising from semiconjugacies of rational maps
arxiv:2611.26184.summary: In this paper, we study real analytic invariant curves arising from semiconjugacies of real rational maps. Such semiconjugacies arise naturally in Eremenko's work on invariant Jordan analytic curves. While invariant generalized circles are easy to obtain from real rational maps, we are interested in curves not contained in any generalized circle.

arxiv:2611.26185.title: Euler up-down numbers and quiver representations
arxiv:2611.26185.summary: We show that Euler up-down numbers enumerate isoclasses of representations arising from quiver Grassmannians which provide an explicit realization of PBW degenerate flag varieties. Using this geometric realization, we derive several formulas connecting Euler up-down numbers, median Genocchi numbers, and Motzkin numbers. We also define a new $q$-analogue of Euler up-down numbers and derive several formulas for these polynomials.
arxiv:2611.26185.authors: Giovanni Cerulli Irelli, Evgeny Feigin, Markus Reineke

arxiv:2611.26189.title: Optimal Radius Ratio of Compact Nonuniform Packings
arxiv:2611.26189.summary: We study the ratio of the smallest to the largest radius in a nonuniform disk packing whose tangency graph triangulates the plane. We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest possible ratio is $s=0.651050185882609\ldots$, attained uniquely up to similarity by packing~53 of Fernique, Hashemi, and Sizova. In fact, every nonuniform packing with radius ratio at least $0.65105$ is similar to this packing.

arxiv:2611.26205.title: Convergence of the Most Probable Transition Paths in Multiscale Systems
arxiv:2611.26205.summary: This paper is devoted to study the convergence behavior of the most probable transition paths in a class of multiscale stochastic dynamical systems. First, based on Euler-Lagrange equations, we establish proximity and convergence results in the space of continuous functions endowed with the supremum norm. These results compare the most probable paths of the multiscale system with those of averaged system derived from the averaging principle.
arxiv:2611.26205.authors: Qiqi Lian, Shanqi Liu, Jinqiao Duan

arxiv:2611.26207.title: Surface sheaves on the quintic I. Expanded degenerations and virtual gluing
arxiv:2611.26207.summary: We study the specialization of Donaldson-Thomas virtual cycles for surface sheaves on a Calabi Yau threefold degenerating to a simple normal crossing threefold, composed of two quasi Fano threefolds glued along a common (double) divisor. The compactification of the two relative sheaf moduli spaces involves construction of suitable moduli space of sheaves on expanded degenerations of each quasi Fano variety. On a fixed expanded fiber the matching datum is an equivalence of the derived restrictions of the component sheaves.

arxiv:2611.26217.title: Surface sheaves on the quintic II. Donaldson-Thomas invariants and the M5-brane modified elliptic genus in string theory
arxiv:2611.26217.summary: We compute Donaldson-Thomas invariants of pure two-dimensional sheaves in the hyperplane class of a smooth quintic threefold. We take advantage of two degenerating families to relate the DT geometry of Quintic threefold to geometry of pure two dimensional shaves on a quartic threefold and correction terms induced by invariants of relative Hilbert schemes of points. For this we use degeneration technique and virtual gluing formula in the prequel Part I.

arxiv:2611.26226.title: The existence of generalized Steiner systems
arxiv:2611.26226.summary: A generalized Steiner system $GS(t,w,n,q)$ is a $q$-ary constant-weight code of length $n$ and weight $w$ that has minimum distance at least $2(w-t)+1$ and attains the Johnson-type upper bound $(q-1)^t\binom nt/\binom wt$. For strengths $t=1$ and $t=2$, such systems were known to exist for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying the necessary divisibility conditions. For general fixed parameters, Liu and Shangguan (J.
arxiv:2611.26226.authors: Xuan Wang, Shitao Li, Minjia Shi

arxiv:2611.26229.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
arxiv:2611.26229.summary: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $\Delta^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}.

arxiv:2611.26237.title: Concentration of plane branches: building a complete equisingularity invariant
arxiv:2611.26237.summary: We study the concentration of the semigroup of values of a plane algebroid branch over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. We give an explicit formula for it in terms of the multiplicities of the branch and of its strict transform; in particular, it is an invariant of the equisingularity class. Applying it to the successive strict transforms, we associate a concentration sequence with each branch.
arxiv:2611.26237.authors: Evelia R. Garc\'ia Barroso, William G. Hern\'andez-Yanes

arxiv:2611.26246.title: Presentations of the cohomology ring of Hessenberg varieties for the minimal nilpotent orbit in type A
arxiv:2611.26246.summary: In 2016 Abe and Crooks found a presentation for the cohomology ring of Hessenberg varieties associated with the minimal nilpotent orbit. Specifically, they presented the ring as a quotient of the cohomology ring of the flag variety, and described the kernel of the quotient map as the span of certain Schubert classes. This note improves upon their result in the Lie type A case, by giving a minimal generating set for the kernel.
arxiv:2611.26246.authors: Giulia Gaggero, Megumi Harada, Hannah Nardone, Brett Nasserden, Jenna Rajchgot, Lisa Seccia, Adam Van Tuyl

arxiv:2611.26253.title: Combinatorial Dvoretzky Theory
arxiv:2611.26253.summary: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional polytope such that $P \subset B_2^n$. Let $M^*(P)$ denote its mean width, and let $N$ be the number of facets (faces of dimension $n-1$) of $P$. We prove the following two bounds: (1) If $N \leq e^n$, then \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{\log^2(\frac{N}{n})}.

arxiv:2611.26259.title: An asymptotic bound for Yuster's independent transversal factor conjecture
arxiv:2611.26259.summary: An $[r,n,1]$-graph has $r$ independent parts of size $n$, with a matching between each pair of parts. Yuster conjectured in 2021 that every such graph has a partition into independent transversals whenever $n\ge 2\lceil r/2\rceil$. We prove that there is an absolute constant $A>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $r$, this partition exists whenever $n\ge\lceil r+A r^{20/21}\rceil$.

arxiv:2611.26277.title: Dense induced bipartite subgraphs under local sparsity
arxiv:2611.26277.summary: The study of dense induced bipartite subgraphs dates back to the work of Erd\H{o}s, Faudree, Pach, and Spencer on triangle-free graphs. In this paper, we study this problem under different local sparsity conditions. First, we prove that for every fixed integer $t\ge 2$ and all sufficiently large $d$, every $K_{t,t}$-free graph of minimum degree at least $d$ contains an induced bipartite subgraph of average degree at least $\log d-16t\log\log d$.
arxiv:2611.26277.authors: Peiru Kuang, Jing Lin, Yan Wang

arxiv:2611.26280.title: Rainbow Matchings in $K_{r+1}$-free Graphs
arxiv:2611.26280.summary: Let $n,m,r$ be positive integers with $n\ge 2m+2$, where $n$ is sufficiently large relative to $r$. Alon and Frankl determined the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing neither $K_{r+1}$ nor a matching of size $m+1$. In this paper, we establish a rainbow analogue of their result.
arxiv:2611.26280.authors: Hongliang Lu, Xinxin Ma, Xing Peng

arxiv:2611.26284.title: Orthosymplectic R-matrix from Hasse diagrams
arxiv:2611.26284.summary: We calculate R-matrix in the basic representation for the ortho-symplectic quantum supergroups in arbitrary polarizations, by a method of Hasse diagrams.
arxiv:2611.26284.authors: D. Algethami, N. Kryazhevskikh, A. Mudrov

arxiv:2611.26290.title: Hilbert schemes of points on plane curves via standard families
arxiv:2611.26290.summary: We describe an approach to computing Hilbert schemes of points on embedded families of plane curves. This is achieved by introducing the notion of a standard family, and the associated Hilbert schemes are shown to be algebraic vector bundles over the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. Any embedded family of plane curves lies in some standard family, which allows for the computation of the corresponding Hilbert scheme from that of the standard family.

arxiv:2611.26300.title: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
arxiv:2611.26300.summary: Photonic GHZ states generated with probabilistic pair sources can be described by edge-coloured, complex-weighted graphs. In this representation, conditioning on an event with one photon in every detector turns the output amplitudes into coherent sums over perfect matchings, and generating an \(N\)-photon \(D\)-dimensional GHZ state is equivalent to constructing a monochromatic quantum graph. Here, we prove that no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for any even \(N\ge4\) when \(D\ge N\).
arxiv:2611.26300.authors: Mario Krenn, Moritz Firsching, George Tsoukalas, Rishikesh Gajjala, Xuemei Gu, Swarat Chaudhuri

arxiv:2611.26301.title: The envelope property for unibranch projective varieties (with an appendix on the singular Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture)
arxiv:2611.26301.summary: We prove the envelope property for every real numerical class on an integral unibranch projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field based on the recent work of Lyuhui Wu. Together with Boucksom-Jonsson's converse, this characterizes unibranchness by the plurisubharmonic envelope property. The Appendix applies the result to the uniform Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture for projective varieties with klt singularities.
arxiv:2611.26301.authors: Yanbo Fang, Jiyuan Han, Mingchen Xia

arxiv:2611.26330.title: Equality in the clique bound for critical graphs
arxiv:2611.26330.summary: A graph is $k$-critical if its chromatic number is $k$ and every proper subgraph is $(k-1)$-colorable. Gao and Ma (2023) proved that every $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph with $n > k \ge 4$ contains at most $n - k + 3$ cliques of size $k - 1$, and asked which graphs attain this bound. We answer this question by showing that equality holds if and only if $n - k + 3$ is odd and the graph is isomorphic to the join of a complete graph on $k - 3$ vertices and a cycle of length $n - k + 3$.

arxiv:2611.26375.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
arxiv:2611.26375.summary: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions.

arxiv:2611.26397.title: Hook histories and a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual canonical Grothendieck functions
arxiv:2611.26397.summary: We establish a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for power-sum multiplication in the dual canonical stable Grothendieck basis. The coefficients admit a closed boundary product formula and a signed combinatorial description by hook histories. We determine their exact support and prove an exact divisibility law for off-diagonal coefficients governed by the edge-connected components of the indexing skew diagram.

arxiv:2611.26429.title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
arxiv:2611.26429.summary: We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic.

arxiv:2611.26439.title: An operator $b$-positivity conjecture for Jack characters
arxiv:2611.26439.summary: Goulden and Jackson defined a Jack deformation $a_{\mu\nu}^\lambda(\alpha)$ of the connection coefficients of the symmetric group and conjectured that these were polynomials in $b=\alpha-1$ with nonnegative interger coefficients. This conjecture was extended to the structure constants of (stable) Jack characters by \'Sniady. We formulate a stronger operator conjecture: the differential operators $\Delta_\mu(\alpha)$ that multiply by stable Jack characters should have coefficients in ${\mathbb N}[b]$ in the normally ordered Heisenberg basis $p_ID_J$.

arxiv:2611.26446.title: Degree Lower Bounds for Symmetric Boolean Functions: Breaking the Prime-Gap Barrier
arxiv:2611.26446.summary: We prove that every nonconstant symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables has exact real polynomial degree at least $n-O(n^{1/3}(\log n)^{2/3})$. This makes progress toward the conjecture of von zur Gathen and Roche that the degree is always at least $n-3$. The original prime-gap argument of von zur Gathen and Roche yields a degree deficit of $O(n^{0.525})$ using the theorem of Baker, Harman, and Pintz, or $O(n^{0.52})$ using an estimate claimed in a recent preprint.

arxiv:2611.26457.title: Comprehensive Gr\"obner Bases in Macaulay2
arxiv:2611.26457.summary: Studying parameter-dependent polynomial systems often requires stratifying parameter space according to the algebraic or geometric properties of the specialised systems. Comprehensive Gr\"obner bases and systems, which provide Gr\"obner bases valid under every specialisation, either uniformly or on specified regions of parameter space, are classical tools for studying polynomial ideals under specialisation. We introduce ComprehensiveGBs, a Macaulay2 package for computing comprehensive Gr\"obner bases and systems, either over the full parameter space or under specified parameter conditions.
arxiv:2611.26457.authors: Mar\'ia Agustina Cagliero, Oliver Clarke, Lorenzo De Biase, Angelo El Saliby, Giulia Gaggero, Weijia Wang

arxiv:2611.26463.title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics
arxiv:2611.26463.summary: Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure.

arxiv:2611.26465.title: Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
arxiv:2611.26465.summary: This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$\alpha$ lattice (FPUT-$\alpha$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion. Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation.

arxiv:2611.26473.title: Preventing cycles in Lotka--Volterra systems
arxiv:2611.26473.summary: We study cycles of heteroclinic connections between equilibria of Lotka--Volterra systems with negative self-interactions. We prove that generalized strict diagonal dominance makes the invasion, connection, and weak graphs acyclic for every intrinsic growth vector. No hyperbolicity assumption is needed, and the associated semiflow is gradient with respect to its equilibria.
arxiv:2611.26473.authors: Matheus C. Bortolan, Piotr Kalita, Jos\'e Antonio Langa, Rafael O. Moura

arxiv:2611.26505.title: Super quantum groups of divided powers \`a la Lusztig
arxiv:2611.26505.summary: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids.

arxiv:2611.26513.title: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemer\'edi
arxiv:2611.26513.summary: A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemer\'edi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Sz\'ekely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $\delta_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of…
arxiv:2611.26513.authors: Michelle Delcourt, Cicely Henderson, Thomas Lesgourgues, Luke Postle

arxiv:2611.26539.title: Large $k$-cross-free families
arxiv:2611.26539.summary: Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$.

arxiv:2611.26556.title: Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
arxiv:2611.26556.summary: Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.
arxiv:2611.26556.authors: Anna Neopryatnaya, Vladimir Verdenko, Vsevolod Voronov

arxiv:2611.26566.title: Topological notions of Shadowing under Semi-Conjugacy
arxiv:2611.26566.summary: We study various notions of shadowing and investigate whether they are preserved under semi-conjugacy and inverse limits. In particular, we study Inverse shadowing, $H$-shadowing, Periodic shadowing, Ramsey shadowing, Density shadowing and Ergodic shadowing.

arxiv:2611.26570.title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
arxiv:2611.26570.summary: The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit.
arxiv:2611.26570.authors: Melda Akyazi-Zavadski, Nathana\"el Berestycki, Sunil Chhita

arxiv:2611.26580.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
arxiv:2611.26580.summary: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

arxiv:2611.26597.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
arxiv:2611.26597.summary: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms.
arxiv:2611.26597.authors: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle

arxiv:2611.26621.title: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
arxiv:2611.26621.summary: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence.

arxiv:2611.26622.title: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
arxiv:2611.26622.summary: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners.

arxiv:2611.26634.title: Almost-sure quenched KAM tori for nonlinear wave equations with a spatial white-noise potential
arxiv:2611.26634.summary: Let \[ A_\omega=-\partial_x^2+\rho\,\partial_xB(x,\omega), \qquad \rho\ne0, \] be the Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operator on $(0,\pi)$ with a spatial Gaussian white-noise potential, realized pathwise via quasi-derivatives. Here $B$ is Brownian motion in the spatial variable $x$, and $\partial_xB$ denotes its distributional derivative. We consider the nonlinear wave equation \[ u_{tt}+A_\omega u+f(u)=0, \] where $f$ is odd and real analytic near zero, with $f(u)=\kappa u^3+O(u^5)$ and $\kappa\ne0$.
arxiv:2611.26634.authors: Yingdu Dong, Wenwen Jian, Xiaoping Yuan

arxiv:2611.26640.title: The maximum area of a snake polyomino in a $12 \times n$ rectangle
arxiv:2611.26640.summary: A snake polyomino is a set of cells of the square lattice whose cells, under edge adjacency, induce a path. Let $T(m,n)$ be the largest number of cells of a snake polyomino contained in an $m \times n$ rectangle, equivalently the largest number of vertices of an induced path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ (OEIS A360917). Blondin Mass\'e and Goupil determined $T(m,n)$ for all $m \le 5$ and proposed the general case as a conjecture; for $m = 12$, entry A397153 of the OEIS records a conjectured generating function, contributed by Goupil in July 2026, which has remained unproved.

arxiv:2611.26645.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Cocomparability, Co-Bipartite, and Distance-Hereditary Graphs
arxiv:2611.26645.summary: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether $\omega(G)$ colors suffice is NP-complete on connected cocomparability graphs of diameter two and independence number three. The reduction supplies a partition into three cliques, a maximum clique, an optimal ordinary coloring, and a dominating edge.

arxiv:2611.26648.title: Extremal Ky Fan $p$-$k$ norms of graphs
arxiv:2611.26648.summary: We study a two-parameter extension of Nikiforov's extremal problems for graph norms, focusing on the quantity $$ S_{p,k}(G) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(G)^p\right)^{1/p}, $$ where $p\ge1$, and $\sigma_1(G) \ge \cdots \ge \sigma_n(G)$ are the singular values of the adjacency matrix of an $n$-vertex graph $G$. This quantity provides a common generalization of the Ky Fan $k$-norm and the Schatten $p$-norm, which correspond to the cases $p=1$ and $k=n$, respectively. We establish upper and lower bounds and characterize extremal and near-extremal graphs within specified parameter ranges.

arxiv:2611.26650.title: The Manhattan cospectrality of the cocktail party graph
arxiv:2611.26650.summary: For a graph $G$ of order $N$ with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_{1}(G)\geq \cdots\geq\lambda_{N}(G),$ the cospectrality of $G$ is the smallest value of $\sum_{i}\left\vert \lambda_{i}(G)-\lambda_{i}(H)\right\vert $ over all graphs $H$ of order $N$ not isomorphic to $G.$ Abdollahi and Zakeri (Ars Math. Contemp. 22(1) (2022) P1.06) conjectured that the cospectrality of the cocktail party graph $CP_{n}$ is attained exactly at the graph $H_{n}.$ This graph is obtained from $K_{1,2,\ldots,2}$ by attaching a pendant vertex to the vertex of the part of size one. We prove this conjecture for every $n\geq2$ by showing that only three explicit graphs (two for $n=2$) are at distance less than $2$…
arxiv:2611.26650.authors: Irena M. Jovanovi\'c, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

arxiv:2611.26653.title: Detour different-distance sets in graphs
arxiv:2611.26653.summary: The detour distance $D(u,v)$ between two vertices of a connected graph is the length of a longest $u,v$-path. A set $S$ of vertices is a detour different-distance set if no vertex outside $S$ has the same detour distance to two vertices of $S$. We study the lower and upper detour different-distance numbers $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)$ and $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$, the smallest and largest orders of maximal such sets; this is the detour analogue of the different-distance sets of Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi, Laskar and Mulder.

arxiv:2611.26654.title: Local connectivity of Julia sets of Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions
arxiv:2611.26654.summary: We study the Newton maps of $\sin z$, $\cos z$, $\sinh z$, and $\cosh z$, each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map $N_{\cos}(z) = z + \cot z$, the half-planes $\{\pm \operatorname{Im} z > M\}$ are repelling petals at infinity for every $M \ge 2$. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Bara\'nski, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpi\'nska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of $N_{\cos}$.

arxiv:2611.26661.title: M\"obius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields
arxiv:2611.26661.summary: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $\lambda\in F^\times$, \[ \card{A+\lambda A^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range.

arxiv:2611.26669.title: On the number of edge-disjoint $K_r$ in $K_{r+1}$-free graphs
arxiv:2611.26669.summary: Gy\H ori and Keszegh [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{37} (2017), 1113--1124] proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. We extend this result to cliques of arbitrary fixed order. Specifically, we prove that for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_{r+1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$, where $t_{r-1}(n)$ denotes the number of edges in the Tur\'an graph $T_{r-1}(n)$.

arxiv:2611.26675.title: Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices
arxiv:2611.26675.summary: A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU).

arxiv:2611.26679.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
arxiv:2611.26679.summary: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way.
arxiv:2611.26679.authors: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle

arxiv:2611.26699.title: Arinkin's sheaf and Hilbert schemes
arxiv:2611.26699.summary: Arinkin's sheaf gives a relative Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence of a general Beauville-Mukai system, extending the usual Poincar\'e bundle over the smooth locus. We provide an alternative construction of it as a deformation of the Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence on the Hilbert scheme of an elliptic K3 surface obtained by lifting the classical Poincar\'e kernel for an elliptic surface. As applications, we show that the $P=C$ property for a general Beauville-Mukai system is equivalent to that for the Hilbert scheme fibration, thus providing new proofs for both.

arxiv:2611.26707.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
arxiv:2611.26707.summary: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $\sigma$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\in\sigma+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals.

arxiv:2611.26719.title: Partial sums of Rogers-Ramanujan functions
arxiv:2611.26719.summary: Explicit positive multisums on base q^5 for the Rogers-Ramanujan sum function and its partial sum are given. 32 combinatorial interpretations for these identities are given. The classical mod 5 Rogers-Ramanujan identities are recovered as a limiting case. These results are equivalent to a quintic basic hypergeometric identity.

arxiv:2611.26721.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
arxiv:2611.26721.summary: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans.

arxiv:2611.26727.title: Dynabase: A Database of Extreme Examples in Arithmetic Dynamics
arxiv:2611.26727.summary: We introduce Dynabase, a database cataloging extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics related to several major open conjectures: the Morton--Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture and the dynamical analogue of Lang's conjecture on canonical heights, as well as data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms. This database collects the known examples of extreme behavior for these problems and tracks the current status of subproblems based on degree and field of definition.

arxiv:2611.26732.title: Connected Cayley Approximation of Power Graphs of Finite Groups
arxiv:2611.26732.summary: For a nontrivial finite group \(G\), we define its connected intersection density as the maximum, over all connected Cayley graphs on \(G\), of the proportion of edges that also belong to the undirected power graph of \(G\). We show that this density is \(1\) if and only if \(G\) is cyclic, and that it is \(1/4\), \(1/6\), and \(1/12\) for \(A_4\), \(S_4\), and \(A_5\), respectively. For the dihedral group of order \(2n\), with \(n\geq 3\), we give a general formula and show that the connected intersection density equals \((\binom{n}{2}+1)/n^2\) if and only if \(n\) is a prime power.

arxiv:2611.26748.title: Generalized anti-Ramsey numbers
arxiv:2611.26748.summary: The anti-Ramsey number was introduced by Erd\H{o}s, Simonovits, and S\'os and is defined to be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color the edges of a graph to avoid a rainbow copy of some graph. One can generalize this by, instead of forbidding a rainbow copy of a graph, putting a cap on the number of colors that appear on any copy of that graph. To be precise, let $\AR(G,H,q)$ be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color $E(G)$ so that every copy of $H$ sees at most $q$ colors.

arxiv:2611.26750.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
arxiv:2611.26750.summary: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $\xi$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center.

arxiv:2611.26768.title: Avoiding squares over words with lists of size three
arxiv:2611.26768.summary: We prove that every sequence of lists of size three admits an infinite square-free word, establishing that the Thue choice number of the path is three. More precisely, the number of compatible square-free words of length $n$ is at least $c(5/4)^n$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. The proof combines a computer-assisted construction of weights with the weighted counting method previously introduced by the author.

arxiv:2611.26781.title: Isolation in Random Graphs
arxiv:2611.26781.summary: We study isolation in the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$. When $p=o(1)$ and $np\to\infty$, allowing an $F$-free graph on the undominated vertices gives the same first-order asymptotics for every fixed forest $F$ as the domination number $\gamma(G)$ in $G(n,p)$. For the ordinary isolation number $\iota(G)$ ($F$ is an edge) we prove two-point concentration when $p$ is bounded away from $1$ and $np^2/(\log n)^3\to\infty$.

arxiv:2611.26786.title: Compression with wildcards: The maximum anticliques of K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graphs
arxiv:2611.26786.summary: By definition a K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graph is such that the cardinality of each maximum matching equals the cardinality of each minimum vertex-cover. Each bipartite graph has this property. We unravel the structure of the family MACL(G) of all maximum anticliques (independent sets) of a K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graph G.

arxiv:2611.26789.title: Opposite filtrations on the parabolic compactified Jacobian
arxiv:2611.26789.summary: We show that the Hikita filtration on the cohomology of the parabolic compactified Jacobian of the plane curve singularity $x^m=y^n$, $(m,n)=1$, is opposite to the perverse filtration in a precise sense. This implies the parabolic Hilb-vs-Quot conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19633, and consequently the main conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2115 for these singularities. The new ingredient is an analysis of how the Bott-Mitchell filtration on the homology of the affine Grassmannian of $SL_n$ relates to both of the above filtrations.

arxiv:2611.26790.title: The 1-Loop and Ohtsuki-Takata Invariants for Alternating Braids
arxiv:2611.26790.summary: In a step towards resolving the 1-loop conjecture, Ohtsuki and Takata defined their own eponymous invariant in terms of an open knot diagram, and showed that it is equal to the adjoint Reidemeister torsion for two-bridge knots. Garoufalidis and Yoon then showed that the 1-loop invariant is equal to the Ohtsuki-Takata invariant using a technique involving a collapsed octahedral decomposition. This paper expands those techniques to relate the matrix determinants of the 1-loop and Ohtsuki-Takata invariants for the case of reduced alternating braids.

arxiv:2611.26798.title: Thurston measure is stationary with exponential Teichm\"uller moment
arxiv:2611.26798.summary: In 1967, Furstenberg proved that every lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center admits a probability measure whose stationary measure on the associated Furstenberg boundary belongs to the Lebesgue measure class. We prove an analogue of this theorem for the action of the mapping class group on Teichm\"uller space. Every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class on the space of projective measured foliations is the stationary measure of a non-elementary random walk with a finite exponential moment in the Teichm\"uller metric.

arxiv:2611.26830.title: Polynomial sequences of Simplex pivots on 0/1-polytopes
arxiv:2611.26830.summary: We study the number of Simplex pivots needed to solve linear programs over $0/1$-polytopes, starting from an arbitrary feasible basis and counting degenerate pivots. It has been known since the 1990s that from any extreme point of a 0/1-polytope there exists a monotone path of linear length to an optimal one. However, translating this into a polynomial sequence of Simplex pivots, i.e., improving basis exchanges, has remained an open question.

arxiv:2611.26846.title: Large 4-tangles in matroids are characterized by large internally 4-connected minors
arxiv:2611.26846.summary: Tangles were first introduced by Robertson and Seymour as an abstract way of treating highly connected substructures in graphs and matroids. For any truly highly connected substructure in a graph or matroid, all of the low-order separations in the object can be oriented towards it. This gives rise to a tangle.
arxiv:2611.26846.authors: Nick Brettell, Johannes Carmesin, Tony Huynh, Matthew E. Kroeker, Florian Lehner, Geoff Whittle

arxiv:2611.26879.title: Small spherical 7-designs in prime dimensions
arxiv:2611.26879.summary: For every prime $p\ge 29$, we construct an antipodal spherical $7$-design on $S^{p-1}$ with $42(p-1)(p+2)^2$ points. The construction uses eigenlines of finite Weil operators.

arxiv:2611.26888.title: Structure of linear extensions of posets and lexicographic shelling
arxiv:2611.26888.summary: We study some structure of linear extensions of a finite poset $P$ by investigating partial orders on the maximal chains of the lattice of order ideals $J(P)$. These partial orders on the maximal chains of $J(P)$ are called maximal chain descent orders (MCDO). MCDOs come from EL-labelings of finite bounded posets and encode the structure of shellings arising from EL-labelings.

arxiv:2611.26896.title: On the cyclic and dihedral Ramsey numbers of separated caterpillars and nested matchings
arxiv:2611.26896.summary: We consider all graphs to have vertex sets of the form $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, n-1\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For graphs $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$, the cyclic Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is the smallest $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every $k$-edge-coloring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H_j$ in color $j$ for some $j \in \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$, with the vertices appearing in the same cyclic order as in $H_j$. The dihedral Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{dih}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is defined analogously, with the difference that the direction of the cyclic order is ignored.
arxiv:2611.26896.authors: Ivan Damnjanovi\'c, Daniil Furmanov, Jon A. Maccarello, Julien Menet

arxiv:2611.26905.title: The Strong AJ Conjecture for Hyperbolic Prime Knots is False
arxiv:2611.26905.summary: Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$. The strong AJ conjecture relates two of its invariants. The first is the minimal-order annihilator $\widehat A$ of the $n$th colored Jones polynomial $J(n)$.

arxiv:2611.26922.title: Categorification of the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebras of polygons
arxiv:2611.26922.summary: Let $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ be the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebra of a polygon with $m$ boundary punctures ($m\geq 3$). Building on the quantum cluster algebra structure of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ established by Cao and the authors, and on the monoidal category $\mathcal{C}(\Delta^{m-2})$ of finite-dimensional modules over the quantum affine algebra $U_q'(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n)$ introduced by Kashiwara, Kim, Oh and Park, where $\Delta$ is the Garside element of ${\rm Br}_n$, we give a monoidal categorification of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$. As a consequence, $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ has a basis with positive structure…

arxiv:2611.26943.title: An Infinite Family of Overpartition Congruences Modulo 1944
arxiv:2611.26943.summary: Let $\overline p(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$. We prove that $\overline p(16^\alpha(96n+76))\equiv0\pmod{1944}$ for all nonnegative integers $\alpha$ and $n$, extending the congruence for $\overline p(96n+76)$ established by Smoot. The key step is a three-term congruence modulo $243$ relating $\overline p(m)$, $\overline p(16m)$, and $\overline p(256m)$ for $m\equiv4\pmod6$.

arxiv:2611.26947.title: Tensor products of additive groups as reciprocity sheaves
arxiv:2611.26947.summary: We compute the Nisnevich reciprocity sheaves associated with tensor products of the cube-invariant objects for the additive and multiplicative groups, with at least one additive factor. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, these sheaves decompose into direct sums of absolute K$\"a$hler differential sheaves with binomial multiplicities. As an application, we compute the associated reciprocity sheaves of the Hochschild homology of the additive object.

arxiv:2611.26953.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on weighted Catalan numbers
arxiv:2611.26953.summary: We construct infinitely many counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on when the 2-adic valuations of weighted Catalan numbers equal those of Catalan numbers.

arxiv:2611.26962.title: Stability of independence polynomials of well-covered Ferrers graphs
arxiv:2611.26962.summary: We prove that every root of the independence polynomial of a well-covered Ferrers graph lies in the open unit disk centered at $-1$, that is, $|x+1|<1$. Consequently, the polynomial is strictly stable. We also exhibit a general Ferrers graph whose independence polynomial is not stable.
arxiv:2611.26962.authors: Ta Quang Anh, Do Trong Hoang, Nguyen Minh Nhat

arxiv:2611.26974.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
arxiv:2611.26974.summary: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.

arxiv:2611.26982.title: Persistent Mayer Path Homology and Mayer Path Laplacian
arxiv:2611.26982.summary: In topological data analysis, path homology accounts for directed graph while combinatorial Laplacian extends homology groups to spectral theory. However, these approaches are built on a boundary operator with condition $\partial^2=0$. Mayer homology replaces this condition with $N$-nilpotent boundary map $\partial^N=0$.

arxiv:2611.26990.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
arxiv:2611.26990.summary: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications.

arxiv:2611.26991.title: Explicit Bases for the Second Integral Homology of Cactus Groups
arxiv:2611.26991.summary: In this paper, we determine the second integral homology $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$ of cactus groups $J_n$. We first use Hopf's formula and Pontryagin products to obtain a smaller generating set of $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$. We then construct a detecting homomorphism to prove that these generators are linearly independent and hence form an explicit basis.

arxiv:2611.27000.title: The Order of the Inertia Bound for Random Graphs
arxiv:2611.27000.summary: For an $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $n_{\geq0}(G)$ be the minimum number of nonnegative eigenvalues among zero-diagonal Hermitian matrices supported on $G$, allowing zero edge weights. For $n\geq2$ and $G\sim G(n,1/2)$, we prove $n_{\geq0}(G)\geq c_2n/\log(2n)$ with probability at least $1-\exp(-c_1n\log(2n))$, where $c_1,c_2>0$ are absolute constants. This proves a Hermitian extension of the Kwan--Wigderson conjecture.

arxiv:2611.27001.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
arxiv:2611.27001.summary: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story.

arxiv:2611.27018.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
arxiv:2611.27018.summary: We study exact representations of maximum functions by ReLU networks with two hidden layers and integer parameters. The least positive output multiplier is two for the six-input maximum, and either two or six for the seven-input maximum. We obtain these bounds from integral cubical fillings and a coefficient-preserving passage from polytope identities to networks.

arxiv:2611.27023.title: Nowhere-zero $9$-flows of signed graphs
arxiv:2611.27023.summary: In 1983, Bouchet conjectured that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $6$-flow. DeVos et al.\ proved that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $11$-flow. In this paper, we show that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $9$-flow.
arxiv:2611.27023.authors: Miaomiao Han, Jiaao Li, Rong Luo, Xiangqian Zhou

arxiv:2611.27025.title: Constructing toric diagonal modules with short linear resolutions
arxiv:2611.27025.summary: For a complete simplicial toric variety $X$, we construct a collection of Cohen--Macaulay modules with linear resolutions where the associated sheaf is the diagonal. Through this work, we see that the resolutions constructed by Favero--Huang from homotopy path algebras and those constructed by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev can be viewed as two dual methods to construct resolutions of the diagonal starting from a compatible $\mathbb{Z}^n$-stratification.

arxiv:2611.27036.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
arxiv:2611.27036.summary: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.
arxiv:2611.27036.authors: Jinbing Chen, Colin Grant, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

arxiv:2611.27040.title: An explicit Cassels--Tate pairing in characteristic $2$ and the parity of $2$-Selmer ranks
arxiv:2611.27040.summary: Let $K$ be a global field of characteristic $2$ and $\varphi\colon E\to E'$ the Verschiebung of an ordinary elliptic curve $E/K$ with a rational point of order $2$. We prove an explicit formula for the homogeneous-space Cassels--Tate pairing on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$ as a sum of local Artin--Schreier symbols, show that it coincides with Kramer's descent pairing and, on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$, with the pairing induced by Milne's flat duality, and deduce that it is non-degenerate on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]/\hat\varphi(\Sha(E'/K)[2])$. For every ordinary elliptic curve $A/K$ we express the parity of $\mathrm{rk}\,A(K)+\dim\Sha(A/K)[2]$ by local terms (after Kramer), and identify these with local root…

arxiv:2611.27054.title: Period maps and the $C_{\rm st}$ conjecture
arxiv:2611.27054.summary: We construct a family of elliptic curves over an open disc whose total space violates the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture in degree $1$. Hence the conjecture, known for proper and for Stein varieties, as well as for products of such, does not extend to proper families over Stein bases. This is an instance of a general criterion: the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture holds for the total space of a smooth proper family over a sufficiently small open disc if and only if its period map is constant, i.e., all Gauss--Manin Higgs fields vanish or, equivalently, the $p$-adic local systems $R^if_*\mathbf{Q}_p$ are geometrically constant.
arxiv:2611.27054.authors: Pierre Colmez, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}, Xinyu Shao

arxiv:2611.27055.title: Real-analytic actions of lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact $n$-manifolds
arxiv:2611.27055.summary: We classify real-analytic actions of arbitrary lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact connected $n$-manifolds without boundary, $n\geq 3$, with no invariant-volume assumption. After finite-index restriction, the action has finite image, extends to a connected Lie group locally isomorphic to $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ with an equivariant finite cover when needed, or is obtained by analytic surgery with at least one torus piece. In the last case the lattice is commensurable with a conjugate of $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb Z)$.

arxiv:2611.27081.title: Demazure-Lusztig type operators and correspondences on Kato Catalan varieties
arxiv:2611.27081.summary: We study the integral equivariant cohomology rings of Kato Catalan varieties $\mathscr{X}_\Psi$ associated with arbitrary root ideals $\Psi$ in type $A$. These varieties are smooth projective compactifications of the vector subbundles $T^*_\Psi\mathcal{B}$ of the cotangent bundle of the complete flag variety $\mathcal{B}$. Let $K$ denote the product of the general linear group (or its maximal torus) with the loop rotation torus $\mathbb{C}^\times$.

arxiv:2611.27098.title: Idempotent generically stable measures in NIP groups
arxiv:2611.27098.summary: Let $\mu$ be a global generically stable Keisler measure on a type-definable group in an NIP theory. Then $\mu$ is idempotent if and only if it is the unique translation-invariant measure on its type-definable stabilizer subgroup. This resolves the NIP case of the Idempotent Measure problem studied by Chernikov, Gannon, and Krupi\'nski.

arxiv:2611.27113.title: The $n!$ theorem via quaternionic rotation of Cherednik algebras
arxiv:2611.27113.summary: We give a proof of the $n!$ theorem based on the representation theory of Cherednik algebras and an analog of the rotation of complex structures arising from an action of the quaternions.

arxiv:2611.27120.title: Recursive Relations for Categorified Young Symmetrizers in Type $\mathbb{B}$
arxiv:2611.27120.summary: The category of bounded-above chain complexes of Soergel bimodules of any finite type $\mathbb{X}_n$ contains a symmetrizer complex $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{X}_n}$ which kills non-identity Soergel bimodules up to homotopy. It has been shown in previous work that, in type $\mathbb{A}$, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_{n+1}}$ can be obtained as a semi-infinite extension between copies of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_n}$ and its product with a Jucys-Murphy complex. We prove an analogous recursion holds between the symmetrizers for type $\mathbb{B}_n$ and $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$.

arxiv:2611.27126.title: Independence number, clique number, and maximum degree
arxiv:2611.27126.summary: We prove that for every integer $r \ge 3$, every $K_r$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $\delta(G) > (5r-11)n/(5r-5)$ satisfies $\alpha(G) \ge n/(r-1)$. This resolves a conjecture posed by Brandt in 2001 and establishes the sharp minimum-degree threshold for guaranteeing an independent set of size at least $n/(r - 1)$ in $K_r$-free graphs.

arxiv:2611.27130.title: Nonreduced Finkelberg-Mirkovi\'c Schubert schemes
arxiv:2611.27130.summary: We develop an effective numerical criterion ($\theta$-minimality) to detect the nonreducedness of Finkelberg-Mirkovi\'c (FM) Schubert schemes via tangent-space comparisons at arbitrary torus-fixed points. We completely classify the dominant coweights admitting $\theta$-minimal pairs. As an application, we obtain nonreduced FM Schubert schemes in every type other than $A_n$ and $C_n$.
arxiv:2611.27130.authors: Marc Besson, Jiuzu Hong, Huanhuan Yu

arxiv:2611.27184.title: Radio antipodal number for the Cartesian product of a complete graph and a path
arxiv:2611.27184.summary: A radio antipodal labeling of a graph $G$ is a function $f$ that assigns a non negative integer to each vertex in such a way that for any pair of distinct vertices $x$ and $y$, the condition $|f(x)-f(y)| \geq d-d(x,y)$ is satisfied, where $d$ and $d(x,y)$ represent the diameter of graph $G$, and distance between $x$ and $y$ in graph $G$, respectively. The span of radio antipodal labeling $f$ is defined as $span(f) = \max\{|f(x)-f(y)| : x,y \in V(G)\}$. The radio antipodal number of graph $G$, denoted by $an(G)$, is defined as $an(G) := \min_{f}\{span(f)\}$ with minimum taken over all radio antipodal labelings $f$ of $G$.

arxiv:2611.27204.title: Rigidity in the Lichnerowicz inequality for word-length semigroups
arxiv:2611.27204.summary: We give an operator-algebraic characterization of Cayley graphs that are partial cubes, that is, embed isometrically into a hypercube. More precisely, noncommutative versions of the Lichnerowicz inequality control the spectral gap of the generator of a quantum Markov semigroup by the constant in the complete $\Gamma_2$-criterion of Junge and Zeng or the constant in the geometric Ricci criterion of Junge, LaRacuente and Li. We show that for word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras, equality in either of these inequalities occurs exactly when the Cayley graph is a partial cube.

arxiv:2611.27205.title: Simple Yetter-Drinfeld Modules and Extensions over Fractional Infinite-Dimensional Taft Algebras
arxiv:2611.27205.summary: We classify all simple Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a fractional infinite-dimensional Taft Hopf algebra $T=T(\underline m,t,\xi)$, including the infinite-dimensional induced family and the finite-dimensional truncated and cyclic families. We determine their explicit structures and isomorphism criteria, and classify first extensions between finite-dimensional simple modules together with their middle modules. We also establish the primary decomposition with respect to $z^t$ and prove that every nonzero-eigenvalue component is wild when $m>1$.

arxiv:2611.27207.title: Tight Probabilistic Aspects of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs
arxiv:2611.27207.summary: Friends-and-strangers graphs, introduced by Defant and Kravitz, model arrangements of people on positions. We consider two graphs $X$ and $Y$ on $n$ vertices. The vertices of $X$ represent positions with edges denoting adjacencies while the vertices of $Y$ represent people with edges denoting friendships.

arxiv:2611.27238.title: Combinatorial relative orientability for toric and tropical geometry
arxiv:2611.27238.summary: Many problems in enumerative geometry are solved by computing the degree of the top Chern class of a suitable vector bundle. Results from $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy theory allow to answer enumerative questions over arbitrary fields, replacing the top Chern class by the Euler class in Chow-Witt groups. For its degree to be well-defined, one needs the vector bundle to be relatively oriented.

arxiv:2611.27275.title: On the Delandtsheer Conjecture
arxiv:2611.27275.summary: We prove the Delandtsheer Conjecture of 1988 that a line-primitive automorphism group of a finite linear space is point-primitive.

arxiv:2611.27280.title: Bridging Badiou's Gaps: Topos Theory and the Bodies of Mathematical Expression
arxiv:2611.27280.summary: This article develops a second stage of an argument begun in 2013, revisiting Alain Badiou's use of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. The previous article diagnosed Badiou's reduction of topos theory to its atomistic, localic form as the scientific scapegoat in his attack on 'democratic materialism'. Now I ask what follows when this logicist illusion is dispelled and the categorical alternative is taken seriously, particularly with respect to forcing, semantic expression, and mathematical subjectification that constitute the key elements of Badiou's earlier work.

arxiv:2611.27284.title: The Four-Cycle Extremal Number of the Seven-Cube
arxiv:2611.27284.summary: We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest number of edges in a four-cycle-free subgraph of the seven-dimensional hypercube is 304. In a hypothetical 305-edge subgraph, three-star counting and a local computational lemma force every degree to be four or five. A square-counting identity and an inequality for opposite facets then reduce the proof to five candidate facet profiles, excluded by two further local statements.
arxiv:2611.27284.authors: Zheli Zhou, Haitong Ma, Ruofeng Yang, Tianzhi Ren, Kuan Yang, Shuai Li

arxiv:2611.27297.title: Chern classes, Poincar\'e polynomials, and Bernstein-Sato polynomials of plane curves
arxiv:2611.27297.summary: We show that the Poincar\'e polynomial of a reduced plane curve $C$ is the Chern polynomial of the dual of the bundle of Jacobian syzygies of $C$. Using the Zeuthen-Segre formula, we prove that its value at $t=-1$ equals the Euler number of the complement of $C$ up to the correction term $\mu(C)-\tau(C)$, so the two numbers coincide if and only if all singularities of $C$ are quasi-homogeneous. As applications, we show that the defect in a combinatorial inequality for free $d$-arrangements is the square of the difference of the exponents, extend the addition technique to arbitrary reduced plane curves, and locate the roots of local Bernstein-Sato polynomials at ordinary singular points.

arxiv:2611.27300.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
arxiv:2611.27300.summary: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions.

arxiv:2611.27312.title: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
arxiv:2611.27312.summary: Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$.

arxiv:2611.27343.title: A general reduction and explicit remoteness formulas for exact slow 2-Nim
arxiv:2611.27343.summary: In exact slow $2$-Nim, a move removes one token from each of two nonempty piles. For any number of piles, we relate Smith remoteness in the exact game to the remoteness $D$ of Moore's slow game on the piles that remain after a largest pile is removed. If the total number of tokens $N$ is odd, the exact game has remoteness $\min(D,\lfloor N/2\rfloor)$.

arxiv:2611.27378.title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
arxiv:2611.27378.summary: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden…

arxiv:2611.27380.title: A Combinatorial Construction of Symmetric Magic Squares of Order Four
arxiv:2611.27380.summary: We construct all symmetric nonnegative integer matrices of order four having a common sum on every row, column, and both diagonals. The construction is a disjoint union of twelve translates of free submonoids, each with five uniquely determined nonnegative integer parameters.Twelve is the smallest possible number of classes among finite disjoint unions of translates of free submonoids generated by five elements, even when generators outside the Hilbert basis are allowed. A comparison-based case analysis supplies integer inverse formulas and assigns every point on the shared faces to exactly one class.

arxiv:2611.27395.title: Real stable multivariate Delannoy polynomials and their Rayleigh differences
arxiv:2611.27395.summary: The univariate Delannoy polynomials are known to have only real zeros. We construct a real stable multivariate refinement of these polynomials using weighted lattice paths and give both algebraic and combinatorial proofs of stability. More strongly, we show that every Rayleigh difference of the multivariate Delannoy polynomials is a perfect square and give an explicit factorization.

arxiv:2611.27429.title: Non-local ergodic measures in symplectic dynamics
arxiv:2611.27429.summary: We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one acts on a compact surface and has a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic perturbation of this system displays a large normally hyperbolic lamination on which the natural invariant measure is ergodic. The proof, which introduces a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity, combines tools ranging from KAM theory to geometric measure theory and is robust enough to be of interest in more general configurations.

arxiv:2611.27472.title: There are hard braids
arxiv:2611.27472.summary: Let us call a trivial braid hard if it cannot be untangled by Reidemeister moves without increasing the number of crossings. Are there hard trivial braids? Our paper answers this question.

arxiv:2611.27475.title: An affine surface with 3-step nilpotent fundamental group
arxiv:2611.27475.summary: We construct a smooth complex affine surface $Y$ such that $\pi_1(Y)$ is virtually $3$-step nilpotent, but not virtually $2$-step nilpotent. This gives a negative answer to the quasi-projective version of Campana's nilpotency problem.

arxiv:2611.27519.title: Additive cubes are avoidable by a non-uniform morphism of length $6$ over $\{0,a,b\}$ (with $b \ge 4$ and $\gcd(a,b) = 1$)
arxiv:2611.27519.summary: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over every ternary alphabet $\{0, a, b\}$ with $1 \le a < b$, $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, and $b \ge 4$, thereby solving and extending Rao's~(2015) conjecture from $b \ge 6$ down to $b \ge 4$. Our construction applies a single dual pair of parameterized non-uniform morphisms of image length at most~$6$ to the additive-cube-free word $\mathbf{w}$ of Cassaigne et al.~(2014). For $b \ge 10$, we prove that every additive square in the image is an abelian square, reducing additive cubes to abelian cubes; the absence of abelian cubes and the $24$ finite cases with $4 \le b \le 9$ are then certified via the finite-graph method of Jamet and Rosenfeld~(2026).

arxiv:2611.27528.title: Rigidity and nonrigidity for interval translation maps
arxiv:2611.27528.summary: Almost every infinite-type interval translation map in the Bruin--Troubetzkoy family, and in Bruin's family with any fixed number of branches, is rigid for its invariant probability, where typicality is understood with respect to the intrinsic induction parameter measure. We prove this by exhibiting explicit repeated-word blocks in the induction and showing that their cylinders recur. In the opposite direction, we give a sufficient condition for nonrigidity of a primitive aperiodic substitution: the existence of a rational periodic vector of its incidence matrix in the return-word space whose coordinate sum is nonzero.

arxiv:2611.27531.title: Squarefree powers of simplicial forests
arxiv:2611.27531.summary: The highest nonzero squarefree power of an edge ideal always has linear quotients, whereas this property can fail even for the facet ideal of a pure two-dimensional simplicial tree. This raises the question of which combinatorial conditions ensure linear quotients beyond the graph case. We characterize the squarefree powers of facet ideals of pure simplicial forests that have linear quotients, showing that this property is equivalent to having a linear resolution or being linearly related.
arxiv:2611.27531.authors: Marie Amalore Nambi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Dharm Veer

arxiv:2611.27557.title: Real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices preserving an ergodic volume
arxiv:2611.27557.summary: We classify real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices that preserve an ergodic smooth volume on a compact manifold. On an invariant open dense set of full volume, the action is analytically conjugate to the restriction of an affine action on finitely many copies of one double quotient. The conjugacy carries Haar probability to the given volume.

arxiv:2611.27562.title: Counting cliques in optimal $1$-planar graphs
arxiv:2611.27562.summary: Extremal problems concerning the maximum number of cliques in $n$-vertex graphs from a given graph class have been widely investigated. In this contribution, we present several results on counting cliques that extend beyond the existing framework. Firstly, we address this problem for the class of optimal 1-planar graphs where we determine the maximum numbers of copies of $K_3$, $K_4$, and $K_5$ in an $n$-vertex optimal 1-planar graphs and characterize all extremal graphs.

arxiv:2611.27575.title: A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions
arxiv:2611.27575.summary: For an integer $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ be the generating polynomial of the Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and weight $c$ at positive height, and let $D_{k,n}(x,c)=\det(a_{i+j,k}(x,c))_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. We prove that for all $k\ge0$ and $n\ge2k+2$ $$D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2,$$ a quadratic recurrence conjectured by J. Cigler in 2023 (eq.

arxiv:2611.27591.title: Determinantal upper bounds for ternary matrices
arxiv:2611.27591.summary: We obtain a new, sharper upper bound for the determinant of a matrix of order $n \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$ with entries in the complex third-roots of unity. This bound is an analog of Ehlich's bound for binary matrices of order $n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and it is obtained by first applying an appropriate normalization, or balancing, procedure for matrices with root-of-unity entries and then generalizing Ehlich's argument. This new bound achieves an asymptotic fraction of approximately 74% of the Hadamard bound.

arxiv:2611.27597.title: Classification of strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure surface singularities with imperfect residue fields
arxiv:2611.27597.summary: We study strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure normal surface singularities whose residue fields are not necessarily perfect. We characterize strong $F$-regularity in terms of the weighted dual graph and geometric reducedness of the exceptional components of the minimal resolution, extending Hara's classification over algebraically closed residue fields. We also determine the possible dual graphs of $F$-pure surface singularities and give converse criteria.

arxiv:2611.27657.title: The categorical graph minor conjecture and matching complexes
arxiv:2611.27657.summary: In the graph minor category $\mathcal G$ of Miyata, Proudfoot and Ramos, the morphisms are the ways of obtaining one connected graph from another by deleting and contracting edges. The categorical graph minor conjecture asserts that every submodule of a finitely generated $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module is finitely generated; it is known for graphs of bounded first Betti number. We disprove this conjecture: it fails for the module assigning to each graph the free module on its spanning trees, which is generated by one element.

arxiv:2611.27685.title: Proximity and Remoteness in Trees with given Segment Sequence
arxiv:2611.27685.summary: The average distance of a vertex $v$ of a connected graph $G$ is the arithmetic mean of the distances from $v$ to all other vertices of $G$. The proximity $\pi(G)$ and the remoteness $\rho(G)$ of $G$ are the minimum and the maximum of the average distances of the vertices of $G$, respectively.
