A segment $S$ of a tree is a path-subtree whose terminal vertices are either branching or pendant vertices, and all internal vertices have degree $2$.
arxiv:2611.27685.authors: Imran Allie, Brandon Du Preez, Zion Hefty, Sonwabile Mafunda

arxiv:2611.27687.title: Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
arxiv:2611.27687.summary: We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(\mu\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows.
arxiv:2611.27687.authors: Shiqi Li, Jiawei He, Jianhua Huang

arxiv:2611.27699.title: Extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number
arxiv:2611.27699.summary: The binding number of a graph, introduced by Woodall [J. Combin. Theory, Ser.

arxiv:2611.27706.title: Projectivized ASEP-Bethe system and counting solutions
arxiv:2611.27706.summary: This paper addresses the problem of counting solutions to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equations. In an earlier preprint, Brattain, Do, and Saenz presented an algebro-geometric method for counting the number of such solutions. As their method relies on sophisticated machinery, it requires advanced knowledge of algebraic geometry and topology.

arxiv:2611.27727.title: Calabi-Yau fibrations and orbifold Mordell
arxiv:2611.27727.summary: We construct isotrivial projective families of Calabi-Yau varieties with arbitrarily large inf-multiplicities and no divisible fibres over the projective line. As an application, we show that any single instance of Campana's Orbifold Mordell Conjecture for a general-type C-pair of genus at most one (with only finite multiplicities) implies that the Weakly Special Conjecture is false.

arxiv:2611.27730.title: Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions
arxiv:2611.27730.summary: Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size.

arxiv:2611.27731.title: Boundary of the Lagrange and Markov spectra near Hall's ray
arxiv:2611.27731.summary: The Lagrange and Markov spectra, denoted by $L$ and $M$, respectively, are closed subsets of the real line with intricate fractal geometry related to Diophantine approximations. In 1975, Freiman proved that both spectra contain the ray $[c_F,\infty)$, where $c_F=4.527829566\dots$, and that this ray is optimal, as both spectra avoid a tiny interval $(\nu_F,c_F)$. Using renormalization techniques and the thickness of Cantor sets, we prove that the boundaries $\partial L$ and $\partial M$ have positive Hausdorff dimensions arbitrarily close to $\nu_F$.
arxiv:2611.27731.authors: Harold Erazo, Carlos Matheus, Carlos Gustavo Moreira

arxiv:2611.27755.title: Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions and the Hirota-Miwa equation
arxiv:2611.27755.summary: For $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ count Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and $c$ above it, and let $D_{k,n}=\det\bigl(a_{i+j,k}(x,c)\bigr)_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. T. Yu proved Cigler's conjecture $D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2$ $(n\ge2k+2)$ by writing $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant of Chebyshev polynomials modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$.

arxiv:2611.27775.title: Splitting types of Richelot isogenies over finite fields and a newform of weight four
arxiv:2611.27775.summary: A factorization $f=uvw$ of a square-free sextic over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic into three monic quadratics defines a genus-2 curve with a rational $(2,2)$-isogeny kernel, and the Richelot construction attaches to it three dual quadratics $U,V,W$. We determine, for every odd prime power $q$, the number of such factorizations with prescribed splitting behaviour over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of all six quadratics. Each of the $64$ counts is $q(q-1)(q+1-n_f)/64$ times $C(q)\pm t_q$, where $n_f$ is the number of roots of $f$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$, $C$ is an explicit monic cubic, and $t_q$ is the trace of Frobenius attached to the newform $\eta(2z)^{4}\eta(4z)^{4}$ of weight $4$ and…

arxiv:2611.27781.title: On the factorization of Dirac hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.27781.summary: A celebrated result from the 70s due to Baranyai states that the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices decomposes into perfect matchings if $k\mid n$. We prove a minimum degree version of this result. Note that a necessary condition for a $k$-uniform hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices to admit a decomposition into perfect matchings is that $G$ is vertex-regular and $k\mid n$.
arxiv:2611.27781.authors: Yangyang Cheng, Stefan Glock, Andrew Lane

arxiv:2611.27793.title: Extremal $K_t$-intersecting graph families for large $t$
arxiv:2611.27793.summary: In this paper, we show that for every sufficiently large positive integer $t$ and every integer $n \ge t$, every $K_t$-intersecting family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs on vertex set $[n]$ has size at most $2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}}$. Furthermore, when the equality is attained, $\mathcal{G}$ must consist of all graphs on $[n]$ that contain some fixed copy of $K_t$. Our result settles a conjecture of Ellis, Filmus, and Friedgut for sufficiently large $t$.

arxiv:2611.27800.title: Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus
arxiv:2611.27800.summary: We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type.

arxiv:2611.27803.title: Kneser-Tits over fields of cohomological dimension $\le 2$ (with an appendix by Alexis Bouthier and Federico Scavia)
arxiv:2611.27803.summary: We settle the Kneser-Tits problem over every field $k$ of (separable) cohomological dimension $\le 2$, thus resolving a conjecture of Gille. More precisely, for such a $k$ and a semisimple, simply connected $k$-group $G$ whose indecomposable factors over $k$ are isotropic, we show that $G(k)$ is generated by "elementary matrices" (the $k$-points of the unipotent radicals of the parabolic $k$-subgroups of $G$), in other words, that $K_1^G(k) \cong 1$. In fact, we show this vanishing already when $k$ has separable $p$-dimension $\le 2$ in the sense of Gille with respect to a subset of the torsion primes $p$ of $G$, and we reinterpret the separable $p$-dimension itself via syntomic cohomology.

arxiv:2611.27825.title: An arithmetic theory of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra
arxiv:2611.27825.summary: We show geometric and dimensional properties of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra for both $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$ using the projective cocycle steering method, which we introduce. In particular, we show the existence of a simultaneous Hall ray for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, a simultaneous Hall interval for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$, regimes of full and positive Hausdorff dimension, a scaling law, empty low spectra in certain cases, a compact set of full Hausdorff dimension in $(2Q\sqrt 3 - \varepsilon, 2Q\sqrt 3)$ where $Q$ is a common denominator of the finite set of rationals giving the translations, and…

arxiv:2611.27828.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
arxiv:2611.27828.summary: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$.

arxiv:2611.27838.title: Elementary Factorization For Continuous Orthogonal Matrices
arxiv:2611.27838.summary: We prove that every nullhomotopic continuous map, from a finite-dimensional normal topological space X to the complex special orthogonal group, is a product of elementary orthogonal matrices with entries in the ring of continuous functions. The number of factors is bounded by a constant depending only on the size of the matrices and the covering dimension of X. The same factorization result holds for nullhomotopic special orthogonal matrices with entries in a unital commutative Banach algebra.
arxiv:2611.27838.authors: Gaofeng Huang, Phan Quoc Bao Tran

arxiv:2611.27840.title: Elementary length of polynomial automorphisms in dimension at least three
arxiv:2611.27840.summary: In the plane the number and the degrees of the de Jonqui\`eres letters in a reduced word of a polynomial automorphism are invariants. For $n\ge3$ we study how much of a decomposition of an automorphism $F$ of $K^n$ into elementary maps can be recovered from $F$. Let $\Gamma(K,n)$ be the group of tame automorphisms of $K^n$ with Jacobian determinant $1$, which is generated by the elementary maps, and let $\ell(F)$ be the least number of elementary factors of $F\in\Gamma(K,n)$.

arxiv:2611.27861.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
arxiv:2611.27861.summary: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds.

arxiv:2611.27879.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$
arxiv:2611.27879.summary: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism.
arxiv:2611.27879.authors: Tobias Barthel, Lucas Mann, Rin Ray, Tomer M. Schlank, Andrew Senger, Jared Weinstein, Xinyu Zhou

arxiv:2611.27887.title: Recurrent sets and Lyapunov functions: from topological dynamics to weak KAM theory
arxiv:2611.27887.summary: The aim of this survey is to clarify the intimate relations between Lyapunov functions and chain recurrent sets. The study of this subject comes from a seminal paper by Conley and has had recent advances by the so-called Weak KAM Theory for homeomorphisms. We provide a survey of the state of the art, presenting recent improvements and connections with the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equation.
arxiv:2611.27887.authors: Olga Bernardi, Mattia Sensi, Jim Wiseman

arxiv:2611.27892.title: Critical Ising and Temperley-Lieb-Jones States: Cone Haag Duality and the Trivial Algebra Object
arxiv:2611.27892.summary: We compute the algebra object of two critical Ising states in the operator algebraic framework of fusion category symmetry. The boundary subalgebra is the even part of the Pauli chain, and its DHR category is the toric code. We treat two models.

arxiv:2611.27908.title: Representations of spectral systems over finite distributive lattices
arxiv:2611.27908.summary: A representation theorem is proved for spectral systems indexed by the lattice of down-sets of a finite poset P. Over an arbitrary associative ring, every excisive, homotopy-exact chain system of differential modules is isomorphic to the chain system of a projective P-graded differential module with a single upper-triangular differential. Consequently, every Cartan-Eilenberg system that is excisive and chain generated, together with its spectral system, admits such a differential model.

arxiv:2611.27925.title: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
arxiv:2611.27925.summary: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point.

arxiv:2611.27926.title: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
arxiv:2611.27926.summary: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram.

arxiv:2611.27934.title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
arxiv:2611.27934.summary: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$.
arxiv:2611.27934.authors: Mayank Goswami, Vasilis Livanos, Pasin Manurangsi, Arturo Merino, GiBeom Park, Adarsh Srinivasan

arxiv:2611.27936.title: Star Triangulations
arxiv:2611.27936.summary: We study full triangulations of planar point configurations consisting of $n$ points in convex position and one point in the interior, assuming that no three points are collinear (star configurations). Our main contribution is a classification of the star configurations up to combinatorial equivalence. We show that there are $2^{n-1}-n$ equivalence classes, by establishing a bijection between a star configuration and a particular Young diagram.

arxiv:2611.27937.title: Intervals of limit points for $B_{\alpha}$-spectral radii
arxiv:2611.27937.summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha A(G)+(1-\alpha)L(G)=(1-\alpha)D(G)+(2\alpha-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq \alpha\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_{\alpha}=1-\alpha$, $b_{\alpha}=|2\alpha-1|$, and $w_{\alpha}=a_{\alpha}+b_{\alpha}$.
arxiv:2611.27937.authors: Francesco Belardo, Callum Huntington, Elismar R. Oliveira, Vilmar Trevisan

arxiv:2611.27965.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
arxiv:2611.27965.summary: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time.

arxiv:2611.27972.title: Localization of weakly integral objects in braided fusion categories
arxiv:2611.27972.summary: An object $X$ of a braided fusion category is called weakly integral if $\mathrm{FPdim}(X)^2$ is an integer. We prove that every nonzero weakly integral object admits a localization, that is, a Yang-Baxter operator $R$ on a finite-dimensional vector space $W$ such that, for every $n$, the algebra homomorphisms from the group algebra of the braid group $B_n$ to $\mathrm{End}(W^{\otimes n})$ and to $\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})$, defined by $R$ and by the braiding, have the same kernel. The operator $R$ can be chosen unitary when the braided fusion category is unitary.

arxiv:2611.27974.title: H\"older continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
arxiv:2611.27974.summary: For a complex analytic variety and an exponent between zero and one, we study the sheaf of meromorphic functions that are locally H\"older continuous with that exponent for the outer metric. It sits between the structure sheaves of the seminormalization and of the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. We prove that these sheaves are coherent and that only finitely many of them are distinct, the exponents at which they change being rational numbers governed by the Rees valuations of the ideal of a certain diagonal.

arxiv:2611.28042.title: Raynaud and Gruson's flattening techniques in Berkovich geometry
arxiv:2611.28042.summary: Raynaud and Gruson introduced a flattening procedure for coherent sheaf in the schemes context that rely on sophisticated techniques of algebra and geometry. These methods were later used by Raynaud, Bosch and L\"utkebohmert in formal geometry, and more recently Ducros has developed analogous tools for Berkovich spaces. However, it should be noted that the expression "flattening by blowing up" is, in this context, a little abusive because the flattening process actually requires a succession of blow up and quasi-\'etale morphisms.

arxiv:2611.28049.title: Foata and Spot Commutation for Parking Functions
arxiv:2611.28049.summary: For a parking function $\alpha$, let $\mathrm{spot}(\alpha)$ be the permutation whose $i$th entry is the space occupied by car $i$ and let $\mathrm{foata}(w)$ be Foata's second fundamental transformation on words. Conjecture 6.3 of Celano et al. asserts that $\mathrm{foata}(\mathrm{spot}(\alpha)) = \mathrm{spot}(\mathrm{foata}(\alpha))$ for every unit interval parking function $\alpha$. This paper proves the identity for a larger class: parking functions where each prime component (borrowing Gessel's definition) of $\alpha$ is nondecreasing.

arxiv:2611.28059.title: Forsyth--Glaisher-Type Series for $1/\pi$ Involving Catalan Numbers and Harmonic Numbers
arxiv:2611.28059.summary: We develop an elementary method for constructing and evaluating families of Forsyth--Glaisher-type series for $1/\pi$. The approach is based on Newton's generalized binomial theorem, identities for generalized binomial coefficients, and Euler's beta integral, together with properties of the gamma and digamma functions. We establish several parameterized identities involving squares of central binomial coefficients and products of odd integers, from which we derive explicit evaluations in terms of $1/\pi$.
arxiv:2611.28059.authors: Kunle Adegoke, Robert Frontczak, Taras Goy

arxiv:2611.28060.title: Short Paper No. 2: Relations between integer sequences A003622 $\&$ A035336 and two criteria in respect of maximum degrees within the family of finite linear Jaco graphs
arxiv:2611.28060.summary: This paper establishes two relationships between integer sequences and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$. First, it characterizes the positive maximum degrees that occur exactly once within the family, showing that they are generated by the integer sequence A003622. Second, it determines the orders of the corresponding graphs and establishes their relationship with the integer sequence A035336.

arxiv:2611.28063.title: The Rotation Strategy Wins Penney's game for Permutations
arxiv:2611.28063.summary: In Penney's game for permutations, two players choose distinct patterns of the same length $k$, and independent random variables with a common continuous distribution are observed until the relative order of $k$ consecutive observations matches one of the patterns; the player who chose that pattern wins. Elizalde and Lin conjectured that the second player wins with probability greater than one half by answering the pattern $a_1a_2\cdots a_k$ with its rotation $a_ka_1\cdots a_{k-1}$. We prove that this conjecture holds for every $k\ge3$.

arxiv:2611.28064.title: Combinatorial Zeta Functions of Type $\widetilde A_2$
arxiv:2611.28064.summary: We develop a combinatorial zeta theory for finite colored triangular complexes $X$ whose vertex links satisfy a local hexagon condition. Their edge and chamber zeta functions $Z_1(X,u)$ and $Z_2(X,u)$ are Euler products over primitive closed geodesics. The M\"obius functions of the augmented local incidence posets define a vertex polynomial $M(X,u)$.

arxiv:2611.28065.title: Quadratic periods and preperiods in subtraction games with one varying move
arxiv:2611.28065.summary: We give two infinite families of counterexamples to Zhang's conjectures on the period and preperiod of the Sprague-Grundy sequence when a single move c is adjoined to a fixed subtraction set S. For S = {4,5,10} and c = 15t+13 with t >= 2, the least period is c+19 and the least preperiod is (c^2+21c+8)/15. For S = {3,7,10} and c = 90t+9 with t >= 1, the least period is (c^2+26c+615)/30 and the least preperiod is 19 less than the period.
arxiv:2611.28065.authors: Ruiqi Zhao, Qi Zhang, Zhihao Shi

arxiv:2611.28066.title: Face-neighbourly polyhedra with eight or nine faces and genus at most three
arxiv:2611.28066.summary: A polyhedral surface is face-neighbourly if every pair of faces shares an edge. We classify the combinatorial types of closed orientable face-neighbourly polyhedral surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with eight or nine faces and genus at most three, assuming trivalent vertices, simple planar polygonal faces and distinct supporting planes for adjacent faces. Several common edges between a pair of faces are allowed.

arxiv:2611.28073.title: Externally supported independence in split and proper interval graphs
arxiv:2611.28073.summary: An independent set $B$ in a graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfying the additional condition that the vertices in $N(B)$ are dominated by vertices in $V(G) \setminus N[B]$ is called an externally supported independent set (ESI-set for short). The maximum cardinality of such a set in $G$ is called externally supported independence number of $G$. We study the externally supported independence number in split graphs and proper interval graphs, two graph classes with unbounded clique-width.
arxiv:2611.28073.authors: Dragana Bo\v{z}ovi\'c, Tanja Dravec, Aleksander Kelenc

arxiv:2611.28155.title: Explicit Error Term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for Function Fields
arxiv:2611.28155.summary: We prove an explicit error term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for finite generically Galois \'etale morphisms of affine varieties over finite fields, under a mild condition on their size. The error term generalises the known results for curves, and depends only on invariants of the varieties. We present several applications to the explicit error term.

arxiv:2611.28162.title: Measure-class classification of achievable Cantorvals
arxiv:2611.28162.summary: An achievable Cantorval is a Cantorval that is the set of subsums of a convergent series of positive terms. We construct an explicit achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Lebesgue measure at least $2\prod_{j\ge 1}(1-2^{-j})=0.5775\ldots$. This answers a question of G{\l}{\k{a}}b and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski and gives a counterexample to the conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski that every achievable Cantorval is standard.

arxiv:2611.28178.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
arxiv:2611.28178.summary: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor.

arxiv:2611.28183.title: Correspondence between orbit equivalences and exact symplectomorphisms for Anosov flows
arxiv:2611.28183.summary: We show that for a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, two Anosov flows are orbital equivalent if and only if the corresponding Anosov Liouville structures are exact symplectomorphic.

arxiv:2611.28192.title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy
arxiv:2611.28192.summary: Training Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) on chaotic systems is difficult because small changes in model parameters can lead to rapidly growing differences in predictions. A rollout is a trajectory predicted by the model. Choosing its length from a single global Lyapunov time overlooks differences in local instability.

arxiv:2611.28204.title: The index from a super-point
arxiv:2611.28204.summary: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT.
arxiv:2611.28204.authors: Dhanvarsh Annamalai, Hyunook Hur, Thomas Hussel, Monica Jinwoo Kang, Craig Lawrie, Jaewon Song

arxiv:2611.28242.title: The Thue-Morse route to chaos in the open quantum baker map
arxiv:2611.28242.summary: We study the resonances of the quantum baker map opened by a window of width $w$ centred at $q_c$. For $q_c=1/2$ the survivor set of the classical doubling map with a hole goes from zero to positive topological entropy along the Thue-Morse route, and we find numerically, for $N$ up to $2^{25}$, that the resonance spectrum follows this route step by step, also where the entropy is zero. Below the threshold $w_c=4a^*-1$, with $a^*$ the Thue-Morse constant, the surviving cycles have periods $2^\nu$ and their thresholds accumulate doubly exponentially.

arxiv:2611.28255.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
arxiv:2611.28255.summary: Let $C/K$ be a curve of genus $g\geq 1$ over a discretely valued field $K$ with algebraically closed residue field. In this paper, we study the behaviour of the reduction type of $C$ under finite tame extensions. If $L/K$ is a tame extension of degree $n$, we give sufficient conditions on the reduction type $R$ of $C$ so that the reduction type of the base change $C_L$ is uniquely determined by $R$ and $n$.

arxiv:2611.28258.title: Low-slope Lefschetz fibrations with finitely presented fundamental groups
arxiv:2611.28258.summary: We prove that for any finitely presented group $G$, there exists a genus-$3k (k\in \Z)$ Lefschetz fibration over the two-sphere having slope as close as desired to $2$ and the fundamental group of the total space is isomorphic to given group $G$. These are the first examples not satisfying the slope inequality with total spaces being non-simply connected. As a corollary, by taking fiber sum of these Lefschetz fibrations with trivial genus-$3k$ Lefschetz fibration over any genus-$h(>0)$ (positive genus) surfaces, we obtain Lefschetz fibrations having slope arbitrarily close to $2$ with different fundamental groups over any genus-$h$ surface.

arxiv:2611.28264.title: A filtered basis for Haiman ideals
arxiv:2611.28264.summary: Given the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n, y_1, \dots, y_n]$, we consider the Haiman ideal $J(d)$ of polynomials that vanish to order $d$ on the diagonals. We define a rotational order on monomials and use it to construct a filtration on $J(d)$ and a bigraded, homogeneous, free $\mathbb{C}[\mathbf{y}]$-basis compatible with this filtration. This gives a new independent proof that $J(d)$ is free over $y$'s.

arxiv:2611.28292.title: The M\"obius Homology Laplacian for Persistence Modules
arxiv:2611.28292.summary: Persistent homology provides a framework for studying the evolution of topological features across filtered spaces. While persistence diagrams give discrete invariants that record the birth and death of homological features, they do not directly encode analytic or geometric structure associated to persistence modules. This paper develops a spectral framework for persistent homology by introducing and studying a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex, called the M\"obius homology Laplacian.

arxiv:2611.28329.title: Bivariant $K$-theory for bornological algebras
arxiv:2611.28329.summary: We construct a presentable, stable \(\infty\)-category \(\bKK\), and exhibit it as the target of the universal functor from the category of bornological algebras into cocomplete, stable \(\infty\)-categories, preserving filtered colimits, and satisfying smooth homotopy invariance, excision, and stabilisation with respect to Schatten-class or smooth compact operators. We also construct a bivariant \(K\)-theory \(\nKK\) for suitably nuclear bornological algebras, and show that it is a right Bousfield localisation of \(\bKK\). The category \(\nKK\) is symmetric monoidal and admits a bivariant Chern character to local cyclic homology.

arxiv:2611.28339.title: Kleinian groups with tunnel number one
arxiv:2611.28339.summary: We give a structural theory for the holonomy groups of hyperbolic links with tunnel number 1 in arbitrary 3-manifolds. This is a first step towards understanding the canonical triangulations of such links, as it generalises the combinatorial structure theory of two-bridge link groups that is an input to the Sakuma--Weeks triangulation.

arxiv:2611.28340.title: Enumerative Chromatic Choosability of Complete Multipartite Graphs with Small Partite Sets
arxiv:2611.28340.summary: Chromatic choosability is a notion of fundamental importance in list coloring. A graph is chromatic-choosable when its chromatic number is equal to its list chromatic number. In their 1979 paper on list coloring, Erd\H{o}s, Rubin, and Taylor showed that complete $m$-partite graphs with every partite set of size 2, denoted by $K_{2*m}$, are chromatic-choosable.
arxiv:2611.28340.authors: Sarah Allred, Joseph T. Brown, Devin Dickinson, H. C. Fritz, Aiden McCain, Jeffrey A. Mudrock, Daniel Smith, Morgan Taylor, Benjamin Whatley

arxiv:2611.28360.title: Triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes
arxiv:2611.28360.summary: We study fractional triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes, unifying the settings of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions and the high-dimensional Dirac problem for Steiner triple systems. We prove that every sufficiently large two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum degree at least $(1-d_1)n$ and maximum missing codegree at most $d_2n$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition, provided $d_1/0.21+d_2/0.27\leq 1$. As an immediate consequence, we prove the asymptotic form of Lee's high-dimensional Dirac conjecture: every sufficiently large admissible $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum codegree at least $(3/4+\varepsilon)n$ contains a Steiner…
arxiv:2611.28360.authors: Michelle Delcourt, Thomas Lesgourgues, Luke Postle

arxiv:2611.28392.title: Improved bounds for the binary Chowla conjecture
arxiv:2611.28392.summary: For the M\"obius function $\mu$ and every fixed $0 < \epsilon < 1$, we prove \[ \sum_{n \le x} \mu(n) \mu(n + 1) \ll_{\epsilon} \frac{x}{(\log x)^{1 - \epsilon}}. \] This improves on OpenAI's recent bound of $x/(\log x)^c$, where $c > 0$ is a tiny absolute constant. The proof echoes the graph expansion framework of Helfgott, Radziwill, and Pilatte on the logarithmic Chowla conjecture, earlier Fourier analytic methods of Matom\"aki, Radziwill, and Tao on the Chowla conjecture on average, as well as work of Ter\"av\"ainen and the author for M\"obius on shifted primes.

arxiv:2611.28406.title: Failed Vertex Covering Graph Reconfiguration
arxiv:2611.28406.summary: A failed vertex cover of a graph is a vertex set that leaves at least one edge uncovered. The associated token addition and removal (TAR) graph has the failed vertex covers as vertices, with two sets adjacent when they differ by one vertex. We characterize when two finite graphs have isomorphic failed vertex cover TAR graphs, allowing disconnected graphs, loops, and parallel edges.

arxiv:2611.28407.title: A general triangle generation of the $d$-dimensional Genocchi numbers
arxiv:2611.28407.summary: We establish a uniform recurrence relation for the rook numbers of generalized Genocchi boards of dimension $d\geq 3$. The recurrence for each row of the rook-number triangle is expressed in terms of the preceding row, with coefficients given by products of consecutive powers and finite sums involving Stirling numbers of the second kind. The proof decomposes the boundary of the board into blocks that correspond to the coordinates equal to 1.
arxiv:2611.28407.authors: Derek Hanely, Edison Mu\c{c}llari, Vasily Zadorozhnyy

arxiv:2611.28412.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
arxiv:2611.28412.summary: Let $\Gamma_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leq\Gamma_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.

arxiv:2611.28415.title: Essential and disjoint edge numbers for graphs and hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.28415.summary: We study the extension to arbitrary forbidden sets of the property that every graph has a bipartition over which at least half of the graph edges are cross-edges, and obtain analogous results in the hypergraph setting.

arxiv:2611.28425.title: A characterization of Ramsey property with application to dynamical systems
arxiv:2611.28425.summary: The infinitary Ramsey theorem says that in any finite partition {V^i;~i=1,2,\cdots,n} of the the family of k-subsets of N, there exists V^i having an infinite subset M of N such that any k-set from M is in V^i. This property of V^i is called the Ramsey property. We characterize this property in term of ultrafilter.

arxiv:2611.28449.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities
arxiv:2611.28449.summary: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $,…

arxiv:2611.28464.title: Spaces of ratios of schemes and \'etale cohomology
arxiv:2611.28464.summary: We introduce the arithmetic topologies on the spaces of ratios for log schemes and prove the basic properties of their cohomologies.
arxiv:2611.28464.authors: Kazuya Kato, Chikara Nakayama, Sampei Usui

arxiv:2611.28470.title: Totally odd clique immersions in graphs with bounded independence number
arxiv:2611.28470.summary: We prove that every $n$-vertex graph with at least one edge and independence number at most an integer $a\ge2$, where $n\ge a$, contains a totally odd strong immersion of \[ K_{\left\lceil (n+a-1)/(2a-3/2) \right\rceil}, \] with every branch path of length at most $2a-1$. We also prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most $a$ and no totally odd strong $K_t$-immersion with branch paths of length at most $2a-1$ satisfies \[ \chi(G)\le\left\lfloor \frac{(2a-3/2)(t-1)-a+2}{2} \right\rfloor \] where $t\ge2$. These bounds reduce the leading denominator coefficient in the general order bound from $9/4$ to $2$ and the colouring coefficient for independence number two from $3/2$ to…

arxiv:2611.28474.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
arxiv:2611.28474.summary: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes.

arxiv:2611.28494.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
arxiv:2611.28494.summary: Let $\Gamma<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/\Gamma$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida.

arxiv:2611.28496.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
arxiv:2611.28496.summary: For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--R\"odl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $\sigma_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$.

arxiv:2611.28518.title: From two heptagrams to a 449-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
arxiv:2611.28518.summary: We construct a 5-chromatic unit-distance graph on 449 vertices. Previously, the smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph had 509 vertices. Our graph is a subgraph of a graph obtained by a simple greedy construction applied to a 14-vertex seed graph consisting of two heptagrams.
arxiv:2611.28518.authors: Marijn J. H. Heule, Benjamin Przybocki

arxiv:2611.28528.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
arxiv:2611.28528.summary: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry.
arxiv:2611.28528.authors: Heein Park (Automation Systems and Research Institute, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Hyeonyeong Jang (Automation Systems and Research Institute, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Alessandro Astolfi (Computer, Electrical and Mathematical Sciences and Engineering Division, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, Thuwal, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia), Hyungbo Shim (Automation Systems and Research Institute, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Jin Gyu Lee (Automation Systems and Research Institute, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

arxiv:2611.28533.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
arxiv:2611.28533.summary: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$.
arxiv:2611.28533.authors: Albert Cochrane, Todd Cochrane, Craig Spencer

arxiv:2611.28562.title: The Sch\"urmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
arxiv:2611.28562.summary: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Sch\"urmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.

arxiv:2611.28570.title: Geometrising discrete representations in \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\)
arxiv:2611.28570.summary: We prove the Deroin--Tholozan conjecture for discrete representations into \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\). More precisely, we give a complete characterisation of those representations of a closed surface group with discrete image that arise as holonomies of branched hyperbolic structures. The proof combines a factorisation theorem of Rong for maps between Seifert fibred spaces with a local surgery that allows one to reinsert pinched handles while preserving the prescribed holonomy.

arxiv:2611.28580.title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
arxiv:2611.28580.summary: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chv\'atal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture.

arxiv:2611.28587.title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
arxiv:2611.28587.summary: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes.
arxiv:2611.28587.authors: Zhicheng Tong, Yong Li, Xuefeng Zhao

arxiv:2611.28588.title: Spectral radii of connected graphs with prescribed maximum degree
arxiv:2611.28588.summary: For a real number $\alpha>0$ and a positive integer $r$, we give recursive characterizations of the existence of finite simple connected graphs $G$ with adjacency spectral radius $\rho(G)=\alpha$ and maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le r$ (or $=r$). Adding one vertex to a graph $F$ at a time to update the Schur-complement $q=\alpha-{\mathbf b}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}{\mathbf b}$, where $B=\alpha I-A(F)$ is positive definite and ${\mathbf b}$ is a nonzero $0$--$1$ that specifies the neighbours of $z$ in $F$. Realizability is characterized by admissible constructions with positive intermediate outputs $q$ and a final zero output.

arxiv:2611.28619.title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
arxiv:2611.28619.summary: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted.

arxiv:2611.28659.title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
arxiv:2611.28659.summary: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$. Groups with a cyclic subgroup of index two that are neither cyclic nor dihedral are not even $2$-Cayley regressions; consequently, a group with a cyclic subgroup of index two is a Cayley regression if and…
arxiv:2611.28659.authors: Yingbi Jiang, Pengfei Guo, Jin-Hua Xie

arxiv:2611.28661.title: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
arxiv:2611.28661.summary: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$.

arxiv:2611.28664.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
arxiv:2611.28664.summary: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$.

arxiv:2611.28672.title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
arxiv:2611.28672.summary: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic.

arxiv:2611.28681.title: Stably irrational algebraically elliptic Fano threefolds
arxiv:2611.28681.summary: We establish algebraic ellipticity in the sense of Gromov of a general hypersurface of bidegree $(2,2)$ in $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$. According to a theorem of B\"ohning and Graf von Bothmer, a very general such hypersurface is a stably irrational Fano threefold.

arxiv:2611.28703.title: On non-canonical maximum cliques in the block graphs of orthogonal arrays
arxiv:2611.28703.summary: In this note, we prove an Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado characterisation of maximum intersecting families of columns of certain orthogonal arrays. This solves a problem of Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher and implies that, in all orthogonal arrays OA$(m,(m-1)^2)$, every non-canonical maximum intersecting family of columns necessarily has the structure of an affine plane.
arxiv:2611.28703.authors: Tao Feng, Sergey Goryainov, Elena V. Konstantinova, Letian Zhang

arxiv:2611.28714.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
arxiv:2611.28714.summary: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.
arxiv:2611.28714.authors: K. S. Lapin, S. V. Lapin

arxiv:2611.28715.title: Arithmetic jet stacks
arxiv:2611.28715.summary: We construct a stack, which generalizes the notion of the arithmetic jet space functor constructed by Borger using the generalized Witt vector constructions. A priori we con- struct the jet space functor for prestacks, consequently showing that this functor preserves stacks. We then proceed to show the representability of the jet space functor applied to a representable morphism of stacks thereby showing that the jet space functor preserves algebraic and Deligne-Mumford Stacks.

arxiv:2611.28722.title: Tannakian Brill-Noether theory of nodal curves
arxiv:2611.28722.summary: Using the Tannakian categories arising from convolutions of perverse sheaves on semi-abelian varieties, we can associate to any subvariety of a semi-abelian variety a reductive group together with a representation. We compute these groups and representations for Brill-Noether varieties of all curves whose generalized Jacobian is semi-abelian, in particular for nodal curves. We also obtain new results on the dimension and non-degeneracy of these Brill-Noether varieties.

arxiv:2611.28724.title: Coordinate Ordering and Non-collinear Central Configurations
arxiv:2611.28724.summary: We establish a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations based on a special coordinate ordering of the bodies. Moreover, we identify a region in the plane that contains no non-collinear central configurations. This provides a way to exclude non-collinear central configurations that are nearly collinear.

arxiv:2611.28733.title: The inverse Erd\H{o}s--Fuchs problem for $k$-fold sums
arxiv:2611.28733.summary: For every fixed integer $k\ge 3$, we construct an infinite set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{h\le n}r_{kA}(h)=\Gamma(1+1/k)^k n+O_k(n^{(1-1/k)^2})$, where $r_{kA}(h)$ counts ordered representations of $h$ as a sum of $k$ elements of $A$, with repetitions allowed. This improves Dai and Pan's bound for a linear main term. In the paired random model used here, fluctuations of the stated order occur infinitely often almost surely.

arxiv:2611.28737.title: Integral abelianizations of higher spin Torelli subgroups
arxiv:2611.28737.summary: We determine the integral abelianizations of the Torelli subgroups preserving an $r$-spin structure for $r\geqslant2$ and genus $g\geqslant5$. Set $n=r/\gcd(r,2)$. For a surface with one boundary component, the free rank agrees with that of the Torelli group, and the torsion subgroup is the direct sum of the usual Birman--Craggs--Johnson $2$-torsion and $\mathbb{Z}/n^2\mathbb{Z}$.

arxiv:2611.28761.title: An Algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay
arxiv:2611.28761.summary: A 4-dimensional algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay over an arbitrary field is constructed. Furthermore, it is shown that every three-dimensional graded ASL domain is Cohen--Macaulay.

arxiv:2611.28767.title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
arxiv:2611.28767.summary: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra.

arxiv:2611.28776.title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
arxiv:2611.28776.summary: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let $S_n(q)$ be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. Levenshtein proved that $S_n(q)\le c_nq^n$, where $c_n=(1/n)\bigl((n-1)/n\bigr)^{n-1}$.

arxiv:2611.28785.title: The Seifert--van Kampen Theorem
arxiv:2611.28785.summary: The Seifert--van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space from an open cover by two path-connected subspaces, provided their intersection is path-connected. This article gives a self-contained account of the theorem, explains its universal-property formulation as a pushout in the category of groups, and derives several standard computations. Particular attention is paid to base points, the role of path-connectedness, and the passage from a topological decomposition to a group presentation.

arxiv:2611.28814.title: Inner derivations and automorphism groups of vertex operator algebras
arxiv:2611.28814.summary: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map $V_1\to\operatorname{Der}(V)$, $h\mapsto h_0$, is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra.

arxiv:2611.28832.title: Lagrangian Construction of the Enveloping Superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$
arxiv:2611.28832.summary: We give a Lagrangian construction of the enveloping superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$. More precisely, we realize the Schur superalgebra $S(m|n,r)$, the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$ on $(\mathbb Q^{m|n})^{\otimes r}$, via the top Borel--Moore homology of mixed Steinberg varieties. Their top-dimensional components are indexed by the admissible matrices of Du and Rui and meet a natural symplectic open subset in Lagrangian subvarieties.

arxiv:2611.28840.title: Congruences modulo powers of $2$ and $3$ for Lin's function $\text{PDO}_t(n)$
arxiv:2611.28840.summary: Let $\text{PDO}_t(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Confirming a conjecture of Singh and Barman (2025), Tang (2026) recently proved that $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{2m-1}n)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+1}}$ for all $m\geq1$ and $n\geq0$. Using elementary techniques, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{m+2}n)$, and we use them to determine $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ modulo one further power of $2$.

arxiv:2611.28843.title: The Dynamical Manin-Mumford Conjecture for automorphisms of H\'enon type
arxiv:2611.28843.summary: We prove the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture for polynomial automorphisms of the complex affine plane of dynamical degree $>1$ proposed by Dujardin and Favre. More precisely, we prove that an irreducible algebraic curve contains infinitely many periodic points of such an automorphism if and only if it is the fixed locus of a polynomial involution conjugating some iterate of the automorphism to its inverse.

arxiv:2611.28852.title: Torrelli's Question for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
arxiv:2611.28852.summary: Torrelli asked whether the class $[1/f]$ belongs to the intersection homology $\mathcal{D}$-module of a hypersurface if and only if $-1$ is a simple root of its local Bernstein-Sato polynomial. We prove this equivalence for isolated hypersurface germs with $2\le n\le 4$ variables, and we construct isolated counterexamples with $n$ variables for every $n\ge 5$. In fact a counterexample with $[1/f]\in\mathrm{IC}_D$ and $\mathrm{mult}_{s=-1}b_f(s)=r\ge 2$ always needs at least $r+3$ variables.

arxiv:2611.28885.title: Finite abelian groups acting on rationally connected threefolds III: Classification
arxiv:2611.28885.summary: We complete the classification of finite abelian groups that admit a faithful action on a rationally connected threefold. For a finite abelian group $G$ with invariant factors $1<d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_s$, put $c(G)=\sum_i(1-1/d_i)$. We prove that for $1\le n\le3$ such a group admits a faithful action on a rationally connected variety of dimension $n$ if and only if $c(G)\le n$.

arxiv:2611.28888.title: Three almost symmetric metatiles generate the Spectre tiling
arxiv:2611.28888.summary: We present a system of three `metatiles' for the Spectre aperiodic monotiling, named `D23'. These are similar in concept to the {\HTPF} system for the hat tiling: the metatiles have their own substitution system which can be iterated as many times as desired, and then the lowest-order metatiles can be converted into Spectre tiles. One of the three metatiles has order-2 rotational symmetry, and the other two are `almost symmetric' with orders 2 and 3 respectively, in the sense that although the region covered by the tile's $n$-times deflation is not exactly identical to its rotation, within their intersection, the proportion of non-matching tiles tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$.

arxiv:2611.28921.title: Filters as a localization of nets
arxiv:2611.28921.summary: Based on different notions of subnet in the literature, we define categories of nets and investigate their categorical relationships. We show that the category of proper filters with filter-preserving functions is, up to equivalence, a localization of four of these categories.
arxiv:2611.28921.authors: Germ\'an I. Gomero Ferrer, Renan M. Mezabarba

arxiv:2611.28938.title: Independent and end-faithful spanning trees in infinite graphs
arxiv:2611.28938.summary: Spanning trees rooted at the same vertex are independent if, for each vertex other than the root, the paths from the root to that vertex are pairwise distinct and internally vertex-disjoint. Zehavi and Itai conjectured that, for every positive integer $k$, every finite $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. We show that every $2$-connected graph, finite or infinite, has two independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex.

arxiv:2611.28952.title: Nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}
arxiv:2611.28952.summary: We determine all nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The problem reduces to describing the set $\cN_n$ of pairs $(d,b)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^{n-1}$ for which the tridiagonal matrices with diagonal $d$ and with products $b_k$ of opposite off-diagonal entries have characteristic polynomial $\lambda^n$. We show that $\cN_n$ is obtained from $\cN_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ by one of two explicit ``folding'' operations, according to the parity of $n$.

arxiv:2611.28955.title: The Z[tau]-foam: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam as arithmetic in the icosahedral module
arxiv:2611.28955.summary: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam is a substitution that fills the regular dodecahedron with dodecahedral bubbles of sizes tau^{-k}, tau=(1+sqrt(5))/2, using the seven kinds of cells into which the twelve planes of its stellation cut it. We rewrite it as exact arithmetic in one Z[tau]-module of rank three, the span M of the six five-fold axes, on which the icosahedral group acts by 120 matrices in GL(3,Z[tau]). A placed inflated copy of a cell is a union of cells iff its facet levels lie in {+-1,+-tau^3} and it lies in the dodecahedron.
arxiv:2611.28955.authors: Miguel E. P\'erez Ibarra, Jaziel Flores Rodr\'iguez

arxiv:2611.28956.title: Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
arxiv:2611.28956.summary: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$.
arxiv:2611.28956.authors: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, S\"{u}meyra Sakall{\i}, Sai-Kee Yeung

arxiv:2611.28984.title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
arxiv:2611.28984.summary: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.

arxiv:2611.29033.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
arxiv:2611.29033.summary: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$
arxiv:2611.29033.authors: Raisa V. Serova, Anastasia V. Vikulova

arxiv:2611.29056.title: Note on OpenAI's proof of the base of Lagrangian fibrations
arxiv:2611.29056.summary: OpenAI proved that every Lagrangian fibration of a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold has a base $\mathbb P^n$. This expository note summarizes the last section of their paper.

arxiv:2611.29063.title: Strong holonomicity of functions on curves
arxiv:2611.29063.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth affine irreducible curve over $\mathbb C$, and let ${\mathcal D} = {\mathcal D} (X)$ be the ring of global differential operators on $X$. To every nonzero operator $L \in {\mathcal D} $ we attach a non-negative integer $n(L)$, the holonomicity index of $L$, which is defined in an elementary way, by counting solutions of $L$ in the truncated local rings at the singular points of $L$. Our main theorem shows that $n(L)$ coincides with the Calogero--Moser index of the Weyl closure ${\rm cl}(L) = {\mathcal D}(K) \cap {\mathcal D} $ of $L$, i.e. with the integer $n$ labelling the Calogero--Moser space $ {\mathcal C}_n(X,\mathcal{I})$ that contains the isomorphism class of the…

arxiv:2611.29073.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature
arxiv:2611.29073.summary: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof.

arxiv:2611.29077.title: Note on the extendability problem for invariant quasimorphisms for mapping class groups
arxiv:2611.29077.summary: In this note, we study the extendability problem of invariant quasimorphisms for short exact sequences related to mapping class groups of surfaces, possibly with one boundary component or one marked point. Using a recent result of Blatz, we prove that if the genus is at least two, then every homogeneous quasimorphism on the Torelli group that is invariant by the conjugation action by the mapping class group is uniquely extendable to the whole mapping class group. Contrastingly, for the surface with one marked point whose genus is at least three, we show the existence of a homogeneous Torelli-group-invariant quasimorphism on the Johnson kernel that is not extendable.
arxiv:2611.29077.authors: Morimichi Kawasaki, Mitsuaki Kimura, Shuhei Maruyama, Takahiro Matsushita, Masato Mimura

arxiv:2611.29088.title: On rescuing diverging algorithms: crossing infinity in continuous Newton methods via a self-similarity detection framework
arxiv:2611.29088.summary: We address the solution of systems of nonlinear algebraic equations via continuous Newton methods; these methods reformulate the discrete Newton update as an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) whose stationary points correspond to the desired roots. A fundamental challenge arises when the Jacobian of these ODEs becomes singular along the solution trajectory, inducing blow-up in the vector field --or in the state itself-- and causing the numerical integration to break down before reaching the desired root. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a directional self-similar blow-up detection and crossing procedure, wrapped around an adaptive step-size…
arxiv:2611.29088.authors: Gianluca Fabiani, Ralf Hannemann-Tam\'as, Alexander Mitsos, Jonathan D. Hauenstein, Constantinos Siettos, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis

arxiv:2611.29111.title: When do local bounds permit optimal edge-colorings?
arxiv:2611.29111.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, maximum multiplicity $\mu(G)$, and chromatic index $\chi'(G)$. A proper edge-coloring is locally bounded if each edge $e$ in $G$ with endvertices $u$ and $v$ is assigned a color at most $\max\{d_G(u)+\mu_G(u),d_G(v)+\mu_G(v)\}$, where $d_G(w)$ and $\mu_G(w)$ respectively denote the degree of $w$ and the maximum multiplicity of an edge incident with $w$. The well-known Vizing's theorem guarantees a proper edge-coloring with at most $\Delta(G)+\mu(G)$ colors.

arxiv:2611.29126.title: Contact rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants
arxiv:2611.29126.summary: We study $C^0$-rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants on closed contact manifolds. We prove that Poisson commutation is closed under uniform convergence, establish weak rigidity for pairs without common zeros, and obtain lower semicontinuity under quantitative control of Reeb derivatives. A three-dimensional counterexample shows that unrestricted weak rigidity fails.

arxiv:2611.29136.title: On the General Position Number of Cacti
arxiv:2611.29136.summary: Given a graph G=(V,E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges, a subset of vertices $S \subseteq V$ is called a General Position Set (GPS) if no shortest path on G between any two vertices in S contains another vertex from S. The General Position Number (GPN) of a graph G is the maximum size of a GPS in G. The decision version of this problem, determining whether the GPN of a graph G is at least a given integer i, is known as the General Position Problem (GPP).
arxiv:2611.29136.authors: Toshihiko Kimura, Yonghwan Kim, Yoshiaki Katayama

arxiv:2611.29157.title: Infinitely many spectral gaps for Anderson--Bernoulli operators with sparse periodic backgrounds
arxiv:2611.29157.summary: We consider discrete Anderson--Bernoulli operators with a periodic background. At a single coupling, every minimal period of at least three admits a background with at most four nonzero sites per period whose almost sure spectrum has infinitely many gaps. We give two constructions.

arxiv:2611.29159.title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
arxiv:2611.29159.summary: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions.
arxiv:2611.29159.authors: Xing Liang, Lei Zhang, Niansen Zhang

arxiv:2611.29161.title: Rough structure. I. Exclusion among series-parallel graphs
arxiv:2611.29161.summary: This is the first in a series of papers about rough structure theorems: graph properties that are implied by the exclusion of some graph as a minor, and imply the exclusion of some larger graph of the same type. Here we look at the structure of the series-parallel graphs that do not contain a given series-parallel graph as a minor. We prove that for every series-parallel graph $H$, there exists $m$ such that every simple two-connected series-parallel graph that does not contain $H$ as a minor admits a tree-decomposition of height at most $m$, where each "torso" is either an outerplanar graph or a planar dual of one.
arxiv:2611.29161.authors: Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, Alex Divoux, Paul Seymour, Liana Yepremyan

arxiv:2611.29166.title: Improved Lower Bound on the Hadwiger-Debrunner Numbers
arxiv:2611.29166.summary: The celebrated $(p,q)$-theorem of Alon and Kleitman asserts that for any $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and any $p \geq q \geq d+1$, every family of convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in which among any $p$ sets, some $q$ intersect, can be pierced by $c(p,q,d)$ points. The minimum numbers $c(p,q,d)$ are called the Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers and denoted $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q)$ and determining them is a longstanding open problem. We prove that for any $d \geq 2$, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,d+1) \geq p^{d-o(1)}$, and more generally, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q) \geq p^{\frac{q-1}{q-d}-o(1)}$.

arxiv:2611.29175.title: Is every knot a three-way deadlock? Counterexamples and a universality conjecture for the segment number
arxiv:2611.29175.summary: The segment number $s(K)$ of a knot $K$ is the minimal number of arcs into which a diagram of $K$ can be cut so that, for every pair of arcs, one of them passes over the other at all of their common crossings. Every non-trivial knot satisfies $s(K)\ge 3$. In the paper introducing this invariant it was conjectured that the bridge number satisfies $b(K)\le s(K)$, and the torus knot $5_1$ was proposed as a candidate for a knot with $s(K)=4$.

arxiv:2611.29192.title: Bruhat Shellings of the Quasisymmetric Flag Moment Complex
arxiv:2611.29192.summary: The quasisymmetric flag variety gives rise to a regular cell complex whose maximal cells are cubes indexed by fully supported noncrossing partitions. Two maximal cubes can meet along several faces. We describe each cube using the block arcs and parent connectors of its indexing partition, and determine its intersection with the union of the preceding cubes in Bruhat order.

arxiv:2611.29198.title: Quaternary games with infinite mis\`ere quotients
arxiv:2611.29198.summary: We study the four wild quaternary games left open by the earlier work of Plambeck and Siegel. For \texttt{0.3102} we discover a special regularity of its two--heap case, give a complete solution of the two--heap case, and deduce from it that its mis\`ere quotient is infinite. For \texttt{0.3122} and \texttt{0.3123} we rigorously prove, by slice--wise algebraic periodicity and hierarchical induction (computer--assisted), that their mis\`ere quotients are infinite.

arxiv:2611.29233.title: Unknotting number is strictly subadditive for the trefoil
arxiv:2611.29233.summary: A trefoil and a certain fourteen-crossing knot take four crossing changes to unknot separately and at most three together. We extend this example to infinitely many prime partners and show that the same partners give a saving for every nontrivial positive braid knot and, up to mirror, every nontrivial torus knot.
arxiv:2611.29233.authors: Anne Dranowski, Yura Kabkov, Daniel Tubbenhauer

arxiv:2611.29234.title: M\"obius Fusion Algebra
arxiv:2611.29234.summary: Given a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with an anti-monoidal involution $\mathsf{P}$, we define a generally non-commutative algebra from this data, which we call the M\"obius fusion algebra $\mathfrak{M}$ of $(\mathcal{C},\mathsf{P})$, in terms of ribbon graphs drawn on the M\"obius band, where the orientation-reversal of the M\"obius band acts on the graphs by $\mathsf{P}$. We show that this algebra is semisimple, and give a formula for the dimensions of its simple modules, in terms of the modular $S$-matrix of $\mathcal{C}$ and a certain set of quantities extracted from the action of $\mathsf{P}$. This formula is expected to play the role of a non-orientable analogue…

arxiv:2611.29239.title: A fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined, although both threefold subbrackets contain zero
arxiv:2611.29239.summary:
We give an explicit example, in the stable homotopy groups of spheres, of a fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined although both of its threefold subbrackets contain zero. Namely, $0\in\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2angle$ and $0\in\langle 2,\eta^2,
uangle$, but $\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2,
uangle$ has no defining system in the sense of Kochman. This answers a question of Isaksen.

arxiv:2611.29297.title: The local lifting conjecture for dihedral groups of order $2p^n$
arxiv:2611.29297.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $D_{p^n}$ denote the dihedral group of order $2p^n$. A local $D_{p^n}$-action is a faithful action of $D_{p^n}$ on the formal power series ring $k[[z]]$ by continuous $k$-automorphisms. The strong Oort conjecture of Chinburg, Guralnick and Harbater predicts that every such action lifts to characteristic zero.

arxiv:2611.29300.title: Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series
arxiv:2611.29300.summary: We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.

arxiv:2611.29304.title: Optimal odd unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$ through $59$
arxiv:2611.29304.summary: It is shown that the largest minimum norm among unimodular lattices is $4$ in dimension $49$ and $5$ in dimensions $50$, $51$, $57$ and $58$. We also study the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in every dimension from $49$ through $59$. In dimensions $50$, $51$ and $57$, the first known examples of unimodular lattices with minimum norm $5$ are obtained from self-dual codes by Construction~A.

arxiv:2611.29308.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
arxiv:2611.29308.summary: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture.

arxiv:2611.29332.title: Odd Chromatic Number of Graph Classes: Bounds and Structural Results
arxiv:2611.29332.summary: A proper coloring of a graph $G$ is called an \emph{odd coloring} if, for every non-isolated vertex $v\in V(G)$, there exists a color that occurs an odd number of times in the open neighborhood of $v$. For a graph $G$, the minimum number of colors required for such a coloring is called the {\em odd chromatic number}, denoted by $\chi_{o}(G)$. The odd chromatic number has been well-studied from both combinatorial and algorithmic perspectives, and several bounds on $\chi_o(G)$ are known.
arxiv:2611.29332.authors: Musarof Hossain, Sandeep Kumar, Vikash Tripathi, Mirza Galib Anwarul Husain Baig

arxiv:2611.29337.title: Unstable Solidification
arxiv:2611.29337.summary: We construct a solidification functor $\LH$ on condensed anima by localizing at the maps inverted by solid integral chains. A pointed connected nilpotent condensed anima is $\Hsol$-local precisely when its fundamental group admits a finite central series with solid abelian factors and its higher homotopy groups are solid. For simply connected condensed anima, we construct a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence \[ E^2_{p,q}=L_ps(\pi_qX)\Longrightarrow\pi_{p+q}\LH X \] where $L_ps$ denotes the $p$-th derived functor of the abelian solidification.

arxiv:2611.29344.title: A new upper bound for the Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres conjecture
arxiv:2611.29344.summary: Let $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ denote the smallest integer such that every set of $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ points in the plane in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. In 1935, Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres conjectured that $\mathrm{ES}(n)=2^{n-2}+1$, and in 1960, they established the corresponding lower bound. A breakthrough on the upper bound was achieved by Suk in 2017, who proved that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{2/3}\log n)}.
arxiv:2611.29344.authors: Yifan Hu, Guokuan Shao, Guozhen Shen

arxiv:2611.29387.title: A transitive $C^{1+\alpha}$ surface diffeomorphism with positive entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy
arxiv:2611.29387.summary: Let $0<\alpha\le 1$. On a closed surface, every topologically transitive $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism with positive topological entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy.

arxiv:2611.29392.title: Admissible balanced pairs over cleft extensions
arxiv:2611.29392.summary: Let $(B, A, i, e, l)$ be a cleft extension of abelian categories such that $e$ has a right adjoint $r$. It is proved that $(C, D)$ is an admissible balanced pair in $B$ if and only if $(\operatorname{add}(lC), \operatorname{add}(rD))$ is an admissible balanced pair in $A$. When the extension is directed with respect to a finite product decomposition of $B$, the lifting of complete hereditary cotorsion pairs $(C, Y)$ and $(X, D)$ to $A$ is characterized by the vanishing of first derived functors.
arxiv:2611.29392.authors: Junpeng Ren, Zheng-Gang Wu, Mengzhen Zhu

arxiv:2611.29397.title: Extremal adjacency and distance spectral radii of graph powers
arxiv:2611.29397.summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let $G^k$ denote its $k$-th power. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, \[ \rho(G^k)\geq \rho(P_n^k) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \rho_D(G^k)\leq \rho_D(P_n^k), \] where $P_n$ is the path of order $n$, and $\rho$ and $\rho_D$ are the adjacency and distance spectral radii, respectively. If $n\geq k+2$, equality in either inequality holds precisely when $G\cong P_n$.
arxiv:2611.29397.authors: Joyentanuj Das, Anto Jerrin Ashni R, Sangeetha C

arxiv:2611.29404.title: Prescribed matrix size for UHF Brauer classes on suspensions
arxiv:2611.29404.summary: Let \(Y\) be a connected finite CW complex, \(L=M_{l^\infty}\) for \(l\geq2\), and \(k\) a positive integer coprime to \(l\). Stable \(L\)-twists on \(\Sigma Y\) have normalized clutching invariants \(1+x\) in \(K^0(Y)[1/l]\). We prove that such a twist is the stabilization of a unital \(M_k(L)\)-bundle exactly when \(kx=0\) additively.

arxiv:2611.29406.title: Regularity of invariant measures of solutions for fractional stochastic partial differential equations with memory and nonlinear noise
arxiv:2611.29406.summary: We are concerned with stochastic fractional partial differential equations involving memory and nonlinear multiplicative noise. Based on the well-known Dafermos method, a suitable variable defined by the integrated past history is introduced.
