This transformation not only overcomes the non-Markovianity of the original problem which prevents us from analyzing invariant measures for the associated Markov semigroup, but also facilitates the analysis of the well-posedness together with the Faedo-Galerkin approximations and Minty's technique.
arxiv:2611.29406.authors: Ran Li, Jiaohui Xu, Dingshi Li, Tomas Caraballo

arxiv:2611.29409.title: The mean orders of even and odd permutations
arxiv:2611.29409.summary: We compare the sums of the orders of the even and odd permutations of a given degree. For all large degrees the odd permutations have the larger sum. The excess equals the sum of orders of the permutations of odd order up to a relative error decaying faster than any power of the degree.

arxiv:2611.29412.title: Principal subspaces of affine vertex algebras at admissible levels
arxiv:2611.29412.summary: We classify generic principal subspaces of admissible affine vertex algebras for all simple Lie algebras. The nongeneric cases occur precisely at denominator two in types $B,C,F_4$ and at denominator three in type $G_2$. The proof uses geometry of nilpotent orbits combined with positive root null vectors.

arxiv:2611.29420.title: Reconstruction and geometry of $4\times4$ quantum Sudoku
arxiv:2611.29420.summary: We study the reconstruction and geometry of $4 \times 4$ quantum Sudoku, viewed as arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks decompose the identity. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for two prescribed opposite blocks to admit a completion, prove its uniqueness, and obtain explicit reconstruction formulas, also expressed in the language of quantum logic. The sixteen overlaps between these blocks determine the unitary equivalence class of the grid, while the number of nonzero overlaps equals its cardinality.
arxiv:2611.29420.authors: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Paolo Facchi, Roberto La Scala, Marilena Ligab\`o, Karol \.Zyczkowski

arxiv:2611.29433.title: Decomposition of completeness and the universality of the Daniell extension
arxiv:2611.29433.summary: An integration system is a triple $(X,L,I)$: a set $X$, a Riesz subspace $L$ of $\mathbb{R}^X$, and a continuous positive linear functional $I$ on $L$. We introduce the category Int whose morphisms are pullbacks along maps of the base spaces. The main result is that the Daniell extension defines a functor from Int to DInt and is left adjoint to the inclusion of the full subcategory DInt of Daniell closed systems, those with $L^1=L$, usually called complete.

arxiv:2611.29437.title: Bounds on periods of curves for split rational maps
arxiv:2611.29437.summary: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be fixed complex rational maps of degree at least two, and let $(A_1,A_2)$ denote the endomorphism of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(A_1(x),A_2(y))$. We show that the periods of irreducible $(A_1,A_2)$-periodic curves with dominant coordinate projections are bounded, unless $A_1$ and $A_2$ belong to the exceptional power, Chebyshev, or Latt\`es families. We also extend this result to periodic subvarieties for endomorphisms of $(\mathbb P^1)^m$.

arxiv:2611.29448.title: On the 0-Rotatability of Regular Spider Trees of Leg Length 4
arxiv:2611.29448.summary: A tree $T$ on $q$ edges is said to be $0$-rotatable if for every vertex $v \in V(T)$, there exists a graceful labeling $f : V(T) \to \{0, 1, \dots, q\}$ such that $f(v) = 0$. Rofa proved that all regular (symmetric) spider trees with leg length at most $3$ are $0$-rotatable and conjectured that the property holds for every leg length. In this note, we settle the first open case of this conjecture by proving that every regular spider tree $T(k, 4)$ with $k \ge 1$ legs of length $4$ is $0$-rotatable.

arxiv:2611.29486.title: An asymptotic form of Thomasse's directed path conjecture
arxiv:2611.29486.summary: Thomass\'e conjectured that every oriented graph of minimum out-degree $d$ contains a directed path of length $2d$. We resolve this conjecture asymptotically by proving that every such graph contains a directed path of length at least $2d-O(d\log\log d/\log d)$.
arxiv:2611.29486.authors: Xinyao Ren, Yisai Xue, Ai Yang

arxiv:2611.29490.title: Combinatorics of equivariant blowups of spherical varieties
arxiv:2611.29490.summary: We explicitly describe the colored fan of the blowup of a smooth spherical variety $X$ along a smooth irreducible $G$-stable subvariety $Y$. The answer is expressed in terms of the colored cone of $Y$ and the localization of the valuation cone at $Y$, and generalizes the star subdivision of fans of toric varieties. We also consider several examples illustrating the main result.

arxiv:2611.29504.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graphs
arxiv:2611.29504.summary: A connected graph of order at least $2k+2$ is {\em $k$-extendable} if it has a matching of size $k$ and every such matching extends to a perfect matching. In particular, a 1-extendable graph is also called a {\em matching covered graph}. A $k$-extendable graph $G$ is {\em minimal} if $G-e$ is not $k$-extendable for every $e\in E(G)$.

arxiv:2611.29505.title: Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
arxiv:2611.29505.summary: We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component.
arxiv:2611.29505.authors: Satoshi Naito, Khanh Nguyen Duc, Daisuke Sagaki

arxiv:2611.29517.title: The Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity
arxiv:2611.29517.summary: In their 2007 paper on the log-convexity of combinatorial sequences, Liu and Wang conjectured that the Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity. We completely solve their conjecture by showing that this transformation preserves strong $q$-log-convexity. More generally, we provide a sufficient condition for a linear transformation, defined by a triangular array satisfying a certain three-term recurrence relation, to preserve strong $q$-log-convexity.
arxiv:2611.29517.authors: Huihua Gao, Xin-Bei Liu, Weilin Wang

arxiv:2611.29524.title: Eight limit cycles in a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system
arxiv:2611.29524.summary: Gyllenberg and Yan conjectured that a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system can have at least five limit cycles. We prove the conjecture by constructing a strictly competitive system in which eight distinct limit cycles coexist near a single positive equilibrium. For each $m=5,6,7,8$, we construct a weak focus of order $m$ and identify parameter directions on the Hopf hypersurface that allow us to vary the first $m-1$ focus quantities independently.
arxiv:2611.29524.authors: Haoyu Albert Wang, Yuxiu Shao, Wei P. Dai

arxiv:2611.29530.title: Nonvanishing of mean indices and stability of symmetric closed characteristics on symmetric star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^4$
arxiv:2611.29530.authors: Zhenxiong Li, Hui Liu, Zhoukai Xu

arxiv:2611.29535.title: A Finiteness Result for Commuting Squares and Quantitative Ocneanu Rigidity
arxiv:2611.29535.summary: We introduce the spanning relative commutant condition (SRC) for nondegenerate commuting squares of matrix algebras. The condition requires that the second relative commutant span the next algebra in the lower row of the basic construction as a right module over the preceding algebra. We prove that if a sequence of SRC squares with fixed tracial inclusion data converges, then all but finitely many terms are isomorphic to the limit square.

arxiv:2611.29544.title: Comparing the $K$-theory of two versions of $\ell^p$-Roe algebras
arxiv:2611.29544.summary: We prove that for any locally finite metric space $X$ and $1<p<\infty$, the canonical inclusion from the $\ell^p$-Roe algebra with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N)$ into that with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N;\ell^2(\mathbb N))$ identifies the former with a full multiplier corner of the latter. Consequently, the inclusion induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory, answering a question of Wang, Xie, Yu, and Zhu. Moreover, at the endpoint $p=1$, we show that the two corresponding Roe algebras are not Morita equivalent whenever $X$ is infinite.
arxiv:2611.29544.authors: Liang Guo, Zheng Luo, Qin Wang

arxiv:2611.29561.title: High order tangencies, paratangencies, and universal dynamics
arxiv:2611.29561.summary: Our research focuses on studying the dynamics in the Newhouse domain $\mathcal N(L)$ -- open regions in the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of a $d$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M^d$ ($r=1,\ldots,\infty,\omega$ and $d\ge 2$) where homoclinic tangencies to a saddle periodic orbit $L$ are persistent. We prove that diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-1 homoclinic tangencies of all orders are dense in such regions. If $L$ is a bi-focus, we reveal novel bifurcations in $\mathcal N(L)$ showing density of diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-2 homoclinic tangencies of all orders.

arxiv:2611.29586.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
arxiv:2611.29586.summary: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincar\'e-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates.

arxiv:2611.29599.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-K\"ahler varieties, III
arxiv:2611.29599.summary: The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-K\"ahler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives.
arxiv:2611.29599.authors: Lie Fu, Robert Laterveer, Carl Mazzanti, Charles Vial

arxiv:2611.29608.title: Rotationa Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
arxiv:2611.29608.summary: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers.
arxiv:2611.29608.authors: Maciej J. Capi\'nski, Sof\'ia Llavayol, Alejandro Passeggi

arxiv:2611.29611.title: Subshifts of finite type and parameter density for intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations
arxiv:2611.29611.summary: We study the subshifts \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) associated with the intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations \(x\mapsto-\beta x+\alpha\pmod1\), where \((\beta,\alpha)\in\Delta_-:=\{(b,a):1<b<2,\ b-1<a<1\}\). We prove that $\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}$ is of finite type if and only if both endpoints of \([0,1]\) reach the discontinuity \(c_{\beta,\alpha}=\alpha/\beta\). We also prove that the set of parameters \((\beta,\alpha)\) for which \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) is a subshift of finite type is dense in \(\Delta_-\).

arxiv:2611.29621.title: Fast growth of periodic orbits, translated points and short Floer bars for contactomorphisms
arxiv:2611.29621.summary: We establish arbitrarily fast growth of distinct periodic orbits and geometrically distinct translated points for contactomorphisms of the unit cotangent bundle of a closed hyperbolic surface. The conclusions hold on residual subsets of a nonempty $C^1$-open set and follow from Chaidez's contact blender and localized contact perturbations. For a specified analytically admissible normalized Rabinowitz Floer family on a closed contact manifold with Liouville filling, we bound fixed-window barcode entropy by topological entropy.

arxiv:2611.29644.title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
arxiv:2611.29644.summary: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph.

arxiv:2611.29669.title: Universal Implications Among $k$-Prime Graph Labelings
arxiv:2611.29669.summary: For $k\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the class of graphs admitting a bijective labeling by consecutive integers beginning at $k$, with coprime labels at adjacent vertices. We determine all universal inclusions between distinct such classes: $\mathcal P_i\subseteq\mathcal P_j$ holds for $i\ne j$ if and only if $(i,j)=(2,1)$ or $(3,1)$. In particular, the classes are pairwise distinct.

arxiv:2611.29683.title: Termination of the Kahler MMP with scaling
arxiv:2611.29683.summary: In this article, we prove termination of klt flips with scaling for strongly \(\mathbb Q\)-factorial compact Kahler klt pairs $(X,B)$ with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary. In particular, compact Kahler klt pairs with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary have minimal models when \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective, and admit Mori fibre space models otherwise.

arxiv:2611.29686.title: Distinct Distances under Well-behaved Norms
arxiv:2611.29686.summary: We improve our understanding of the Erdos' distinct distances problem under non-Euclidean norms, in two ways: (i) For norms that are definable in an o-minimal structure and whose non-line bisectors have a finite intersection, we obtain a lower bound of \(\Omega(n^{5/6})\) for the minimum number of distinct distances. In particular, this improves the current best bound of \(\Omega(n^{4/5})\) for all \(\ell_{p}\) norms with non-integer \(p > 1\). (ii) We derive the stronger bound \(\Omega(n^{6/7-\epsilon})\) under all semi-algebraic smooth norms.

arxiv:2611.29688.title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
arxiv:2611.29688.summary: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education.
arxiv:2611.29688.authors: Luca Meacci, Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no

arxiv:2611.29705.title: Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
arxiv:2611.29705.summary: Let $\varphi_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $\varphi_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $\varphi_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper.

arxiv:2611.29713.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
arxiv:2611.29713.summary: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb…

arxiv:2611.29718.title: Unary maps are restrictions of linear maps and $k$-ary maps are restrictions of homogeneous maps
arxiv:2611.29718.summary: We study maps on a finite set $S$ under renaming elements of $S$ and extending $S$. We show that every unary map is linear and every $k$-ary map is homogeneous with respect to such renamings and embeddings.

arxiv:2611.29726.title: Counting Eulerian Orientations in Regular Graphs
arxiv:2611.29726.summary: Let $G$ be a pseudograph, and let $\varepsilon(G)$ denote the number of Eulerian orientations of $G$. Lieb and Wu, and later Schrijver, showed that if $G$ has degree sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$, where each $d_i$ is a positive even integer, then \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \prod_{i = 1}^n 2^{-d_i/2} \binom{d_i}{d_i/2}.\] Schrijver conjectured that for simple $d$-regular graphs, $\varepsilon(G)\leq\varepsilon(K_{d+1})^{n/(d+1)}$, with equality attained by disjoint unions of cliques of order $d+1$. In this paper, we prove a multigraph bound that implies the known case $d=4$, and we also improve Schrijver's lower bound for $d$-regular graphs, using an inductive relation between $\varepsilon(G)$…
arxiv:2611.29726.authors: Srinjoy Srimani, Jacques Verstraete, Jason Yang

arxiv:2611.29743.title: On the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibrium in planar restricted $(n+1)$-body problem
arxiv:2611.29743.summary: In this paper, we consider the restricted $(n+1)$-body problems, where the $n$ primaries forming an a homographic motion generated by the planar central configuration, and the massless particle is attracted by this $n$ primaries. We are interested in the linear stability of the elliptic relative equilibria of the massless particle under the pulsating coordinates. The main contribution of this paper first lies in the investigation of a general $(\alpha,\beta)$-system (1.7).

arxiv:2611.29746.title: The probability that two random generalized derangements have the same number of cycles
arxiv:2611.29746.summary: Using singularity analysis, we show that the probability that two independently and uniformly selected generalized derangements of size $n$ have the same number of cycles is asymptotically the same as the corresponding probability for unrestricted permutations, namely, $\sim \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi\log n}}\;.$

arxiv:2611.29751.title: A compact nonformal manifold with holonomy Spin(7)
arxiv:2611.29751.summary: We construct a compact simply connected eight-manifold with holonomy Spin(7) and a triple Massey product of degrees $(3,2,2)$ that does not contain zero. The manifold is a resolution of a flat orbifold. Joyce's gluing theorem gives it a torsion-free Spin(7) structure.

arxiv:2611.29763.title: Hodge cycles of Klein hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.29763.summary: We study the space of Hodge cycles on Klein varieties. Relating it to the Hodge characters in a covering Fermat variety, we decompose the space of Hodge characters into a part generated by classes of rational subvarieties, and a non-trivial part which we call exceptional. Using Dirichlet characters we show that the exceptional part is always finite.

arxiv:2611.29782.title: Commutative bishuffle algebras and Pattern Avoidance
arxiv:2611.29782.summary: This paper introduces the notion of a commutative bishuffle algebra, that linearizes classical pattern avoidance. The free commutative bishuffle algebra on one generator has a basis of permutations, divisibility of monomials is pattern containment, and the classes of permutations avoiding given patterns are the monomial bases of its quotients by monomial ideals. This free algebra is not Noetherian, but we show that its quotient by the antisymmetrizer $e_k$ is Noetherian for every $k$, and we conjecture that the same holds for its quotient by any nonzero ideal stable under the symmetric groups, in analogy with the Specht problem.

arxiv:2611.29786.title: Parity-safe digraphs with countably many ends are kernel-perfect
arxiv:2611.29786.summary: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set that every other vertex points into, and a digraph is kernel-perfect if every induced subgraph has a kernel. A digraph without odd cycles in which no ray contains infinitely many vertices that each send an infinite fan of disjoint paths to that ray is safe. The conjecture that every safe digraph is kernel-perfect was proved earlier for digraphs with finitely many ends.

arxiv:2611.29803.title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
arxiv:2611.29803.summary: In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere. Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1.

arxiv:2611.29812.title: Form of Words in Free Products with scl 1/12
arxiv:2611.29812.summary: Let $G = *_\lambda G_\lambda$ be a free product of groups and let $g\in G$ be any element not conjugate into any free factor and not conjugate to its inverse. Then $\mathrm{scl}(g) \ge \frac{1}{12}$ and $\mathrm{scl}(g) = \frac{1}{12}$ if and only if $g$ is a product of an element of order $2$ and an element of order $3$. In particular, this classifies all elements in $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{scl}_G(g) = \frac{1}{12}$.

arxiv:2611.29819.title: General bounds for metric dimension of diameter-two graphs with applications
arxiv:2611.29819.summary: We study the metric dimension of several classes of graphs with diameter two. First, we establish a general lower bound for the metric dimension of graphs with diameter two in terms of their order and maximum degree. We then apply our results to Grassmann graphs, Moore graphs, and bilinear forms graphs.

arxiv:2611.29825.title: Twisted K-Theory and Reduced Norms over Global and Higher Local Fields
arxiv:2611.29825.summary: We prove the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture concerning reduced norms over both global and local fields. Furthermore, in both settings, we construct maps between truncated K-theory spectra that induce the reduced norms in degrees 1 and 2, and show that these maps are equivalences over local fields. Over global fields, we establish finiteness properties of their fibers and give a detailed description of their structure.

arxiv:2611.29848.title: Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension
arxiv:2611.29848.summary: The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e.

arxiv:2611.29860.title: Cylindrical dimers and monomial immanants
arxiv:2611.29860.summary: For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them.

arxiv:2611.29862.title: Exceptional Rays of Invariant Processes on Trees
arxiv:2611.29862.summary: Let $A$ be an ergodic, non-constant random process on the $d$-regular tree $T_d$, with marginal distribution $X$. We prove that there always exist "exceptional" rays, whose asymptotic means are at least $\mathbb{E}(X)+\delta$; furthermore, for edge processes, $\delta > 0$ can be taken to depend only on the law of $X$. We compare different definitions of "maximal asymptotic means", relating them to different notions of speed of tree-indexed random walks.

arxiv:2611.29864.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
arxiv:2611.29864.summary: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected.

arxiv:2611.29878.title: Explicit Response Formulae and Request Problem for Smooth Expanding Endomorphisms
arxiv:2611.29878.summary: In this paper, we investigate the higher order differentiability of physical measures, in the category of smooth expanding endomorphisms of compact manifolds, and we establish the explicit response formulae of any order. The proof is based on the elegant Keller-Liverani-Gou\"ezel perturbation theory of transfer operators. Furthermore, we provide the solutions to the high order request problem, which is regarded as the inverse problem to response formulae, that is, we make perturbations to realize prescribed responses up to any finite order, and we establish the existence of minimizers for a relaxed optimization problem associated with suitable cost functionals.
arxiv:2611.29878.authors: Jianyu Chen, Na Zhang, Yufeng Zhang

arxiv:2611.29890.title: Parking Functions inspired by board games
arxiv:2611.29890.summary: We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park.
arxiv:2611.29890.authors: Alexander Clifton, Pamela E. Harris, Maryam Khaqan

arxiv:2611.29898.title: Frobenius $2$-algebras and $R$-matrices
arxiv:2611.29898.summary: In this paper, introducing Frobenius $2$-algebras, which are categorical generalizations of Frobenius algebras, we show that every Frobenius $2$-algebra determines an $R$-matrix satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation in the monoidal category of endomorphisms of its underlying object. Moreover, we illustrate this construction through three examples: a pair of objects in a braided monoidal category, a Hopf algebra with invertible antipode, and representations of the Heisenberg double of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. In particular, in the third example, we recover Kashaev's construction of the universal $R$-matrix.

arxiv:2611.29929.title: Local Limits and Structures of Nearest-Predecessor Random Graphs
arxiv:2611.29929.summary: We study the two-sided nearest-predecessor graph on $[n]$, where vertices arrive in a uniformly random order and each new vertex connects to its nearest earlier vertex on each side. We construct an infinite graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ from i.i.d. continuous insertion times and prove quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence to it almost surely. The limit is almost surely one-ended and recurrent.

arxiv:2611.29949.title: Levi Dynamics and Largest Domains of Discontinuity on Flag Manifolds
arxiv:2611.29949.summary: Divergent sequences in a semisimple Lie group have a bounded Levi part that is invisible to Cartan projections and limit flags. We show that this Levi part is a genuine dynamical invariant and determines much of the large-scale behaviour of discrete groups on flag manifolds. For every real flag manifold, we compute the complete moving-source destination relation of a divergent sequence, including the Levi contribution.
arxiv:2611.29949.authors: \'Angel Cano, Marlon M. L\'opez-Flores, Jos\'e Seade, Andrew Shaw

arxiv:2611.29951.title: From Low-Dimensional Chaos to High-Dimensional Dynamics in Self-Attention Systems
arxiv:2611.29951.summary: Continuous-time particle models of self-attention are often studied under symmetry assumptions that yield a gradient structure and constrain the dynamics to convergence toward equilibria. We investigate the behavior of these systems beyond the gradient setting, considering autonomous projected self-attention models with constant query, key, and value matrices and particles constrained to an ellipse. For three particles, the equations define a vector field on the three-dimensional torus.

arxiv:2611.29984.title: Computable certificates for data-driven dimension reduction on reaction-diffusion lattices
arxiv:2611.29984.summary: Data-driven methods recover low-dimensional coordinates from high-dimensional spatiotemporal data. Whether those coordinates track a genuine invariant object or a finite-resolution artifact is not settled. On reaction-diffusion lattices, the spectral-gap condition of inertial-manifold theory reduces to a critical lattice size $n_*$.

arxiv:2611.30000.title: A cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values
arxiv:2611.30000.summary: In this paper we introduce a cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values. For a diagonally constant index on a periodically extended skew Young diagram, it is a sum over semi-standard cyclic Young tableaux. It includes the cyclic multiple zeta values of Hirose, Murahara and Murakami as a special case.
arxiv:2611.30000.authors: Ku-Yu Fan, Hau-Yi Lin, Jinbo Yu

arxiv:2611.30029.title: An Exact Vertex Localization of Zykov's Theorem
arxiv:2611.30029.summary: We establish a vertex-based localization of the exact form of Zykov's theorem. For a graph $G$ of order $n\geq1$, let $N(G,K_t)$ denote its number of copies of $K_t$, and let $c(v)$ be the order of a largest clique containing $v$. Write $Z_t(n,s)=N(T_s(n),K_t)$, where $T_s(n)$ is the balanced complete $s$-partite graph on $n$ vertices.

arxiv:2611.30030.title: Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes
arxiv:2611.30030.summary: This paper investigates the list-recoverability of folded Reed--Solomon codes and provides new evidence toward a recent conjecture. Chen--Zhang (STOC 2025) established that for any $\ell,a \ge 2$ and $L = \ell^a - 1$, if a folded Reed--Solomon code of rate $R$ is $(\rho,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, then $\rho\leq \frac{L+1-\ell}{L+1}(1-\frac{aR}{a-1}).$ It is conjectured that this upper bound is tight. We provide two pieces of evidence concerning this conjecture.
arxiv:2611.30030.authors: Yeyuan Chen, Mahdi Cheraghchi, King-Siong Si, Zihan Zhang

arxiv:2611.30053.title: Trajectory arclength reveals thermodynamic criticality
arxiv:2611.30053.summary: Thermodynamic criticality arises at continuous phase transitions, where collective interactions produce non-analytic behavior in equilibrium thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit. We show that this criticality also leaves an analytically predictable signature in the arclength of microscopic Hamiltonian trajectories. For the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field model, we derive the thermodynamic limit of the equilibrium-averaged arclength, formulated as a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, and demonstrate that it develops a kink precisely at the phase transition.

arxiv:2611.30056.title: H(n)-Gordian graphs of knotoids and their quotients: Gromov hyperbolicity
arxiv:2611.30056.summary: In this paper, we study $H(n)$-moves on knotoid diagrams and the corresponding $H(n)$-Gordian graphs. We establish that the $H(n)$-Gordian graphs of knotoids are not Gromov hyperbolic. We also consider quotient graphs of the $H(n)$-Gordian graph of knotoids by the following knotoid invariants: the height of a knotoid, the span of the affine index polynomial, the $y$-span and $z$-span of the invariant $H_K(t, y, z)$, and the span of the Jones polynomial.

arxiv:2611.30089.title: GIT-thresholds for K-moduli spaces of Hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.30089.summary: In this note, we confirm the first wall $c_1(d)$ of K-moduli of hypersurfaces of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq n+1$, where $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd}$ if $d$ is even; and $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd-(n+1)}$ if $d$ is odd. Before this wall, the K-moduli is identical to the GIT-moduli for degree $d$ hypersurfaces, so we also call this number the GIT-threshold.

arxiv:2611.30095.title: A complete knot invariant from grid diagrams
arxiv:2611.30095.summary: Using grid diagrams, we define an infinite graph associated to each knot type. We prove that the isomorphism class of this grid graph is a complete invariant of the knot, up to mirroring. Even more, we prove that algorithmically determinable finite parts of this graph are enough to determine the knot type.
arxiv:2611.30095.authors: Agnese Barbensi, Daniele Celoria, Lavender Marshall, Finn Thompson

arxiv:2611.30110.title: A Constructive Lower Bound for the Growth Constant of Ternary Cap Sets
arxiv:2611.30110.summary: Let $r_3(d)$ denote the maximum size of a cap set in $\mathbb{F}_3^d$. We prove that the exponential growth constant $\Lambda = \lim_{d\to\infty} r_3(d)^{1/d}$ is strictly greater than $2.22920646813$. The main advance comes from combining two-color recursive synchronization with cross-layer joint filling of a seven-dimensional local alphabet that contains collinear triples (lines).

arxiv:2611.30132.title: Reverse Schensted bumping, inverse reduction map and concatenation in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
arxiv:2611.30132.summary: Provided the explicit formula for the inverse reduction map, arXiv:2606.24840, we exhibit for symplectic bumped intervals and for symplectic bumped columns disjoint for the action of the parity involution, the feasibility of the concatenation operation to return a semi-standard tableau in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection

arxiv:2611.30137.title: Free rational curves on singular Fano varieties
arxiv:2611.30137.summary: We prove that every klt Fano variety admits a free rational curve in its smooth locus.

arxiv:2611.30138.title: The Riemann Hypothesis for L-Functions of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Frobenius Polynomials and Intersection Cohomology
arxiv:2611.30138.summary: We study Frobenius polynomials attached to linearly constrained Kloosterman families, taking the rank-$r(n)=2^n-\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, weight-$(n+1)$ sheaf of the author's companion papers as an explicit input. The present contribution is the passage from that sheaf to local characteristic polynomials and the intermediate-extension intersection cohomology on $(\mathbb P^1)^n$. We prove the local reciprocal-root bounds and the degreewise purity of the completed factors; their weights are $n+1+i$ in cohomological degree $i$.

arxiv:2611.30147.title: Compatible expansions and rigidity in subtraction games with a single pass
arxiv:2611.30147.summary: We study normal-play subtraction games with one globally shared pass. An expansion of the subtraction set is pass-equivalent if it leaves the pass-available Sprague--Grundy sequence unchanged. We show that pure periodicity of the ordinary sequence, together with an eventual translation identity for the pass-available sequence, forces every pass-equivalent expansion to preserve the ordinary sequence.

arxiv:2611.30174.title: Products of translates: bounds and constructions
arxiv:2611.30174.summary: We study products of translates of the form $(A+d)(A+d)$ with $d\in D$, where both $A$ and $D$ are finite subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. We show that $|(A+a)(A+a)|\ge C|A|^{5/3}$ for some $a\in A$, and that $|(A+D)(A+D)|\le |A|^{2-c(\alpha)}$ for some $c(\alpha)>0$ when $|D|=|A|^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha<1$.
arxiv:2611.30174.authors: Sian Fang, Danqing He, Xinyu Zhu

arxiv:2611.30197.title: Homotopical interpretation of directed Van Kampen
arxiv:2611.30197.summary: We construct the Grandis model structure on directed spaces with $\Delta$-generated underlying spaces and on the full subcategory of $\Delta$-Hausdorff objects. In either setting the model structure is left proper, and its weak equivalences are precisely the maps that induce equivalences of fundamental categories in the sense of Grandis. The fundamental category functor preserves all small homotopy colimits with values in the folk model structure on small categories.

arxiv:2611.30217.title: Synchronisation under quasi-periodic forcing of circle diffeomorphisms with two attracting and two repelling fixed points
arxiv:2611.30217.summary: We study the dynamics of circle diffeomorphisms, which have exactly two attracting and two repelling fixed points, under quasi-periodic forcing. For sufficiently small forcing, such a system exhibits uniformly hyperbolic behaviour. The results focus on systems with larger forcing, where every orbit intersects the basins of attraction of both attracting fixed points infinitely often.

arxiv:2611.30227.title: $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property
arxiv:2611.30227.summary: Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.

arxiv:2611.30231.title: A construction of proper Jordan schemes of rank $5$
arxiv:2611.30231.summary: Let $q$ be a prime power such that $m=q^2+q+1$ is a prime satisfying $m\equiv 1\pmod{4}$. We construct a proper symmetric Jordan scheme of rank $5$ on $2m$ vertices using a Singer difference set with parameters $(m,q+1,1)$ and the Paley graph on $m$ vertices.

arxiv:2611.30234.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
arxiv:2611.30234.summary: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two…

arxiv:2611.30237.title: The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds
arxiv:2611.30237.summary: We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4.

arxiv:2611.30248.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
arxiv:2611.30248.summary: Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$.
arxiv:2611.30248.authors: Hanzhi Bai, Xinyu Hu, Kaidi Liu, Guanghui Wang

arxiv:2611.30261.title: Sierpi\'{n}ski Gaskets Julia set and Postcritically finite fractals
arxiv:2611.30261.summary: Devaney's work on the Julia sets of the McMullen family, established these rational maps as central objects in holomorphic dynamics. For Misiurewicz parameters, that is when the orbits of the critical points are all strictly preperiodic to a repelling cycle, the topological point of view taken by Kameyama links the dynamics of such rational maps to that on the attractors of invertible self-similar iterated function system. Ero\u{g}lu, Rohde, and Solomyak showed that in favorable cases the topological conjugacy is in fact quasisymmetric.

arxiv:2611.30294.title: Periodic orbit asymptotics and dynamical zeta functions for smooth surface diffeomorphisms
arxiv:2611.30294.summary: Let $f$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a closed surface $M$, and let $H$ be a closed homoclinic class with topological entropy $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f|H)>0$ and homoclinic period $\ell$. We prove that \[ \forall\,0<\chi<h,\qquad \lim_{\ell\mid n,\;n\to\infty} \frac{\#\mathrm{Per}_\chi(n,H)}{e^{nh}}=\ell, \] where $\mathrm{Per}_\chi(n,H)$ denotes the saddle points in $H$ of least period $n$ whose Lyapunov exponents lie outside $[-\chi,\chi]$. We also prove exponential remainders for the class and global counting formulas.

arxiv:2611.30295.title: Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities
arxiv:2611.30295.summary: We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.

arxiv:2611.30317.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-2: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
arxiv:2611.30317.summary: We study foliated deformations of compact complex manifolds with dimension 1-foliations and codimension 1-foliations, and unfoldings of compact complex manifolds with codimension 1-foliations in terms of deformations of sections with classical examples in deformation theory of complex structures.

arxiv:2611.30327.title: Tropical limits of holomorphic linking for toric hypersurfaces and points
arxiv:2611.30327.summary: A holomorphic top form on a smooth hypersurface in a smooth projective toric variety has a unique meromorphic residue lift when the ambient dimension is at least two. Evaluating this lift at a point, relative to the logarithmic volume form, gives a complex linking number. For a one-parameter family of hypersurfaces and a normalised monomial residue, we prove that this function converges to the indicator of the corresponding tropical chamber.

arxiv:2611.30333.title: Alpha-points of a putative binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane
arxiv:2611.30333.summary: A point $P$ of a putative $q$-analog $\mathcal{D}$ of the Fano plane is an $\alpha$-point if the derived design of $\mathcal{D}$ in $P$ is a Desarguesian line spread. Kiermaier showed that for $q$ prime or even every hyperplane contains a point which is not an $\alpha$-point. For $q=2$ we study the $45$ blocks of $\mathcal{D}$ inside a hyperplane $H$.

arxiv:2611.30364.title: Eigendecomposition for instantons via infinity-category
arxiv:2611.30364.summary: Suppose $L$ is a framed link in a balanced sutured manifold $(M, \gamma)$. We construct a link spectral sequence in sutured instanton homology. For properly embedded surfaces in $M$ disjoint from $L$, we refine the spectral sequence to preserve the induced multi-grading.

arxiv:2611.30371.title: The limit shape of uniform random antichains in $[0,1]^d$
arxiv:2611.30371.summary: For each $d\ge2$, we study $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, conditioned to form an antichain: no point is strictly smaller than another in every coordinate. We prove that the point cloud converges in Hausdorff distance to the closure of the hypersurface \[\mathcal S_d=\left\{\mathbf x\in(0,1)^d: \sum_{i=1}^d\Phi^{-1}(\mathbf x_i)=0\right\}\] in probability as $n\to\infty$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The proof also shows that the antichain probability $a_n$ satisfies $\log a_n=-\frac{n}{d-1}\log n+\beta_d n+o(n)$ for a finite constant $\beta_d$.

arxiv:2611.30377.title: Dimension-uniform Connectivity Laws and Hitting Times for Spherical Random Geometric Graphs
arxiv:2611.30377.summary: Let $G_d(n,p)$ be the graph formed by joining pairs of $n$ independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ within a radius chosen to give edge probability $p$. For each fixed integer $K\ge0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, we prove that at $np=\log n+K\log\log n+t$, the probabilities of $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity both converge to $\exp(-e^{-t}/K!)$ uniformly over all $d=d(n)\ge3$. This is the same limit as in the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph.

arxiv:2611.30386.title: Quasi-abelian Cousin groups of number fields:a Galois-orbit criterion and the complete list
arxiv:2611.30386.summary: Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary.

arxiv:2611.30403.title: Quantum walks and conformal mappings
arxiv:2611.30403.summary: We study the most elementary discrete model of an electron moving along a line, known as Feynman checkers, quantum walk, or the six-vertex model with special complex weights, and provide a uniform asymptotic formula for the wave function in the whole xt-plane. In addition to the well-known appearance of the Airy function that describes the transition between the oscillating and exponentially decaying regimes, we observe a second transition governed by the gamma function when the electron speed approaches the speed of light. We prove two general theorems producing uniform asymptotic formulae involving the Airy and gamma functions, using conformal mappings associated with the underlying…
arxiv:2611.30403.authors: Fedor Kuyanov, Michael Drmota, Mikhail Skopenkov, Alexey Ustinov

arxiv:2611.30462.title: Consecutive sums and Reconstructing Problems
arxiv:2611.30462.summary: We study several problems concerning consecutive sums of integer sequences and their relationship with Sidon sets. We also provide new lower bounds for an extremal function related to sequences with distinct consecutive sums, and consider reconstruction problems from multisets of consecutive sums.
arxiv:2611.30462.authors: Norbert Hegyv\'ari, P\'eter P\'al Pach, Quanyu Tang

arxiv:2611.30470.title: One-shot identification of analytic systems
arxiv:2611.30470.summary: We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective.
arxiv:2611.30470.authors: Nicolas Boull\'e, Diana Halikias, Samuel E. Otto, Alex Townsend

arxiv:2611.30506.title: Functionals commuting with reparametrizations
arxiv:2611.30506.summary: Motivated by the study of tangent curve bundles of algebraic varieties, we consider the following simple-looking problem: given a space $E$ of functions, describe functionals from $E^n$ to $E$ which commutes with reparametrizations, i.e. with the right-composition with an element of $E$. Our main result is a complete description of the algebraic solutions of this problem when $E$ is the space of polynomials vanishing in $0$, which we denote by $\mathbb C[T]_0$. This description involves a simple operation, which we call semi-product, with interesting algebraic and geometric properties.
arxiv:2611.30506.authors: Pierre-Emmanuel Chaput, David Dos Santos Ferreira, Valentin F\'eray

arxiv:2611.30510.title: Algorithms and topological invariants for dynamic systems. IV. Topological Equivalence of Functions and Hamiltonian Dynamical Systems
arxiv:2611.30510.summary: This is the fourth part of a series on algorithms and topological invariants for dynamical systems. We study the topological equivalence of smooth functions and of Hamiltonian flows on surfaces, and the discrete invariants, Reeb graphs and cell decompositions, that classify them. We recall the notions of topological equivalence and structural stability, introduce two equivalences of functions (with and without the order of the critical values) and show that simple Morse functions on closed orientable surfaces are classified by their Reeb graphs with vertex odering, while simple Hamiltonian flows are classified by Reeb graphs with marked edges.

arxiv:2611.30512.title: A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
arxiv:2611.30512.summary: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstra\"{e}te conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $\gamma(G)\le n/3$.
arxiv:2611.30512.authors: Kun Cheng, Changlong Shen, Leilei Zhang

arxiv:2611.30544.title: A corank one Lipschitz normally embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with non-trivial link
arxiv:2611.30544.summary: We show that the knot-triviality theorem for Lipschitz normally embedded (LNE) corank one surface singularities in $\mathbb{R}^4$ proved by Birbrair, Mendes and Nu\~no-Ballesteros (2018) does not generalize unrestrictedly. More precisely, we exhibit a polynomial map germ $F:(\mathbb{R}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{R}^4,0)$ of corank one at the origin, with isolated singularity and $2$-jet $(x,0,0,0)$, whose image $X=F(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is LNE at the origin, yet its link is the granny knot $T\#T$, and hence non-trivial. The example is obtained via a general uniform-degree homogenization procedure applied to a known polynomial parametrization of the trefoil knot.
arxiv:2611.30544.authors: L. Birbrair, Rodrigo Mendes, J. J. Nu\~no-Ballesteros

arxiv:2611.30551.title: On \(q\)-ary Minimal Linear Codes from Hierarchical Posets
arxiv:2611.30551.summary: In this paper, we study several families of \(q\)-ary linear codes constructed from two-level hierarchical posets over finite fields \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q>2\). By using generating functions and additive characters, we determine their complete weight distributions, dimensions, and minimum distances. This paper focuses on constructing minimal codes that violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

arxiv:2611.30562.title: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
arxiv:2611.30562.summary: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles.

arxiv:2611.30566.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
arxiv:2611.30566.summary: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$.
arxiv:2611.30566.authors: Shuai Guo, Longting Wu, Lei You

arxiv:2611.30618.title: A uniform Picard-rank bound for Calabi Yau threefolds with finitely many flop chambers
arxiv:2611.30618.summary: We prove that a smooth projective strict Calabi Yau threefold of sufficiently large Picard number either has infinitely many marked flop chambers or admits a fibration on a smooth flop model.

arxiv:2611.30619.title: The Hamilton cycle space in the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process
arxiv:2611.30619.summary: Let $G(n,m)$ denote the graph at step $m$ of the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process on $n$ vertices. The process starts with the edgeless graph and adds one edge at each step, chosen uniformly at random from the missing edges. Let $\tau_3$ be the first step at which the minimum degree of $G(n,m)$ reaches three.
arxiv:2611.30619.authors: Hao Zhang, Wensheng Sun, Panpan Cheng

arxiv:2611.30644.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
arxiv:2611.30644.summary: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the Andr\'e-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.

arxiv:2611.30677.title: On $k$-very ample line bundles on blowups of surfaces
arxiv:2611.30677.summary: In this article we study the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow ups of some smooth surfaces. We begin by investigating the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow-ups of smooth surfaces with Picard number $1$, extending the previously known cases of uniform line bundles to arbitrary line bundles, under certain restrictions. We then show that for blowups of smooth surfaces with trivial canonical divisor, $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles implies the $k$-very ampleness of arbitrary line bundles.
arxiv:2611.30677.authors: Suratno Basu, Abhirup Das, Umme Joinab, Rupam Karmakar

arxiv:2611.30682.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
arxiv:2611.30682.summary: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two.

arxiv:2611.30684.title: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
arxiv:2611.30684.summary: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings.

arxiv:2611.30718.title: A variant of the Erd\H{o}s--Gy\'arf\'as problem for $K_9$ and $K_{12}$
arxiv:2611.30718.summary: For a graph $H$, let $r_H(n)$ be the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of $K_n$ such that every copy of $H$ contains a color appearing an odd number of times. We prove that $r_{K_9}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ and $r_{K_{12}}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$. These bounds on $r_H(n)$ yield linear graph codes of density at least $\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ that avoid images of $K_9$ and $K_{12}$.
arxiv:2611.30718.authors: Luyi Li, Guiying Yan, Zicheng Ye

arxiv:2611.30721.title: Partition rank and analytic rank over finite field
arxiv:2611.30721.summary: We prove that the partition rank and the analytic rank of a tensor over any finite field are equivalent up to a constant depending only on the order of the tensor. The proof combines Mili\'cevi\'c's theorem on dense multilinear varieties with the differential Schur complement of Moshkovitz and Zhu. The new ingredient is a method for approximately eliminating multilinear equations.

arxiv:2611.30724.title: Bifurcation Structure and Coexisting Dynamical States in Two Inductively Coupled Josephson Junctions
arxiv:2611.30724.summary: Inductively coupled Josephson junctions support coexisting stationary and running states whose selection depends on both circuit parameters and initial conditions. We investigate the model of a direct current-driven resistively and capacitively shunted junction pair as coupled nonlinear oscillators at zero external magnetic flux, allowing unequal bias, damping and inductive coupling parameters. Equilibrium equations, nullclines, and Jacobian spectra are combined with multiple-initial-condition simulations, finite-time Lyapunov spectra, and Poincar\'e returns to characterize changes in the system dynamics under varying initial conditions and parameter settings.

arxiv:2611.30731.title: Via a New LP Relaxation: Stronger Performance Guarantees for WSEPT, and an LP-Based Proof of Kawaguchi & Kyan
arxiv:2611.30731.summary: We present a new linear programming relaxation for minimizing the total weighted completion time on identical parallel machines. Its right-hand side is supermodular, so the relaxation can be solved by a greedy algorithm. We show that the WSPT rule is within a factor $\frac{1}{2}(1 + \sqrt{2})$ of the optimal LP value.
arxiv:2611.30731.authors: Maximilian von Aspern, Andreas S. Schulz, Eugenio Vairo

arxiv:2611.30749.title: Notes on an elementary proof of Weil II from Hexagon
arxiv:2611.30749.summary: Recently, L. Alp\"oge sketched an elementary proof of Deligne's weight bound in footnote 3 of his remark on joint work with Claude on the Riemann hypothesis. An expanded, AI-generated account appeared on Hexagon, where it was posted by F.

arxiv:2611.30752.title: A Keller--Segel Chemotaxis Model on One-Dimensional Moving Domains
arxiv:2611.30752.summary: We study a one-dimensional Keller--Segel system on an interval whose boundary moves according to a prescribed contracting law. The boundary motion makes the problem genuinely nonautonomous and destroys the mass conservation available on fixed domains. A time-dependent change of variables, combined with a time reparametrization, reduces the problem to a semilinear system on a fixed interval with time-independent principal part and nonautonomous transport terms.
arxiv:2611.30752.authors: Jackeline C. Huaccha Neyra, John Matos Ascona, Lizet Santa Cruz Calder\'on, Heraclio L\'opez-L\'azaro

arxiv:2611.30760.title: Categorical Torelli theorem for quintic threefolds
arxiv:2611.30760.summary: We prove that two smooth quintic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$ are isomorphic if their bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves are equivalent.

arxiv:2611.30772.title: Automorphism groups of mixing shifts of finite type
arxiv:2611.30772.summary: We prove that nontrivial two-sided mixing shifts of finite type are flip conjugate if and only if their automorphism groups are abstractly commensurable. This resolves an outstanding question of Boyle, Lind, and Rudolph from 1988.

arxiv:2611.30783.title: A mean index criterion for multiple closed characteristics
arxiv:2611.30783.summary: Let $n\ge2$. We prove that a compact strictly star-shaped $C^3$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ carries at least $n$ geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics if all iterates are nondegenerate and all mean indices are at least one. It suffices that all mean indices are positive and that the bound holds only for prime characteristics with negative mean Euler characteristic in the variational grading.

arxiv:2611.30790.title: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
arxiv:2611.30790.summary: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$.

arxiv:2611.30791.title: Joint statistics on vexillary involutions via Fulton's essential set
arxiv:2611.30791.summary: We jointly enumerate various statistics over vexillary involutions among which there are the number of descents and the number of peaks. As a by-product, we get an equidistribution result between vexillary involutions and 3412-avoiding involutions, which, notably, implies that, for every $n$ and $k$, the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $3412$ and having $k$ descents equals the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $2143$ and having $k$ ascents. The proof describes $2143$-avoiding involutions through Fulton's ranked essential set, translates the count into a weighted enumeration of walks in the quarter plane, and solves the latter explicitly.

arxiv:2611.30797.title: Spherical CR uniformization for 7 links
arxiv:2611.30797.summary: We consider subgroups in $PU(2,1)$ generated by three involutions $I_1,I_2,I_3$ such that $I_2I_3$ has order $p$ and the elements $I_1I_2$, $I_2I_3$, $I_1I_3I_2I_3$ are all in the same conjugacy class of $PU(2,1)$. We show that these groups are discrete whenever $I_1I_2$ and $I_1I_2I_3$ are non-elliptic and we study the orbifolds at infinity. In addition, we show that for $3 \leq p \leq 9$ the complement of a symmetric cyclic chain of $p$ simple links admits a spherical CR uniformization.

arxiv:2611.30801.title: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
arxiv:2611.30801.summary: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $\lambda > 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $\lambda > 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.

arxiv:2611.30807.title: Zariski-constructible functions of class $\mathcal{C}^k$
arxiv:2611.30807.summary: Let $R$ be a real closed field. A Zariski-constructible subset of $R^n$, $\mathcal{ZC}$-set for short, is a Boolean combination of algebraic subsets of $R^n$. Euclidean closed Zariski-constructible subsets of $R^n$ are the closed subsets of a Noetherian topology finer than the Zariski topology of $R^n$.
arxiv:2611.30807.authors: Jean-Baptiste Campesato, Jean-Philippe Monnier, Enrico Savi

arxiv:2611.30833.title: Disc functionals and rational curves
arxiv:2611.30833.summary: We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact K\"ahler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact K\"ahler manifolds.
arxiv:2611.30833.authors: Yinji Li, Haoyuan Sun, Zhiwei Wang, Xiangyu Zhou

arxiv:2611.30837.title: On the Geometry of Quadratic Maps
arxiv:2611.30837.summary: To analyse a homogeneous quadratic map $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the critical value variety $\Sigma_{Q}$ of its restriction to the unit sphere is very useful but difficult to handle. We prove its dual hypersurface $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is of degree $k$ (providing its equation) and is $\mathit{hyperbolic}$: every line though the origin in $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ cuts it at $k$ real points, counting multiplicities. These facts imply: $\boldsymbol{1}$.

arxiv:2611.30847.title: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
arxiv:2611.30847.summary: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urba\'nski in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound.

arxiv:2611.30861.title: The spectrum of codegree Tur\'an densities of 3-graphs
arxiv:2611.30861.summary: The \emph{minimum codegree} $\delta_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Tur\'an density} $\gamma(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $\delta_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $\alpha\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Tur\'an density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_\alpha$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $\gamma(\mathcal{F}')>\alpha$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_\alpha$.
arxiv:2611.30861.authors: Jun Gao, Oleg Pikhurko, Mingyuan Rong, Shumin Sun

arxiv:2611.30864.title: Hypergeometric Abelian Surfaces and Triangle-Group Levels
arxiv:2611.30864.summary: We study three families of hypergeometric abelian surfaces with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We determine their integral homology lattices and monodromy, including the choice of lattice at the ramified prime above $5$ in the plus family. One family is isomorphic to an explicit quadratic twist of a genus-two Frey Jacobian, with the two real-multiplication embeddings exchanged.

arxiv:2611.30871.title: A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle
arxiv:2611.30871.summary: We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori.

arxiv:2611.30887.title: A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT
arxiv:2611.30887.summary: We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. For each integer $w\ge5$, we encode 3-CNF formulas with exactly $m=2^w-1$ clauses over $m$ available variables using $n=3m(w+1)$ bits. The proof embeds Boolean tests in variable identifiers while retaining $n-o(n)$ free bits, and combines weighted gate elimination with a nonlinear-gate lower bound from the tests' full algebraic degree over $\mathbb F_2$.

arxiv:2611.30899.title: The number of non-isomorphic spanning trees in regular graphs
arxiv:2611.30899.summary: By a classical theorem of Otter, the number of non-isomorphic trees on $n$ vertices is $\alpha^n\exp(-o(n))$, where $\alpha\approx 2.956$ is Otter's constant. We prove that every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains $\alpha^n\exp(-o_d(n))$ non-isomorphic spanning trees, where $o_d(n)/n\to0$ as $d\to\infty$.

arxiv:2611.30929.title: Quartic hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{A}^3$ isomorphic to the affine plane
arxiv:2611.30929.summary: In 1975 Abhayankar and Moh have shown that over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 all polynomial embeddings of the affine line into the affine plane are equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. For embeddings of the affine plane into $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose image is a hypersurface of degree 3, it is shown in arXiv:1912.02144 that they are also equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. We will consider the case where the image is a quartic hypersurface of $\mathbb{A}^3$ and classify all such hypersurfaces up to affine automorphisms.

arxiv:2611.30941.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
arxiv:2611.30941.summary: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal.

arxiv:2611.30946.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems II: Upper Right Quadrant
arxiv:2611.30946.summary: We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories.

arxiv:2611.30952.title: Three commuting matrices whose lifts never commute
arxiv:2611.30952.summary: We construct pairwise commuting matrices over $\mathbb{F}_p$ which have no pairwise commuting lifts to $\mathbb{Z}/p^2\mathbb{Z}$. Equivalently, there are mod $p$ representations of the absolute Galois group of the field of iterated Laurent series $\mathbb{C}((x_1))\cdots((x_d))$ which do not lift modulo $p^2$.

arxiv:2611.30971.title: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
arxiv:2611.30971.summary: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.

arxiv:2611.30975.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
arxiv:2611.30975.summary: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants.

arxiv:2611.30981.title: Automorphisms Induced on Cartan Tori and Centers of Quantized Enveloping Algebras
arxiv:2611.30981.summary: Let \(U=U_q(\mathfrak g)\) be the root-lattice form of the quantized enveloping algebra associated with a complex simple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), over a field \(\mathbb{k}\) of characteristic zero, with \(q\in\mathbb{k}^{\times}\) not a root of unity. We determine the groups of automorphisms induced by algebra automorphisms of $U$ on its Cartan torus $U^0$ and its center $Z(U)$. These groups are \[ \Aut_U(U^0)\cong\Hom(Q,\{\pm1\})\rtimes\Aut(\Phi), \] \[ \Aut_U(Z(U))\cong\Hom((P/Q)[2],\{\pm1\})\rtimes\Gamma, \] where $Q$ and $P$ are the root and weight lattices, $\Phi$ is the root system, $\Gamma$ is the automorphism group of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak g$, and $(P/Q)[2]$ is the…

arxiv:2611.30987.title: Gaudin's determinantal norm formula and Hall--Littlewood polynomials
arxiv:2611.30987.summary: The Hall--Littlewood polynomials are orthogonal with respect to a discrete measure stemming from a discretization of the Lieb--Liniger model that describes $q$-bosons on the circle. This note establishes a previously conjectured Gaudin-type determinantal formula for their quadratic norms.

arxiv:2611.30988.title: Roman-Type Domination on Bisplit Graphs: Hardness and Inapproximability
arxiv:2611.30988.summary: Inspired by the structure and name of split graphs, bisplit graphs have three independent sets $I,A,B$, where every vertex of $A$ is adjacent to every vertex of $B$, and vertices of $I$ may have arbitrary neighborhoods in the core $A\cup B$. Thus they have a complete bipartite core together with the remaining vertices, making them a structured setting in which to study how core size affects complexity. Mann and Fernau's construction already implies NP-completeness of perfect Roman domination on bisplit graphs with a singleton core side \citep[Theorem~20]{mann-fernau-pr}.

arxiv:2611.30995.title: Connected Lie groups with a left-invariant intrinsic chronometer
arxiv:2611.30995.summary: In this paper, we investigate left-invariant intrinsic chronometers (time functions) on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups. We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. A one-to-one correspondence is established between chronometers satisfying the proposed system of axioms (including upper semi-continuity and the condition that the interiors of chronological rhombi form a base for the topology) and smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures.

arxiv:2611.30999.title: The monodromy conjecture for remarkable poles
arxiv:2611.30999.summary: We prove the strong monodromy conjecture for the remarkable numbers of a regular function f on a smooth complex variety. We show more generally that the log canonical modification of f computes the remarkable numbers and gives roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of f.
arxiv:2611.30999.authors: Nero Budur, Quan Shi, Huaiqing Zuo

arxiv:2611.31031.title: Tame homotopy theory and the Goodwillie tower of the identity
arxiv:2611.31031.summary: The purpose of this note is to provide a modern treatment of Dwyer's tame homotopy theory and extend it to non-simply connected spaces, exploiting a connection with the work of Heuts on the Goodwillie tower of the identity. As an application, we construct spectral Lie algebraic models for Hess's $r$-mild homotopy theory.

arxiv:2611.31042.title: Degree three unramified cohomology of homogeneous spaces with finite stabilisers
arxiv:2611.31042.summary: We provide an explicit formula for the third unramified cohomology group of homogeneous spaces of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with finite stabilisers and a rational point, valid over an arbitrary field of characteristic prime to the order of the stabilisers. As a concrete application, we compute this group explicitly for every generalised quaternion group over an arbitrary field of characteristic 0, and settle Noether's problem over the rational numbers in the negative for those of order at least 16, thereby generalising a classical result of Serre. Over an algebraically closed field, our formula recovers and sharpens a theorem of Peyre; we further show that universal triviality of unramified…

arxiv:2611.31066.title: Griffiths-Dwork Reduction For Smooth Hypersurfaces in Grassmannians
arxiv:2611.31066.summary: We give an explicit Griffiths-Dwork pole-order reduction algorithm for a smooth hypersurface $Z$ in a Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$. Under two arithmetic conditions on $k,n$, and the degree of $Z$, the residue construction describes the Hodge filtration on the middle cohomology of the complement in terms of the Jacobian ring. We explicitly characterize the required cohomological vanishings.

arxiv:2611.31067.title: $k$-ary Legendre pairs
arxiv:2611.31067.summary: We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$.
arxiv:2611.31067.authors: Ilias S. Kotsireas, Huaning Liu, Arne Winterhof

arxiv:2611.31070.title: A quasi-tree expansion for the two variable Bollob\'as--Riordan polynomial using a single basepoint
arxiv:2611.31070.summary: We give a quasi-tree expansion formula for the two variable Bollob\'as--Riordan polynomial of ribbon graphs that uses a single basepoint (a point on the boundary of the ribbon graph) as auxiliary datum.

arxiv:2611.31091.title: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
arxiv:2611.31091.summary: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^\gamma y,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $\gamma\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a B\^ocher-type…

arxiv:2611.31104.title: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
arxiv:2611.31104.summary: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

arxiv:2611.31111.title: Holomorphic Foliations with a Single Singularity on Orbifold Projective Surfaces
arxiv:2611.31111.summary: We investigate holomorphic foliations on orbifold projective surfaces with cyclic divisor class group, assuming that the foliation has a unique singular point of algebraic multiplicity one. If the normal degree of the foliation is sufficiently large, then we prove that it admits no invariant algebraic curve. Furthermore, we present several examples showing that the bound obtained is optimal.
arxiv:2611.31111.authors: Ruben Lizarbe, Liliana Puchuri, Rudy Rosas
