arxiv:2611.31120.title: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
arxiv:2611.31120.summary: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $\omega(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line.

arxiv:2611.31121.title: A Characterization of Tangle Matroids
arxiv:2611.31121.summary: We prove that a matroid with at least two elements is a tangle matroid if and only if it cannot be covered by three hyperplanes. Some consequences of this theorem are also noted. In particular, no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid.

arxiv:2611.31124.title: Euler Characteristics of Perverse Sheaves on Complex Ball Quotients
arxiv:2611.31124.summary: Let $X=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{B}^n$ be a finite-volume complex ball quotient with neat lattice. We prove that every nonzero algebraically constructible perverse sheaf on $X$ has positive Euler characteristic. More generally, we establish a criterion for strict positivity on smooth quasi-projective varieties whose logarithmic cotangent bundle is nef and admits an ample negative rational twist of the boundary divisor.

arxiv:2611.31136.title: Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices
arxiv:2611.31136.summary: Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.

arxiv:2611.31151.title: Standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart rings have unimodal $h$-vectors
arxiv:2611.31151.summary: We prove that the $h$-vector $(h_0,\ldots,h_s)$ of every standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart ring is unimodal, with a peak at position $\lceil s/2\rceil$. More generally, a standard graded Ehrhart ring has an alternatingly increasing $h$-vector if the radical of the ideal generated by the degree-one part of its canonical trace ideal contains the homogeneous maximal ideal. In characteristic zero or two, the generic Artinian reduction of each such ring has the strong Lefschetz property.

arxiv:2611.31152.title: A remark on cohomological and Chow decompositions of the diagonal
arxiv:2611.31152.summary: We construct a quartic double solid whose desingularization admits an integral cohomological decomposition of the diagonal but no Chow decomposition.

arxiv:2611.31188.title: On the space of left orders on the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H \text{ and }G_\infty$
arxiv:2611.31188.summary: We introduce the notion of a left order on a group with a certain specification of signs for the elements of a subset. We obtain an equivalent criterion for the existence of such a left order and apply it to obtain a new proof of the fact that any of the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H,\,G_\infty$ admits infinitely many non-Conradian left orders. We introduce the notion of separation of free subsemigroups of a left ordered group by its left translation induced actions on a point in the group and show that the above three groups admit such left orders.

arxiv:2611.31191.title: Cop-Win Edge Completion: Hardness, Structure, and Parameterized Algorithm
arxiv:2611.31191.summary: We study Cop-Win Edge Completion: given a graph $G$, find the minimum number $\copfill(G)$ of edges whose addition lets one cop capture a visible robber. We first give an exact reduction from Dominating Set, constructing for every nonempty graph $H$ a graph $G_H$ on $2|V(H)|+2$ vertices with $\copfill(G_H)=\gamma(H)$. This resolves a complexity question of Mertzios et al. and implies NP-completeness even for connected graphs of diameter two with a dominating edge and domination number two.

arxiv:2611.31199.title: Toward a Classification of Differentially $3$-Uniform Power Mappings over $\F_{p^2}$ and $\F_{p^3}$
arxiv:2611.31199.summary: We study the classification, up to the CCZ-equivalence, of differentially $3$-uniform power mappings over quadratic and cubic extensions of prime fields. Over $\F_{p^2}$ exhaustive searches for primes $3<p<300$ found only the known families E1 and E4 for $p>23$. Over $\F_{p^3}$, the previously unexplained exponents for $7<p<200$ belong to a single family.

arxiv:2611.31219.title: Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$
arxiv:2611.31219.summary: Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$.

arxiv:2611.31226.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
arxiv:2611.31226.summary: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the…
arxiv:2611.31226.authors: Andreas Chatziafratis, Guenbo Hwang, Georgia Karali

arxiv:2611.31229.title: Central limit theorem for energies of determinantal point processes on complex manifolds I
arxiv:2611.31229.summary: We study the Bergman determinantal point process associated with a positive line bundle on a compact Riemann surface. Consider the U-statistic given by the Green function, called the Green energy. For a configuration of $N$ points, the expectation of Green energy is $\frac12 N\log N+O(N)$, and the variance is $(\log 2-\pi^2/24)N+O(\log^2 N)$.

arxiv:2611.31244.title: On the invertibility of saddle-point matrices: exact algebraic conditions and applications to constrained dynamics
arxiv:2611.31244.summary: The solvability of constrained dynamical systems governed by D'Alembert--Lagrange mechanics relies directly on the invertibility of the coefficient matrix describing the underlying saddle-point structure, which couples system inertia with kinematic constraints. Standard formulations often rely on overly restrictive sufficient assumptions, such as global positive definiteness or semi-definiteness of the mass matrix, frequently combined with generalized inverses to handle singular mass distributions. In this work, we establish the purely necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for matrix invertibility: the kinematic independence of the constraints and a kernel intersection condition…

arxiv:2611.31289.title: Minor--Skein Spatial Negami Splitting Vectors and a Gluing Formula for Marked State Sums
arxiv:2611.31289.summary: We organize the edge states of a decorated spatial graph by the minors of their underlying abstract graphs. For pieces with disjoint edge sets, Negami's component formula and functorial ribbon evaluation express each marked sector as a boundary pairing, provided the local data determine its marker. We give two explicit rules for this last step.

arxiv:2611.31290.title: Ramsey numbers of fixed-length cycles, paths and stars in set-colored triple systems
arxiv:2611.31290.summary: Let $R_3(H;r,s,t)$ be the least order of a complete triple system in which every assignment of $s$ of $r$ colors to each triple forces a copy of $H$ whose edges share at least $t$ colors. Fix $r\ge s\ge t\ge1$ and let $n$ count edges. We prove that the Ramsey numbers of the linear path and the linear cycle of fixed length $n$ are both $\gamma n+o(n)$ as $n\to\infty$, with $\gamma=2$ if and only if $r=s$.

arxiv:2611.31300.title: Power-Law Lower Bounds for Edges in Odd Induced Subgraphs
arxiv:2611.31300.summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $g(G)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an induced subgraph of $G$ in which every vertex has odd degree. Motivated by Scott's question of whether $g(G) \geq cm$ for every graph with $m$ edges, we prove that $g(G) \geq cm^{4/7}$ for every finite simple graph with $m \geq 1$ edges, where $c > 0$ is an absolute constant. For bipartite graphs, we obtain the stronger bound $g(B) \geq cm^{2/3}$.

arxiv:2611.31323.title: Depth of leaves in closed linear $\lambda$-terms: exact recurrence, limit law and edge window
arxiv:2611.31323.summary: Let $K_n$ (resp.\ $D_n$) be the depth of a uniform leaf (resp.\ node) in a uniform closed linear $\lambda$-term of size $n$. A bijective \emph{grafting identity} yields an exact polynomial-time recurrence for the full depth profile. By the method of moments, $K_n/n$ converges in law to the density $3x/\sqrt{1-2x}$ on $[0,\frac12]$, i.e.\ $2K_n/n\to\Beta(2,\frac12)$, with $\mathbb E[K_n^r]/n^r\to3(r+1)!/(2r+3)!!$; likewise $1-2D_n/n\to\Beta(\frac12,1)$.

arxiv:2611.31324.title: Bounds for the small Davenport constant of extraspecial groups of exponent three
arxiv:2611.31324.summary: Let $E_s$ be the extraspecial group of order $3^{2s+1}$ and exponent three. We prove $4s+2r+2\le d(E_s\times C_3^r)\le 4s+2r+3$ for $s\ge1$ and $r\ge0$. For $s\ge2$, the degree in the polynomial proof is optimal among weights depending only on group-element multiplicities modulo three.

arxiv:2611.31328.title: Ternary Perfect $2$-Burst-Correcting Codes
arxiv:2611.31328.summary: A construction for a ternary perfect linear $2$-burst-correcting code is presented for every redundancy $r \geq 5$. The construction is recursive with seeds given for $5 \leq r \leq 7$. The construction of redundancy $r \geq 8$ is derived from a code of redundancy $r-3$ and it distinguishes between codes of even and odd length.

arxiv:2611.31336.title: Quadratic periods after adjoining one move to a fixed subtraction game
arxiv:2611.31336.summary: Zhang conjectured that adjoining one move $c$ to a fixed subtraction set $S$ gives a Grundy sequence whose least preperiod and period are both $O_S(c)$. For every $q=20+9s$ with $s\ge0$, take $S=\{3,6,q-3\}$. Along $c=qk+1$ with $k\ge2$, the Grundy and win/loss sequences are periodic from heap zero with common least period $(k+2)(c+6)-11$, asymptotic to $c^2/q$.

arxiv:2611.31337.title: Products and duality for framed 1-flow categories
arxiv:2611.31337.summary: We describe a product between framed 1-flow categories and show that it satisfies the expected Cartan formula on its second Steenrod squares. We also describe a dual framed 1-flow category and show that, like the Spanier-Whitehead dual of spectra, the homology groups of a framed 1-flow category can be shown to be isomorphic to the cohomology groups of its dual and that this isomorphism can be shown to cooperate with the framed 1-flow category structure in a suitable sense.

arxiv:2611.31356.title: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
arxiv:2611.31356.summary: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).
arxiv:2611.31356.authors: G Conant, J Freitag, C Terry

arxiv:2611.31409.title: RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations
arxiv:2611.31409.summary: There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$, where $L(\lambda)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$.

arxiv:2611.31420.title: Fake surfaces for some potential Andrews-Curtis counterexamples
arxiv:2611.31420.summary: Andrews and Curtis famously conjectured that every contractible $2$-complex $3$-deforms to a point and, in fact, it suffices to consider contractible closed fake surfaces. The traditional potential counterexamples are given as balanced presentations of the trivial group. In this article, we construct closed fake surfaces for the Akbulut-Kirby family of potential counterexamples using geodesic loops in a metric classifying space for the $3$-strand braid group.

arxiv:2611.31443.title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
arxiv:2611.31443.summary: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.

arxiv:2611.31485.title: Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program
arxiv:2611.31485.summary: I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.

arxiv:2611.31490.title: Doubly Intermittent Singular Skew Products
arxiv:2611.31490.summary: We study a large class of skew product systems, which can also be thought of as random dynamical systems, coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full branch interval map with two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives. This significantly generalizes the setting of several skew products considered in the literature, in particular the Gou\"ezel skew products [Gou\"ezel, Statistical properties of a skew product with a curve of neutral points, Erg. Th. & Dyn.

arxiv:2611.31505.title: Topological Inference for degree-Cech complexes
arxiv:2611.31505.summary: We study topological inference for the degree-Cech bifiltration from noisy samples of a manifold. Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals.

arxiv:2611.31507.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
arxiv:2611.31507.summary: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, Andr\'e, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

arxiv:2611.31510.title: Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules
arxiv:2611.31510.summary: There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$ when $\mu$ is obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one to a part of $\lambda$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $\lambda$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms.

arxiv:2611.31538.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
arxiv:2611.31538.summary: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group.

arxiv:2611.31546.title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
arxiv:2611.31546.summary: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials.

arxiv:2611.31550.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
arxiv:2611.31550.summary: The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2.

arxiv:2611.31551.title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
arxiv:2611.31551.summary: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior.

arxiv:2611.31552.title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
arxiv:2611.31552.summary: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.

arxiv:2611.31562.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
arxiv:2611.31562.summary: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.
arxiv:2611.31562.authors: Stephanie Chan, Peter Koymans, Nick Rome, Tim Santens

arxiv:2611.31599.title: Major progress on hamiltonian saturation in hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.31599.summary: For $1\leq \ell< k$, an \emph{$\ell$-overlapping $k$-cycle} is a $k$-uniform hypergraph in which, for some cyclic vertex ordering, every edge consists of $k$ consecutive vertices and every two consecutive edges share exactly $\ell$ vertices. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is $\ell$-\emph{hamiltonian saturated} if $H$ does not contain an $\ell$-overlapping Hamilton $k$-cycle but every hypergraph obtained from $H$ by adding a new edge does contain such a cycle. For $n$ divisible by $k-\ell$, let sat$(n,k,\ell)$ be the smallest number of edges in an $\ell$-hamiltonian saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

arxiv:2611.31602.title: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
arxiv:2611.31602.summary: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes.

arxiv:2611.31618.title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
arxiv:2611.31618.summary: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $\tau$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$.
arxiv:2611.31618.authors: Masood Shahbaz Shoukat, Luca Di Persio, Wensheng Jia

arxiv:2611.31639.title: Determinant and quasi-alternateness of checkerboard colorable links
arxiv:2611.31639.summary: We give a connected state expansion of the determinant of checkerboard colorable links and extend the notion of quasi-alternateness from classical links to this setting. We provide an obstruction to quasi-alternateness and we characterize classicality of alternating virtual links. Then, we show that quasi-alternateness is preserved under rational extensions of quasi-alternating crossings.
arxiv:2611.31639.authors: Mohammed Sabak, Khaled Qazaqzeh, Hamid Abchir

arxiv:2611.31642.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds
arxiv:2611.31642.summary: We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes.

arxiv:2611.31691.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
arxiv:2611.31691.summary: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample.

arxiv:2611.31711.title: Combinatorial characterizations of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of positive alternating links and 3-braids
arxiv:2611.31711.summary: The $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link polynomial is a higher rank relative of the Jones polynomial which can be studied entirely diagrammatically using Kuperberg's web calculus. Building on the work of Harper and Kalfagianni, we construct formulae for the fourth and fifth coefficients of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link invariant on positive alternating link diagrams in terms of data read from the associated Seifert graph. Then, we give a characterization of the invariant on positive alternating fibered links in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials.
arxiv:2611.31711.authors: Matthew Harper, Joshua O'Connor, Jos\'e S\'anchez Mench\'en, Angie Wu

arxiv:2611.31759.title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
arxiv:2611.31759.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(\Gamma)$ is edge-transitive, then $\Gamma$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(\Gamma)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry.
arxiv:2611.31759.authors: Zai Ping Lu, Hai Ze Wang

arxiv:2611.31778.title: 10/8-inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary and its application
arxiv:2611.31778.summary: As an application of 10/8 inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary, we give criteria of homology 3-spheres represented by certain framed links for having infinite order in the homology cobordism group of homology 3-spheres. Such a class of homology 3-spheres includes certain plumbed 3-manifolds, 1/odd surgeries along certain knots with many twists, for example, certain Montesinos knots, $(p,q)$ cable knots of any knot with some large $p$, $q$, etc.

arxiv:2611.31796.title: A short proof of Serre positivity
arxiv:2611.31796.summary: Recently, OpenAI found a proof of the positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity. The two main ingredients are a descent result on rational $K$-theory with support; and a construction of certain category of asymptotic complexes that identifies with the category of perfect complexes over a connective (non-commutative) derived ring. In this article, we present a simpler proof of Serre positivity that circumvents the second step; instead, we use a ``reduction to the diagonal" trick via the $A_{\text{inf}}$-construction.

arxiv:2611.31807.title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
arxiv:2611.31807.summary: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields.

arxiv:2611.31809.title: The Borel Topos
arxiv:2611.31809.summary: We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.
arxiv:2611.31809.authors: Joseph Helfer, Patrick Lutz, Forte Shinko

arxiv:2611.31820.title: Fibered-knot braids and symplectic fake quadrics
arxiv:2611.31820.summary: We construct aspherical symplectic four-manifolds with the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$ by summing ruled surfaces along braided multisections. For each $m\geq1$, we form two symplectic sums with the same gluing map in the chosen surface markings and normal framings, using a stabilized braid for the trefoil in one sum and for the torus knot $T(2,7)$ in the other. Both sums have integral first homology $({\mathbb Z}/2)^2\oplus{\mathbb Z}/(4m)$.
arxiv:2611.31820.authors: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, Sai-Kee Yeung

arxiv:2611.31827.title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
arxiv:2611.31827.summary: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane.

arxiv:2611.31828.title: A logarithmic saving in the sum-free subset problem
arxiv:2611.31828.summary: For every sufficiently large $n$ there is a set of $n$ positive integers, all at most $n^2$, whose largest sum-free subset has size at most $n/3+O(n/\log n)$. We bound the number of small divisible elements in a dense set with few Schur triples. A fixed-accuracy cyclic model gives a rotation, and the original integer triple count controls its density at the required scale.

arxiv:2611.31846.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger systems
arxiv:2611.31846.summary: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pm\lambda_{1},\pm\lambda_{2}$ satisfying $0<\lambda_{1} < \lambda_{2} < 2\lambda_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet.

arxiv:2611.31862.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
arxiv:2611.31862.summary: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles.

arxiv:2611.31879.title: Modular Schur functions and Macdonald characters
arxiv:2611.31879.summary: Modular Schur functions arose from the problem of determining the characters of simple polynomial representations of the general linear group in positive characteristic. We prove three results about these functions. (i) In finitely many variables, we obtain two bases for a space of symmetric polynomials with bounded degree in each variable, one consisting of modular Schur polynomials and the other of products of truncated complete symmetric polynomials.

arxiv:2611.31911.title: Linearization for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth
arxiv:2611.31911.summary: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound.

arxiv:2611.31913.title: Linear programming certificates for dimension bounds of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
arxiv:2611.31913.summary: We use linear programming to derive upper bounds for the dimension of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes from local geometric and arithmetic estimates. Rational certificates give the bounds $57$ for finite-volume polytopes, $17$ for compact polytopes, and $15$ for compact arithmetic polytopes. In the finite-volume case, the certificate is a weight function on incidences between vertices and two-dimensional faces.

arxiv:2611.31934.title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
arxiv:2611.31934.summary: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior.
arxiv:2611.31934.authors: Rezwana Razzaque Angana, Brendan Harding, Dimitrios Mitsotakis

arxiv:2611.31946.title: Finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for real-weighted quivers
arxiv:2611.31946.summary: We study finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for quivers with positive real weights. We characterize finite Coxeter type by the condition that every weight in the mutation class has the form $2\cos(\pi/m)$ for some integer $m\geq3$. Under total sign-coherence, we then show that a quiver with finitely many $g$-clusters is $2$-finite, that is, every weight in its mutation class is less than $2$.

arxiv:2611.31963.title: Blow-up size for the noncommutative rank of linear symbolic matrices with low-rank coefficients
arxiv:2611.31963.summary: The noncommutative rank (nc-rank) of a linear symbolic matrix $A = A_0 x_0 + A_1 x_1 + \dots + A_m x_m$ is the supremum of $1/k$ times the rank of the $k$-th blow-up $\sum_i A_i \otimes X_i$ of $A$, where $X_i$ are $k \times k$ matrices consisting of distinct variables. In this paper, we show that the blow-up size needed to attain the nc-rank is bounded by the ranks of the coefficient matrices. More precisely, if $A_1, \dots, A_m$ have rank at most $r$, with no restriction on $A_0$, then the $k$-th blow-up attains the nc-rank for every $k \geq r$.

arxiv:2611.31967.title: The Generalized Volterra Signature
arxiv:2611.31967.summary: In this paper, we introduce the generalized Volterra signature \(\gvsig(\bX)\) of a path \(\bX\), extending the classical Volterra signature introduced in [Hager, Harang, Pelizzari \& Tindel, arXiv:2603.04525, 2026], which extends Lyons' path signature to the Volterra setting. We establish a new algebraic structure to encode the generalized Volterra signature. We also establish a generalized Chen's identity.
arxiv:2611.31967.authors: Munawar Ali, Qi Feng, Samy Tindel

arxiv:2611.32052.title: Full Support For the Degree-Zero Hitchin Morphism
arxiv:2611.32052.summary: We present a draft argument for the full-support conjecture for the canonical GLn Hitchin morphism in degree zero over a smooth complex projective curve of genus at least two. The whole-base Ng\^o support equality yields a finite necessary classification in terms of weighted products of maximal equigeneric spectral-factor families. We study their generic nodality, develop moving-cycle arguments for arbitrary multiplicities, and give an intersection calculation using generalized parabolic presentations and intrinsic Nash transforms.

arxiv:2611.32058.title: Strong convergence rate for non-autonomous slow-fast SDEs driven by Brownian motions and {\alpha}-stable processes
arxiv:2611.32058.summary: In this paper, we establish a quantitative strong averaging principle for a class of time quasi-periodic slow-fast stochastic differential equations driven by both Brownian motions and multiplicative $\alpha$-stable L\'evy processes. We show that the slow component converges strongly to an autonomous averaged equation with rate $\varepsilon^{\min\{1-1/\alpha_2,\,1/(\nu+2)\}}$, where $\alpha_2\in(1,2)$ is the fast stability index and $\nu$ comes from the quasi-periodic structure. Our strategy is as follows.

arxiv:2611.32079.title: Dissipative Geometric Flows and Certified Phase-Volume Contraction
arxiv:2611.32079.summary: This paper develops an approach to uniform phase-volume contraction for prescribed dynamical systems. The main result is that every positive rate strictly below the invariant-measure bound can be certified in finite search time by a regularized Sobolev gradient flow. The resulting positive density ensures exponential contraction of the weighted phase volume with unit prefactor.

arxiv:2611.32080.title: Chern classes of vanishing cycles for maps having no blowups
arxiv:2611.32080.summary: We study the nearby and vanishing cycles for maps with no blowups. For holomorphic maps between complex manifolds admitting at most ICIS, we show that the Riemann-Hurwitz defect in Chern classes is compensated for by the Chern class transformation of the Milnor number constructible function.

arxiv:2611.32112.title: Contractible 4-Manifolds with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature and Euclidean Volume Growth
arxiv:2611.32112.summary: We prove that every contractible smooth 4-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^4$. More precisely, every compact subset lies in the interior of a connected compact regular domain with simply connected complement. The key construction produces compact domains whose boundaries admit positive scalar curvature and which are regular sublevels of global strictly three-convex Morse exhaustions.

arxiv:2611.32124.title: Rich\'ard Wiegandt's theory of M\"obius products revisited
arxiv:2611.32124.summary: In a 1959 paper Rich\'ard Wiegandt defined a general notion of M\"obius product of functions on arbitrary locally finite posets, and determined when this product is commutative and associative. He gave an example showing that not all locally finite posets allow such a M\"obius product. Here we characterize those posets of height 3 that can be equipped with a commutative and associative M\"obius product.

arxiv:2611.32201.title: The backtrackless circuits of $D(k,q)$ obtained by lifting
arxiv:2611.32201.summary: For integer $k\geq2$ and power $q$ of prime $p$, the algebraic bipartite graph $D(k,q)$, proposed by Lazebnik and Ustimenko in 1993, is $q$-regular, edge-transitive and of girth at least $k+4$. For $q\geq4$, it was conjectured in 1995 that the exact girth of $D(k,q)$, denoted by $g(D(k,q))$, is equal to $g_k$, where $g_k$ is defined as $k+5$ if $2\nmid k$ and as $k+4$ if $2|k$. It is now known that this conjecture is true when $g_k$ is of form $hp^t$, where $h$ is a factor of $4(q-1)$.
arxiv:2611.32201.authors: Xiaoyan Cheng, Chen Zhang, Yuansheng Tang, Ming Xu

arxiv:2611.32249.title: On the bounds of path-unique subgraph of De Bruijn graph
arxiv:2611.32249.summary: The De Bruijn graph is a directed graph G(n, m) such that V = (Zn)m and there is an edge from A to B iff A deletes the first coordinate equals to B deletes the last coordinate. Based on the background of achieving DNA labeling with minimum labels, we consider the De Brujin graph and its path-unique subgraph with maximum edges. Hofmeister gave an estimation of the lower bound and upper bound of the biggest number of the ratio of the edges we can keep in a path-unique subgraph, given the upper bound and lower bound and proved that the limit goes to 1 when n tends to infinity, and a lower bound m+1 2m when m tends to infinity.
arxiv:2611.32249.authors: Jiacheng Cao, Xin Wei, Xiande Zhang

arxiv:2611.32253.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
arxiv:2611.32253.summary: We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras.

arxiv:2611.32267.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
arxiv:2611.32267.summary: We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence.
arxiv:2611.32267.authors: Maciej Ga{\l}\k{a}zka, Jaewoo Jung, Hyunsuk Moon

arxiv:2611.32276.title: Weak oddness to resistance ratios in snarks
arxiv:2611.32276.summary: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. If $G$ is not 3-edge-colourable, we call it a \textit{snark}. The \textit{resistance} of $G$, denoted $r(G)$, is the minimum number of edges which can be removed from $G$ in order to render $G$ 3-edge-colourable.

arxiv:2611.32278.title: Quasiperiodicity breakdown and homoclinic bifurcations in the forced librations of a parametric oscillator
arxiv:2611.32278.summary: Above its instability threshold, a parametrically excited oscillator settles into one of two phase states. The response of these states to a second, much slower modulation of the same stiffness is investigated. In the rotating frame, this modulation periodically varies the detuning and drives the phase librations.

arxiv:2611.32318.title: The Orientable Genus of Generalized Corona Graphs
arxiv:2611.32318.summary: The generalized corona of a graph with a family of graphs, one for each vertex, is obtained by joining every vertex of the base graph to all vertices of its own copy of the corresponding graph; the corona of Frucht and Harary is the case in which all graphs in the family are equal. Each attached copy meets the rest of the graph in a single vertex, so additivity of the orientable genus over blocks reduces the genus of a generalized corona to the genus of the base graph plus the genera of the graphs obtained from the attached graphs by adding a dominating vertex. We study this last quantity through faces that meet every vertex, and we determine it for complete graphs, balanced complete…

arxiv:2611.32339.title: Alexander modules and Milnor fibers of topological line arrangements
arxiv:2611.32339.summary: We study the Alexander module and a distinguished cyclic cover, which we call the \textit{topological Milnor fiber}, of the complements of topological line arrangements. For every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines, where $n$ is not a prime power, we prove that the first Betti numbers of its topological Milnor fibers are unbounded. Moreover, any finite abelian group occurs as a direct summand of the integral homology of a topological Milnor fiber within the given combinatorial type.

arxiv:2611.32354.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
arxiv:2611.32354.summary: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let \((X,B)\) be a projective log canonical pair with \(X\) of Fano type, \(-(K_X+B)\) nef and coefficients of \(B\) in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index.

arxiv:2611.32363.title: Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over $C^{\ast}$-algebras
arxiv:2611.32363.summary: In a recent paper, Tobias Fritz and the second author identified $\sigma C^*$-algebras as a tentative noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces. We advance this analogy by establishing monadicity of $\sigma C^*$-algebras over $C^*$-algebras and proving several results of interest to both the category theory and operator algebra communities. In detail, we show that: - The associated probabilistic morphisms, $\sigma$-cpu maps, admit a description via a comonad closely related to the Giry monad.

arxiv:2611.32366.title: A Sylow reduction for isomorphisms of Cayley graphs on abelian groups of cube-free order
arxiv:2611.32366.summary: The isomorphism problem for Cayley graphs is one of the fundamental problems in algebraic combinatorics. Dobson studied this isomorphism problem and asked whether, assuming that the group generated by the left regular representation and its conjugate under an isomorphism admits a complete sequence of normal block systems, the isomorphism problem for Cayley digraphs on a finite abelian group of cube-free order can be reduced to the corresponding problem on its Sylow subgroups. We answer this question affirmatively.
arxiv:2611.32366.authors: Tingzeng Wu, Liang Qin, Yong Yu, Xing Gao

arxiv:2611.32376.title: A proof of the toughness conjecture for Kneser graphs
arxiv:2611.32376.summary: As a measure of the connectivity of graphs, Chv\'atal \cite{Chvatal} introduced the concept of toughness. For integers $k\geq2$ and $n\geq2k+1$, the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ has all the $k$-subsets of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ as its vertices, and two vertices are adjacent if they are disjoint. Cioab\u{a} and Wong~\cite{CW} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,2)$.

arxiv:2611.32404.title: Noncommutative $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed beta functions of first and second kind : beta gamma relations, shift identities and symmetrisation
arxiv:2611.32404.summary: We develop the theory of the beta functions attached to the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba, for structure functions whose deformed numbers are generated by two deformation functions $\phi_{1}>\phi_{2}>0$. Working with the Jackson type series representation of the deformed integral, we define a first kind beta function on $[0,1]$ from the deformed power $(1\ominus\phi_{2}t)^{y-1}$, extended to complex exponents, and a second kind beta function on the half line from $(1\oplus\phi_{1}t)^{-x-y}$. The first kind function equals $\phi_{1}^{(y-1)(2x+y-2)/2}\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x)\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(y)/\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x+y)$ for all…
arxiv:2611.32404.authors: Kaw\`eyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph D\'esir\'e Bukweli Kyemba

arxiv:2611.32425.title: Three combinatorial identities of the Rogers-Ramanujan type
arxiv:2611.32425.summary: The purpose of the present paper is to establish three combinatorial Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Although their motivation comes from the representation theory of affine Lie algebra of type $A_2^{(2)}$, our proofs are entirely combinatorial and analytic. They follow the automata-theoretic approach introduced by Takigiku and Tsuchioka in their proof of Nandi's conjecture and adapt it to the present setting.
arxiv:2611.32425.authors: Stefano Capparelli, Arne Meurman, Mirko Primc

arxiv:2611.32426.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
arxiv:2611.32426.summary: These lecture notes on o-minimal geometry comprise six chapters: 1 - O minimal Structures. 2 - Cell Decomposition. 3 - Connected Components and Dimension. 4 - Definable Triangulation. 5 - Generic Fibers for Definable Families. 6 - Smoothness.

arxiv:2611.32429.title: Homothetic Copies of Polytopes and Binomial Barcodes
arxiv:2611.32429.summary: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite full-dimensional configuration, and put $F_X(N)=\max_{S\subset\mathbb{R}^d, |S|=N}\#\{(\mathbf{v},\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\infty):\mathbf{v}+\lambda X\subseteq S\}$. Elekes and Erd\H{o}s posed the problem of estimating $F_X(N)$. In this article, we determine its exact value when $X$ is the vertex set of a simplex.

arxiv:2611.32436.title: Trace-defined double covers of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(2^n)$
arxiv:2611.32436.summary: For $q=2^n\ge 4$, we construct a family of Deza double covers $\Gamma(q,\xi)$ of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(q)$, parametrized by $\xi\in\mathbb F_q^*$. We show that each resulting cover is connected, arc-transitive and amply regular with parameters $(2(q^2-1),q,Tr(\xi),1)$, where $Tr$ denotes the absolute trace. We also show that the trace-one covers are antipodal of diameter $5$ and girth $3$, whereas the trace-zero covers are non-antipodal of diameter $3$ and girth $5$.
arxiv:2611.32436.authors: G. A. Glinskikh, L. Yu. Tsiovkina

arxiv:2611.32454.title: Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras
arxiv:2611.32454.summary: We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). A unified linear system yields explicit matrix parametrizations and the dimensions of both homogeneous components of the derivation superalgebra. The results are given in block-matrix form.
arxiv:2611.32454.authors: Muratova Kh. A., Tyan M. D

arxiv:2611.32460.title: Counting tree-child and reticulation visible networks
arxiv:2611.32460.summary: For tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulations, we identify an entire critical scaling function at $k=x\sqrt n$ and its first uniform correction. The function is a Gaussian factor times the Laplace transform of Brownian excursion area. An exact coefficient integral then yields the explicit amplitude $\pi\Ai'(a_1)$ for the maximal-reticulation count, where $a_1$ is the largest negative Airy zero, together with three logarithmic corrections.

arxiv:2611.32465.title: A sharp form of Welsh's log-concavity inequality for chromatic polynomials
arxiv:2611.32465.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge 1$, and let $P_G(x)$ be its chromatic polynomial. In the early 1970s, Welsh conjectured that $P_G(k)^2 \ge P_G(k-1)P_G(k+1)$ holds for any positive integer $k$. This conjecture was also independently proposed by Brenti in 1992, while in 1997, Seymour disproved it for $k=6$ by constructing an infinite family of graphs of sufficiently large order as counterexamples.

arxiv:2611.32469.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
arxiv:2611.32469.summary: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.

arxiv:2611.32494.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
arxiv:2611.32494.summary: For a finite group acting on a smooth projective separably rationally connected variety over an algebraically closed field, we prove that the rational quotient map induces a surjection from the coinvariants of its second Kato homology onto the second Kato homology of any smooth projective quotient model (with coefficients invertible in the ground field). The integral Hodge and Tate conjectures for one-cycles consequently descend to such quotient models. The proof uses weak approximation over function fields to retain the image of a smooth fiber in the total space.

arxiv:2611.32507.title: Steiner porism and boundary value problems
arxiv:2611.32507.summary: The aim of this paper is to describe several interpretations of Steiner chains of circles in terms of certain boundary value problems and give a short review of related results. Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We also mention a few feasible problems and generalizations suggested by the constructions and considerations presented in the paper.

arxiv:2611.32512.title: Characterizing $2$-slices over finite groups
arxiv:2611.32512.summary: For a finite group $G$, we characterize the $2$-slices of $G$-spectra in the regular slice filtration in terms of their homotopy Mackey functors and $k$-invariant. We explicitly compute this for cyclic $p$-groups and the alternating group $A_4$.

arxiv:2611.32528.title: The Min-Cut Formulation of Ollivier-Ricci Curvature
arxiv:2611.32528.summary: Computing Ollivier-Ricci curvature normally requires a local distance matrix and a linear program per edge, prompting workarounds based on entropic regularization or combinatorial proxies. We show that exact curvature needs neither. For any one-step measures, the Kantorovich dual has an integral three-level optimum, reducing each edge to one minimum s-t cut on a distance-free network linear in the read adjacency lists.

arxiv:2611.32555.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
arxiv:2611.32555.summary: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $\omega\in \Omega_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$.

arxiv:2611.32557.title: A Proof of the Balister-Gy\H{o}ri-Schelp Conjecture on Perfect Matchings with Prescribed Differences
arxiv:2611.32557.summary: We prove the conjecture of Balister, Gy\H{o}ri and Schelp on perfect matchings with prescribed differences. Let $n\ge 2$ and let $d_1,\dots,d_{2^{n-1}}$ be nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, with repetitions allowed. The space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ can be partitioned into pairs $\{x_i,y_i\}$ with $x_i+y_i=d_i$ for every $i$ if and only if $\sum_i d_i=0$.

arxiv:2611.32559.title: On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints
arxiv:2611.32559.summary: Global rigidity asks whether a realisation of a graph is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean congruence, by its edge lengths. In this paper, we study global rigidity of bar-joint frameworks under finite point-group symmetry constraints. A framework is called forced-symmetric globally rigid in $d$-space if every realisation of the graph in $\mathbb R^d$ with the same edge lengths and the same prescribed symmetry is congruent to it.
arxiv:2611.32559.authors: James Cruickshank, Csaba Kir\'aly, Bernd Schulze, Shin-ichi Tanigawa

arxiv:2611.32567.title: Irreducibility, inertia and invertibility of the eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs
arxiv:2611.32567.summary: The eccentricity matrix of a connected graph $G$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}(G)$, is obtained from the distance matrix of $G$ by keeping each entry that is the largest in its row or the largest in its column, and replacing all other entries by $0$. The eigenvalues of $\mathcal{E}(G)$ are called the $\mathcal{E}$-eigenvalues of $G$. In this article, we consider the eccentricity matrix of unicyclic graphs and study its various spectral properties.

arxiv:2611.32570.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
arxiv:2611.32570.summary: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties.
arxiv:2611.32570.authors: Sungyoon Cho, Qiao He, Chul-hee Lee, Zhiyu Zhang

arxiv:2611.32571.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
arxiv:2611.32571.summary: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$.

arxiv:2611.32594.title: On some off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey problems
arxiv:2611.32594.summary: We give a new short proof of a theorem of Fox and He that the $3$-uniform Ramsey number $r_3(K_4^-, K_n)$ is at least $2^{\Omega(n \log n)}$. The construction exploits a new connection with a directed graph recently introduced by Brada\v{c} in his work on off-diagonal graph Ramsey numbers. Moreover, it generalizes naturally to give sharp bounds for several extensions of this problem in higher uniformity, answering questions raised by Mubayi and Suk.

arxiv:2611.32597.title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
arxiv:2611.32597.summary: This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling.

arxiv:2611.32607.title: Sparse Additive Spanners and the Cost Spectra of Group Actions
arxiv:2611.32607.summary: How sparse can a Cayley graph become if we retain all its vertices and allow distances to increase by at most a fixed additive constant? We study invariant random spanning subgraphs, measuring sparsity by the expected degree at a vertex. On the square grid, a random translate of a sparse mesh brings the mean degree arbitrarily close to two.

arxiv:2611.32648.title: Twisted Poincar\'e series at zero on surfaces
arxiv:2611.32648.summary: Let $(\Sigma,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $\Sigma$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in \Sigma$, $\rho \in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincar\'e series $s \mapsto \eta_{g,\rho,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincar\'e series does not vanish at zero.
arxiv:2611.32648.authors: Tristan Humbert, Thibault Lefeuvre, Sebasti\'an Mu\~noz-Thon, Zhongkai Tao

arxiv:2611.32655.title: One monoid to realize them all: a master monoid for homotopy types
arxiv:2611.32655.summary: Homotopy theory has traditionally been approached either through topological spaces or through categories of presheaves on suitable combinatorial categories, a perspective subsumed by Grothendieck's theory of test categories. In this paper, we develop a more algebraic viewpoint: homotopy types can be represented by actions of a single monoid on sets. This monoid is obtained by identifying all the objects of the semisimplicial category while retaining its face operators.

arxiv:2611.32669.title: Erd\H{o}s Distance Results for $k$-Degenerate Graphs with $m$ Edges
arxiv:2611.32669.summary: The Erd\H{o}s distinct distances problem asks how many distinct distances $N$ points must determine. In the plane, Guth and Katz determined the optimal power of $N$. A natural generalization fixes a finite graph $G$ with $m$ edges and records, over all injective embeddings of $G$ into a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, the vectors of edge-lengths realized; we write $\Delta_G^\circ(P)$ for this set of edge-distance vectors.
arxiv:2611.32669.authors: Luv Barnwal, Yuda Chen, Eon Lee, Eyvindur Palsson, Braiden Pulver, Steven Senger

arxiv:2611.32673.title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
arxiv:2611.32673.summary: We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs. For two-photon sources, the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4.

arxiv:2611.32684.title: Schnyder Woods and the Chromatic Polynomial
arxiv:2611.32684.summary: Let $\chi_G(q)$ be the chromatic polynomial of a graph $G$. Analogous to the classical results of Greene and Zaslavsky interpreting $(-1)^{n-1}\chi_G'(0)$ and $(-1)^n\chi_G'(1)$ as counting certain orientations of $G$, we show that if $G$ is a triangulation, $\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n-1}\chi_G'(2)$ counts the number of Schnyder woods on a plane embedding of $G$. We also generalise this result to graphs obtained by removing certain edges of $G$.

arxiv:2611.32711.title: A Classification of Trees Without Unique Subgraphs
arxiv:2611.32711.summary: We study trees without unique subgraphs, in both the induced and non-induced settings. Graphs without unique induced subgraphs, called anchor-free graphs, form a natural candidate class for counterexamples to the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture, but their structure remains poorly understood. We develop a framework for studying anchor-free graphs based on a covering lemma that characterizes anchor-freeness via induced subgraph coverings of vertices.

arxiv:2611.32717.title: Temporal Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
arxiv:2611.32717.summary: Motivated by the study of time-dependent propagation processes in inhomogeneous populations, we extend Burova, Lugosi and Perarnau's results on the temporal stochastic block model to graphon-based random graphs with a continuous and strictly positive kernel. We consider such a graph in the regime where connection probabilities are of the order of $\log n/n$, and equip its edges with a uniformly random ordering, interpreted as timestamps. We study the size of reachable sets via increasing paths (that is, paths whose edge timestamps are strictly increasing).

arxiv:2611.32721.title: Quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory
arxiv:2611.32721.summary: We study quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. This allows to generalise Friedlander's formula for the homotopy fibre of geometric fibrations to the case of an arbitrary qcqs base scheme that is not necessarily normal. Among the applications to geometric fibrations are (1) specialisation is an equivalence on the pro-$\Sigma$ completed profinite \'etale homotopy types of geometric fibres, (2) a long exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in characteristic 0, and (3) a partially $\Sigma$-completed exact sequence of \'etale…
arxiv:2611.32721.authors: Tim Holzschuh, Alexander Schmidt, Jakob Stix

arxiv:2611.32730.title: A degree-sum condition for paths through prescribed vertices
arxiv:2611.32730.summary: Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and let $S\subseteq V(G)$. Denote by $\kappa(S)$ the minimum size of a vertex set separating two vertices of $S$, and by $\sigma_p(S)$ the minimum degree sum over all independent sets of $p$ vertices in $S$. We prove that if $\kappa(S)\ge k\ge2$ and $\sigma_p(S)\ge n+(p-1)^2$ for every integer $p\ge k$, then any two distinct vertices of $S$ are joined by a path containing all vertices of $S$.

arxiv:2611.32733.title: On the generalized foliated cone theorem of rank one
arxiv:2611.32733.summary: We prove the cone theorem for generalized foliated quadruples of rank one in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of MMP outputs for log canonical generalized foliated quadruples of rank one.

arxiv:2611.32740.title: Fluctuations in the k-cut numbers of random recursive trees
arxiv:2611.32740.summary: We consider the k-cut procedure introduced by Cai et al. [EJP, 2018] on random recursive trees. Our main result identifies the fluctuations in the number of cuts required to isolate the root as the tree size tends to infinity. This extends the results by Drmota et al. [RSA, 2009] and Iksanov et al. [ECP, 2007] for the classical cutting procedure.
arxiv:2611.32740.authors: Laura Eslava, Marco L. Ortiz, Minmin Wang

arxiv:2611.32744.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
arxiv:2611.32744.summary: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family.

arxiv:2611.32746.title: The majority game chromatic number for dense random graphs
arxiv:2611.32746.summary: We show that for every fixed $2/3<p<1$ the majority game chromatic number of the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph $G_{n,p}$ is $3$ with high probability.
arxiv:2611.32746.authors: Stijn Cambie, Annika Heckel, Brahadeesh Sankarnarayanan, Gabri\"elle Zwaneveld

arxiv:2611.32752.title: Line bundles on regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
arxiv:2611.32752.summary: Let $G$ be a connected simply-connected simple algebraic group over $\mathbb{C}$ and $B$ be a Borel subgroup of $G$. Let $Y$ be an irreducible regular semisimple Hessenberg variety in $G/B$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the natural restriction map $\mathrm{res}: \mathrm{Pic}(G/B)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pic}(Y)$ of Picard groups induced by the inclusion $Y\subseteq G/B$ to be an isomorphism.

arxiv:2611.32763.title: An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture
arxiv:2611.32763.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. A subgraph $H$ of $G$ is \emph{$\Delta$-overfull} if $|E(H)|>\Delta\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. The Overfull Conjecture, proposed by Chetwynd and Hilton in 1986, states that a graph $G$ with $\Delta>|V(G)|/3$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $\Delta$-overfull subgraph.

arxiv:2611.32767.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
arxiv:2611.32767.summary: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of K\"ahler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.

arxiv:2611.32771.title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle
arxiv:2611.32771.summary: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.

arxiv:2611.32794.title: Spanning cyclability of split graphs
arxiv:2611.32794.summary: For a positive integer $k$, a graph $G$ is called $k$-spanning cyclable (resp. $k$-edge spanning cyclable) if, given any $k$ distinct vertices $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_k$ (resp. $k$ independent edges $e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_k$) of $G$, there exist $k$ vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k$ in $G$ such that $v_i \in V(C_i)$ (resp.
arxiv:2611.32794.authors: Jingfan Zai, Wenjing Lv, Eminjan Sabir

arxiv:2611.32833.title: Even Quartets and the Maximum Density of a Simplical 3-Cocycle
arxiv:2611.32833.summary: Colour the triples of an $n$-element set red or blue, and call a four-set even if it contains an even number of red triples. We prove that the minimum number of even four-sets is $\frac5{16}\binom n4-\Theta(n^3)$. In particular, the maximum asymptotic density of a simplicial $3$-cocycle over the field of two elements is $11/16$.

arxiv:2611.32836.title: Patterson-Sullivan Theory for Approximate Groups
arxiv:2611.32836.summary: In this paper we consider the limit set of a uniformly discrete approximate subgroup acting on a negatively curved manifold, and prove several properties comparable to that of the classical case of discrete groups, including a version of the dichotomy between elementary and non-elementary groups. Furthermore, we adapt the Patterson-Sullivan construction for discrete groups to obtain asymptotic counting results for the orbits of infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on a negatively curved manifold.

arxiv:2611.32845.title: ab-indices for lattice path matroids
arxiv:2611.32845.summary: The base polytopes of connected lattice path matroids admit subdivisions into snakes. We use these to obtain an explicit positive combinatorial description of their ab-indices, their Chow polynomials and their chain polynomials. We finally apply this description to the particular case of the ab-index of Schubert matroids.
arxiv:2611.32845.authors: Cenk Aydin, Giovanni Caiolo, Chiara Giardino, Mara Gru{\ss}, Mikael H\"aglund, Elena Hoster, Christian Stump

arxiv:2611.32872.title: A short proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture
arxiv:2611.32872.summary: We give a short alternative proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture, recently proved by OpenAI. Our proof combines their reduction with a different argument showing that every nontrivial oriented graph $G$ contains a nonempty set $X$ such that $X^+\ne V(G)$ and $|(X^+)^+\setminus X^+|\geq|X^+\setminus X|$, where $X^+=N_G^+[X]$.
arxiv:2611.32872.authors: Romain Bourneuf, Pierre Charbit, Samuel Coulomb, St\'ephan Thomass\'e

arxiv:2611.32875.title: Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties
arxiv:2611.32875.summary: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents.

arxiv:2611.32879.title: Convexification effects of $L_p$-sums
arxiv:2611.32879.summary: It is a classical result, quantified by Shapley, Folkman, and Starr, that the Minkowski averages of any compact set asymptotically approach its convex hull in the Hausdorff metric. In this paper, we investigate the analogous convexification phenomenon for the Firey $L_p$-sums of compact sets. First, we establish new structural properties of the $L_p$-sum.
arxiv:2611.32879.authors: Matthieu Fradelizi, Auttawich Manui, Mark Meyer, Maud Szusterman, Artem Zvavitch

arxiv:2611.32880.title: Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems
arxiv:2611.32880.summary: Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.

arxiv:2611.32912.title: Elimination Methods for Computing Invariant Algebraic Surfaces and Hopf Bifurcations
arxiv:2611.32912.summary: This paper presents efficient algorithmic methods for computing invariant algebraic surfaces and Hopf bifurcations in parametric polynomial differential systems. For invariant algebraic surfaces of bounded degree, we establish two complementary elimination frameworks: combining Gr\"obner bases with saturation and prime decomposition yields the Zariski closure of the parameter existence locus (necessary conditions), whereas triangular decomposition into strong regular systems recovers the exact pointwise constructible locus (necessary and sufficient conditions) via the projection property. We further present a hybrid approach for identifying such surfaces by integrating prime decomposition…
arxiv:2611.32912.authors: Changbo Chen, Bo Huang, Valery Romanovski, Linpeng Wang

arxiv:2611.32921.title: Analytic properties of Boolean-Narayana numbers
arxiv:2611.32921.summary: Very recently, B\'ona introduced the Boolean-Narayana numbers BoNa(n,k) as the number of 0-1-trees on n+1 vertices with k right edges. We prove the total positivity of the Boolean-Narayana triangle by providing an explicit matrix factorization, and construct a planar digraph for this triangle. We give two combinatorial interpretations of the gamma-coefficients of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials.

arxiv:2611.32956.title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
arxiv:2611.32956.summary: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Pl\"ucker divisors. For the full Pl\"ucker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields.

arxiv:2611.32965.title: Boomerang identities and binomial transform
arxiv:2611.32965.summary: In Pascal's triangle, the boomerang identities, which were recently introduced, combine and extend the well-known hockey-stick identities of the binomial coefficients by allowing additional terms. We show that the binomial transform of sequences in a ring play a central role in this context. Subsequently, we show several applications to Bell and Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Appell polynomials, as well as, to harmonic, Fibonacci, Lucas, and Stirling numbers.

arxiv:2611.32976.title: Traversing hyperplane arrangements with an affine objective
arxiv:2611.32976.summary: We give geometric constructions of directed acyclic graphs on the chambers of a locally finite affine hyperplane arrangement. Fix a nonconstant affine objective. At each chamber where it is bounded above, a choice of flag based at the optimal face determines $2^r-1$ outgoing edges, where $r$ is the codimension of that face.

arxiv:2611.32999.title: Triangle-free planar graphs need not be POSH
arxiv:2611.32999.summary: We show that a triangle-free planar graph need not be partial one-sided Hamiltonian. This disproves a conjecture of Felsner, Schrezenmaier, Schr\"oder and Steiner.

arxiv:2611.33025.title: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
arxiv:2611.33025.summary: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant.
arxiv:2611.33025.authors: Margaret H. Regan, Frank Sottile, Simon Telen

arxiv:2611.33046.title: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Ap\'ery spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
arxiv:2611.33046.summary: For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return.

arxiv:2611.33066.title: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
arxiv:2611.33066.summary: We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones.
arxiv:2611.33066.authors: Peter Jipsen, Erkko Lehtonen, Reinhard P\"oschel

arxiv:2611.33084.title: One-Relator Products of Left-Orderable Groups
arxiv:2611.33084.summary: We prove that, for left-orderable groups $A,B$ and a word $w\in A*B$ which is not conjugate into $A$ or $B$ and is not a proper power, the one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ is torsion-free, answering a question posed by Chen and Lodha. We do this by proving a relative asphericity result for the one-relator product. We also generalise the B.
arxiv:2611.33084.authors: Alba Gonz\'alez, Tejas Mittal, Andrew Wood

arxiv:2611.33087.title: The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation
arxiv:2611.33087.summary: How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\to\rho\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-\rho)/(2-\rho)$.

arxiv:2611.33107.title: An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
arxiv:2611.33107.summary: We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets.

arxiv:2611.33108.title: Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.33108.summary: Let \(k\ge2\), let \(H\) be a fixed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph on \(h\) vertices with at least one edge, and let \(a>0\). We prove that every sufficiently large \(n\)-vertex \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with at least \(a n^h\) copies of \(H\) contains a blow-up of \(H\) with at least \(b(\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) vertices in each part, where \(b=b(H,a)>0\). The exponent of $\log n$ is best possible.

arxiv:2611.33113.title: Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle
