arxiv:2611.33113.summary: We explore the Koszul resolutions of a family of ideals, each generated by multivariate polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The motivating examples come from the game Permutation Wordle of Kutin and Smithline, as analyzed by Kutin, Smithline, and Vatter, and an open question, Conjecture 4.5 in Kutin and Smithline's work on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. For each ideal in this family, with our chosen generators, the Koszul differentials are strict for the max-degree filtration and, more generally, at every multidegree whose coordinates form a set of consecutive integers.

arxiv:2611.33120.title: Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting
arxiv:2611.33120.summary: We consider reconfigurations of integer assignments to planar lattice regions that preserve specified line totals, which are motivated by questions of combinatorial construction, algorithmic sampling and approximate counting. An elementary prototype is provided by contingency tables, i.e. two-dimensional grids of non-negative integers with prescribed row and column sums, which can be reconfigured by basic switches of the form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. More difficult combinatorial instances include reconfiguration of Latin squares or queens configurations.

arxiv:2611.33125.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
arxiv:2611.33125.summary: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions.

arxiv:2611.33127.title: Winning and losing NoGo is PSPACE-complete
arxiv:2611.33127.summary: We resolve an open problem of Burke and Hearn and show that the combinatorial game NoGo is PSPACE-complete on grids. This is the usual geometry the game is played on, including at the tournament at a 2011 Banff workshop. In addition to this result, we show that it is also PSPACE-complete under mis\`ere play on grids.
arxiv:2611.33127.authors: Kyle Burke, Alfie Davies, Craig Tennenhouse

arxiv:2611.33136.title: A canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem
arxiv:2611.33136.summary: In this note, we prove a canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem: for any finite set of points $S\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, any colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a scaled (and possibly rotated) copy of $S$ that is either monochromatic or rainbow.

arxiv:2611.33152.title: Abelian envelopes and quantum groups in Knop's interpolation categories
arxiv:2611.33152.summary: We show the existence of abelian envelopes for large classes of subcategories of Knop's tensor envelopes. It follows that these abelian envelopes correspond to groups or more generally Hopf algebras (``quantum groups'') in their parent interpolation categories. As a special case, we obtain that the interpolation categories in the sense of Flake--Maassen (2022) of all so-called group-theoretical easy quantum groups have abelian envelopes given by quantum groups in Deligne's interpolation category of the symmetric groups.

arxiv:2611.33154.title: Dominoes tiling a common figure
arxiv:2611.33154.summary: Call a two-element subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ a domino. Given finitely many dominoes $D_1,\ldots,D_k$, we show that there exists a finite non-empty $B\subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $B$ can be partitioned into disjoint translates of $D_i$ for all $i$. The proof uses a new absorption mechanism for perfect matchings in algebraically defined hypergraphs.

arxiv:2611.33191.title: On a Problem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham Related to Restricted Order
arxiv:2611.33191.summary: Let $A$ be a set of nonnegative integers. We prove that if $A\setminus F$ has a finite order for every finite subset $F\subseteq A$, then $A$ has finite restricted order. This resolves a problem posed by Erd\H{o}s and Graham in 1980.
arxiv:2611.33191.authors: Shi-Qiang Chen, Quan-Hui Yang, Lilu Zhao

arxiv:2611.33205.title: Multiplicativity of Vertex Energy Under the Kronecker Product
arxiv:2611.33205.summary: We prove that vertex energy is multiplicative under the Kronecker product. Using this core property, we introduce a unified theorem to compute vertex energies for any graph operation obtained through the Kronecker product. As direct applications, we derive exact vertex energy formulas for semishadow, generalized splitting, and shadow-splitting graphs.
arxiv:2611.33205.authors: Ronak B Dudhat, Vinodray J Kaneria, Kalpesh M Popat

arxiv:2611.33209.title: Besicovitch Pseudo Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes and Their Applications to Delayed Stochastic Neural Networks
arxiv:2611.33209.summary: The Besicovitch almost periodic concept is a generalization of the Bohr, Stepanov, and Weyl almost periodic concepts and, in a certain sense, has broader coverage and weaker conditions. However, the concept of pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes in the Besicovitch sense has not yet been systematically proposed, which limits the characterization of the complex oscillatory behavior of a broader class of stochastic non-autonomous systems. This paper proposes the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes.
arxiv:2611.33209.authors: Yongkun Li, Yuwei Cao, Bing Li

arxiv:2611.33212.title: Constructions and Upper Bounds for Trifferent Codes
arxiv:2611.33212.summary: A ternary code of blocklength $n$ is trifferent if every three distinct codewords have a coordinate at which they take all three values. Let $T(n)$ be the largest size of such a code. We prove that $T(n)=\Omega(1.162579^n)$ and $T(n)=O(n^{-1/2}(3/2)^n)$.

arxiv:2611.33216.title: Semisimple-Unipotent Decomposition and the Exact Order of a Linear Cellular Automaton over F_2
arxiv:2611.33216.summary: We study the linear cellular automaton on the cyclic graph $C_n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by the local rule $v_i(t+1)=v_{i-1}(t)\oplus v_i(t)\oplus v_{i+1}(t)$ (Wolfram's Rule 150 under periodic boundary conditions). Identifying the configuration space $V_n=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $R_n = \mathbb{F}_2[x] / \langle x^n - 1 \rangle$, the evolution operator corresponds to multiplication by $G(x)=1+x+x^{n-1}$. We re-derive the invertibility criterion $3\nmid n$, classify periodic and transient behaviour, and prove that Hamming weight is non-monotone for every $n\ge3$.

arxiv:2611.33222.title: Syringe reuse in HCV transmission among people who inject drugs: behavioral thresholds and optimal control
arxiv:2611.33222.summary: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) transmission among people who inject drugs (PWID) is driven largely by syringe sharing and reuse, yet existing models rarely treat reuse as a behavior that individuals adopt and abandon. In this work, we develop and analyze a four-compartment epidemic model that explicitly incorporates syringe reuse as a distinct behavioral process, introducing a high-risk susceptible subgroup that acquires infection through both direct contact and syringe-mediated transmission. We establish the well-posedness and biological feasibility of the model, derive the basic reproduction number, and analyze the existence and stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria along with…
arxiv:2611.33222.authors: Mohammad Zaman, Emel Khan, Ishfaq Ahmad, Hiromi Seno

arxiv:2611.33230.title: Cyclicity of period annuli of quadratic codimension four centers
arxiv:2611.33230.summary: Quadratic systems with a center fall into four classes: Hamiltonian $Q_3^H$, reversible $Q_3^R$, generalized Lotka--Volterra $Q_3^{LV}$, and codimension-four $Q_4$. Before this work, the cyclicity of period annuli under quadratic perturbations had been completely determined for $Q_3^H$, whereas only certain special cases had been resolved for $Q_3^R$, $Q_3^{LV}$ and $Q_4$. In this paper, we establish that the period annulus of every center in $Q_4$ has cyclicity three under quadratic perturbations, thereby proving \.{Z}o{\l}{\k{a}}dek's 1994 conjecture for this class.

arxiv:2611.33233.title: The smallest vertex triangle in a fixed polygon
arxiv:2611.33233.summary: Among the triangles determined by $n$ points in convex position in the unit square, one has area at most $32/n^3$. Equality is possible exactly when $4$ divides $n$, and then the maximizing point set is unique. We prove a fixed-container theorem for a class of convex $s$-gons that includes affinely regular polygons and a one-parameter family of pairwise affinely inequivalent hexagons without a centre of symmetry.

arxiv:2611.33253.title: The regular polygon maximizes the first positive Steklov eigenvalue among simple polygons at fixed area
arxiv:2611.33253.summary: For $N\ge5$ and every simple planar polygon $P$ with at most $N$ sides, $\sqrt{|P|}\,\sigma_1(P)\le\sqrt{|R_N|}\,\sigma_1(R_N)$, where $\sigma_1$ is the first positive Steklov eigenvalue and $R_N$ is a regular $N$-gon. Equality holds precisely for polygons similar to $R_N$. This answers Oudet's fixed-area open problem \cite{AIM} for all $N\ge5$.

arxiv:2611.33310.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
arxiv:2611.33310.summary: We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras. Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras.

arxiv:2611.33320.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
arxiv:2611.33320.summary: We prove Mosher's Transverse Finiteness Conjecture, posed in 1996. This states that every taut, finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows, up to orbit equivalence. Our strategy is to organize the flows that are almost transverse to $\mathcal F$ using their associated universal circles.
arxiv:2611.33320.authors: Michael P. Landry, Samuel J. Taylor

arxiv:2611.33321.title: Kov\'acs Vanishing for Excellent Log Canonical Threefolds
arxiv:2611.33321.summary: We prove a vanishing theorem of S. Kov\'acs for excellent log canonical threefolds whose closed points have perfect residue fields of sufficiently large characteristic. This vanishing theorem roughly says that LC threefold pairs are not far from being rational pairs (in the sense of Koll\'ar \& Kov\'acs and Schwede \& Takagi) if one includes a correction term.

arxiv:2611.33355.title: Graphs with the largest chainable index and their properties
arxiv:2611.33355.summary: This paper provides a complete characterization of the set of graphs with the largest chainable index. In particular, it is shown that the number of arcs and vertex degrees of such graphs satisfy strong restrictions. Moreover, graphs with the largest chainable index form five parametric families, and exactly one of them consists of graphs that are not strongly connected.
arxiv:2611.33355.authors: Alexander Guterman, Svetlana Zhilina, Evgenii Shafeev

arxiv:2611.33366.title: Nash-Williams' Orientation Theorems for Infinite Graphs
arxiv:2611.33366.summary: Nash-Williams proved in 1960 that every finite multigraph has a \emph{well-balanced} orientation: for all vertices $x$ and $y$, the maximum number of arc-disjoint directed paths from $x$ to $y$ is at least half, rounded down, of the maximum number of edge-disjoint $x$--$y$ paths. In particular every finite $2k$-edge-connected multigraph has a $k$-arc-connected orientation. He announced an extension to infinite graphs whose details, as far as is known, never appeared, and the two statements for infinite graphs have since been known as the strong and the weak orientation conjecture of Nash-Williams.
arxiv:2611.33366.authors: Amena Assem, Mohammad A. Mahmoud, Bobby Miraftab

arxiv:2611.33372.title: The generalized Segal conjecture and the coalgebraic Frobenius
arxiv:2611.33372.summary: We prove the generalized Segal conjecture, extending work of Bergsaker and Rognes and confirming a conjecture by the author: for every finite group $G$ and every bounded-below spectrum $X$, the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm $N_e^G X$ becomes Borel-complete after completion at the augmentation ideal of the Burnside ring. Equivalently, for every non-trivial finite $p$-group $G$, the proper Tate diagonal $X\to(X^{\otimes G})^{\varphi G}$ is a $p$-completion. The proof reduces to the case $X=\Fp$, established by Bergsaker and Rognes, and removes the finiteness hypotheses from their theorem by abstract manipulations.

arxiv:2611.33418.title: Gerbe-corrected stringy E-functions
arxiv:2611.33418.summary: We define an invariant of $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein complex varieties with at worst log-terminal singularities equipped with a rational Brauer class $\alpha$ that generalizes existing versions of the $\alpha$-corrected stringy $E$-polynomial, which are defined only for quotients of quasi-projective varieties by finite groups. Using recent results from $p$-adic integration, this new invariant can be shown to behave well for degenerate dual abelian fibrations and to agree with the intersection or BPS $E$-polynomial for certain moduli problems.

arxiv:2611.33423.title: From random intersection to spatial graphs: a unified asymptotic framework
arxiv:2611.33423.summary: Random intersection graphs and spatial random graphs provide different mechanisms for generating edges and clustering. We investigate their interplay through geometric random intersection graphs, where vertices are adjacent whenever they share a spatially located group. First, a Poisson decomposition by attachment sets yields exact subgraph probabilities and laws of large numbers for connected subgraph densities.
arxiv:2611.33423.authors: Alessandra Bianchi, Alberto De Nicol\`o, Riccardo Michielan

arxiv:2611.33427.title: Graceful Colorings for Random Graphs
arxiv:2611.33427.summary: Given a vertex coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$, the graceful induced edge labeling is the induced edge coloring $c'(uv):=|c(u)-c(v)|$. A vertex coloring $c$ is a \textbf{graceful coloring} if $c$ is a proper vertex coloring and $c'$ is a proper edge coloring. The graceful coloring number $\chi_g(G)$ is the least $k$ such that there exists a graceful coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$.
arxiv:2611.33427.authors: Sean English, Edward Janosko, Erik Slivken, Sid Touzeau

arxiv:2611.33449.title: Quantifying combined rate- and noise-induced transitions in a multiscale system
arxiv:2611.33449.summary: Excitations in multiscale dynamical systems produce persistent but impermanent excursions away from a quiescent state. A novel mechanism for inducing excitations, through a combination of rate-dependent parametric and stochastic forcing, is discussed using the FitzHugh-Nagumo model as an example. In the absence of noise, a quasithreshold separating the state space between supercritical and subcritical behaviour is defined with respect to slow manifolds associated with the metastable excited state.
arxiv:2611.33449.authors: Ryan Deeley, Peter Ashwin, Ulrike Feudel

arxiv:2611.33463.title: Global dynamics of impulsive reaction-diffusion systems with asymptotically unbounded domain
arxiv:2611.33463.summary: This paper is devoted to the study of the global dynamics of continuous-discrete hybrid population models with an asymptotically unbounded domain. We first prove a global attractivity result for a class of impulsive reaction-diffusion equations whose diffusion coefficients vanish asymptotically. A cut-off function is combined with an auxiliary impulsive kinetic system to construct a subsolution that is compatible with the birth update at every cycle.

arxiv:2611.33477.title: On the non existence of minimal non-uniquely ergodic 4-IETs with flips
arxiv:2611.33477.summary: The existence of minimal non uniquely ergodic oriented IETs of n intervals requires that n>= 4 by Th. 2.12 from (W. A. Veech, Interval exchange transformations, J.
arxiv:2611.33477.authors: Antonio Linero Bas, Gabriel Soler L\'opez

arxiv:2611.33485.title: Fast Algorithms for Permanents of Permutationally-Dominant Matrices
arxiv:2611.33485.summary: We establish a fast algorithm for approximating the permanent of permutationally-dominant matrices. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial randomised approximation scheme whose runtime is quadratic in both the dimension of the matrix and the inverse of the approximation error. Our approach is based on a polymer model representation of the permanent and importance sampling of the logarithm of its partition function via the theory of heaps of pieces of Viennot.

arxiv:2611.33491.title: Primitive Collections for Klyachko Varieties
arxiv:2611.33491.summary: Klyachko introduced a family of $S_m\times S_n$-invariant toric Gorenstein Fano varieties, $X_{mn}$, with connections to representation theory, algebraic groups, and graph theory. He focused on the case in which $m$ and $n$ are coprime, for which $X_{mn}$ are smooth, and hence Fano. Klyachko and Voskresenskii later proved that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are stably rational when $m, n$ are coprime, and that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are rational when $n$ is congruent to 1 modulo $m$.

arxiv:2611.33494.title: On the Cluster Duration Distribution of the Markovian Hawkes Process
arxiv:2611.33494.summary: The duration of a Hawkes process cluster, meaning the time from first point to last point in an entirely endogenously generated progeny stream, has been stubbornly resistant to analysis; even the mean has not been known in closed form. Recently, uniformly random parking functions have been found to be hidden spines of these history-driven clusters, offering a probabilistic combinatorial structure within self-excitement that has opened new avenues for analysis. Here, we leverage and refine this decomposition to provide a closed-form expression for the mean cluster duration in the case of an exponential excitation kernel.

arxiv:2611.33500.title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
arxiv:2611.33500.summary: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.

arxiv:2611.33501.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
arxiv:2611.33501.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one edge, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal over a field $K$. We prove that if $G$ is gap-free, then $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q=\max\{2q,\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)+q-1\}$ for all $q\geq 1$. This answers both open problems of Nevo and Peeva on ordinary powers: $I(G)^q$ has a linear resolution exactly when $q\geq \mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, and their proposed regularity recurrence holds with equality.

arxiv:2611.33512.title: The squared antipode of a twisted function algebra is locally unipotent
arxiv:2611.33512.summary: Let $G$ be a proalgebraic group over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $F:{\rm Rep}(G)\to {\rm Vect}(k)$ be a dimension-preserving tensor functor, possibly nonsymmetric. We prove that a tensor automorphism $T$ of $F$ is locally unipotent if and only if its trace on $F(V)$ equals ${\rm dim} V$ for every $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$. Applied to the Drinfeld element of a dual twisted function algebra $(\mathcal{O}(G)^J)^*$, this proves our conjecture from 2000 that the square of the antipode in $\mathcal{O}(G)^J$ is locally unipotent (arXiv:0002128).

arxiv:2611.33516.title: Linear images of graphs of vector-valued affine fractal interpolation functions
arxiv:2611.33516.summary: We determine the Hausdorff and box dimensions of every linear image of the graph of a vector-valued affine fractal interpolation function with positive vertical factors. The same formula holds for signed factors under a rank condition on the active branches. Outside an explicit finite union of hyperplanes in the space of vertical factors it holds simultaneously for all choices of interpolation knots and all linear images.

arxiv:2611.33518.title: Singular rational S-functions of second-order ODEs: structure, degree bounds and a Kovacic-type search
arxiv:2611.33518.summary: For a rational second-order ODE $y''=phi(x,y,y')$, the $S$-function method reduces the search for a first integral to finding a rational solution $S$ of the Riccati-type equation $X(S)=S^2+phi_z S-phi_y$ along the total-derivative field $X$. The standard ansatz $S=P/N^k$, with $N=den(phi)$, misses every $S$ with poles outside $N=0$. Such singular solutions cannot be avoided: for point transforms of linear equations without hyperexponential solutions we describe every quasi-regular $S$ explicitly, and for a generic transformation none exists.
arxiv:2611.33518.authors: L. G. S. Duarte, L. A. C. P. da Mota

arxiv:2611.33530.title: Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques
arxiv:2611.33530.summary: We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory. We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules.

arxiv:2611.33535.title: Inverses of split graphs via Ferrers diagrams and degree sequences
arxiv:2611.33535.summary: A graph is a split graph if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and a stable set and is a partitioned split graph if the partition is also specified. The inverse of a partitioned split graph is formed by removing all edges within the clique and adding all edges between vertices in the stable set, while preserving the edges between the two parts. In this paper we compare two forms of the degree sequence of a graph: the conventional form and the block representation.
arxiv:2611.33535.authors: Karen L. Collins, Tantan Dai, Ann N. Trenk

arxiv:2611.33540.title: Graphon hitting times: connectivity and minimum degree
arxiv:2611.33540.summary: A classical result in random graphs states that the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process becomes connected at exactly the moment its last isolated vertex disappears. The main goal of this paper is to establish a graphon analogue of this result. Let $G(n,W)$ be the inhomogeneous random graph sampled from a graphon $W$, and reveal its edges one by one in a uniformly random order.
arxiv:2611.33540.authors: Constanza Gacit\'ua Fuentes, Marcos Kiwi, Mat\'ias Pavez-Sign\'e

arxiv:2611.33548.title: Helly complexes are minimal fillings
arxiv:2611.33548.summary: We show that Helly complexes are universal minimal fillings. More precisely, if $X$ is a Helly complex, and $Y$ is a simplicial complex whose boundary is isomorphic to that of $X$ and such that the distances between the boundary vertices induced by $Y$ are at least as large as those induced by $X$, then $Y$ has at least as many vertices as $X$. The same type of inequalities hold for $i$-dimensional simplices of $X$ and $Y$ for all $i=0,1,\ldots$, i.e., for all coordinates of the $f$-vectors of $X$ and $Y$.
arxiv:2611.33548.authors: Mart\'in Blufstein, J\'er\'emie Chalopin, Victor Chepoi

arxiv:2611.33552.title: Link invariants from charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators
arxiv:2611.33552.summary: Turaev's enhanced Yang--Baxter operators produce invariants of oriented links from solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation. If the enhancing endomorphism is diagonal with generic eigenvalues, Turaev's compatibility condition forces the Yang--Baxter operator $R$ to be charge-conserving, that is, to send each $e_i\otimes e_j$ into the span of $e_i\otimes e_j$ and $e_j\otimes e_i$. Charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators were classified by Martin and Rowell.

arxiv:2611.33558.title: Deleted square of a cone over a graph
arxiv:2611.33558.summary: The deleted square of a topological space is a subspace of the Cartesian product of this space with itself, obtained by removing the diagonal. Conjecturally, the deleted square of a cone over a graph has the homotopy type of a wedge sum of spheres of dimensions at most 3. We propose a geometric construction that is a key motivation for the conjecture and provides a major step towards its proof, while yielding direct results on deleted squares of certain families of graphs.

arxiv:2611.33568.title: Controlability of the 1D wave equation by point sources: outgoing states, circle rotations and small divisors
arxiv:2611.33568.summary: We characterise the states reachable from rest for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line driven by finitely many fixed point sources. The characterisation reduces the control problem to a cohomological equation on a circle whose length is twice the distance between the outermost sources, with support constraints determined by the control time. For two sources, the reachable set is closed and the controls are unique at every finite time.

arxiv:2611.33569.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
arxiv:2611.33569.summary: Every finite population is eventually driven to extinction by demographic noise, even when the deterministic dynamics have a stable coexistence state. We develop a large-deviation theory of this process for hierarchical food webs of arbitrary size. In a community of $N$ species, the basal species $X_1$ reproduces intrinsically and every consumer may prey on all species below it, so that omnivory is built into the interaction graph.
arxiv:2611.33569.authors: Varun Nevash, Eric Forgoston, M. Ani Hsieh

arxiv:2611.33572.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
arxiv:2611.33572.summary: The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$.

arxiv:2611.33575.title: Reflections in graphs
arxiv:2611.33575.summary: We introduce and study an operation on graphs, called edge reflection, modeled on the effect of a reflection on the inversion graph of a permutation. The edge reflection length of a graph counts the fewest edge reflections needed to reduce it to the edgeless graph. Emptying a graph one edge at a time, or one vertex at a time, gives two upper bounds on this length, and each holds with equality precisely when the graph is a forest.
arxiv:2611.33575.authors: Sean Mandrick, Bridget Eileen Tenner, Vincent Vatter

arxiv:2611.33597.title: Proof of a cardinality conjecture for the correction terms in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom
arxiv:2611.33597.summary: We prove a conjecture due to Kato and Sagaki (arXiv:2604.04476) concerning the cardinality of sets of directed paths in the quantum Bruhat graph that occur in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom for the full flag manifolds in the quasi-minuscule case. We prove that the cadinality is equal to one or even, and its signed sum vanishes in the latter case. Consequently, the cancellation-free divisor axiom obtained by Kato and Sagaki under this conjecture holds unconditionally.

arxiv:2611.33631.title: Extension complexity is not additive under Cartesian products
arxiv:2611.33631.summary: We prove that the linear extension complexity of a Cartesian product of polytopes can be strictly smaller than the sum of the extension complexities of its factors. This disproves Conjecture 1.2 of Grande, Padrol and Sanyal. We construct a rational 24-dimensional polytope $P$ with 50 facets and 150 vertices such that $P$ has extension complexity 40 and $P \times P$ has extension complexity exactly 79.

arxiv:2611.33638.title: Simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over finite fields
arxiv:2611.33638.summary: In this paper we provide a partial classification (necessary conditions) for all possible simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $A$ be such an abelian variety, i.e. $A$ is simple over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and splits as $A \sim B^s$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ for some simple abelian variety $B$.

arxiv:2611.33663.title: Graded Monoidal Categories and Internalization
arxiv:2611.33663.summary: In stable homotopy theory, there are a variety of ways to construct a point-set level smash product of spectra, each with its own advantages and limitations. These constructions often involve internalizing some graded external product. In this paper, we aim to formalize this process through a general categorical framework, providing a common language for these constructions.

arxiv:2611.33669.title: A fake quadric that is not a bidisk quotient
arxiv:2611.33669.summary: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a construction of a fake quadric $S$ that is a $32$-fold branched cover of $\mathbf{CP}^1\times\mathbf{CP}^1$ along nine curves. This configuration is given by four horizontal lines, four vertical lines and the diagonal.

arxiv:2611.33681.title: Generalized oriented chromatic numbers and directed generalized coloring numbers of graphs
arxiv:2611.33681.summary: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $q$, we bound the $q$-transitive oriented chromatic number $\chi_o^q(G)$ in terms of the directed weak coloring number $\overrightarrow{wcol}_{2q}(G)$. For orientations with no directed cycle of length at most $2q$, we compare $q$-transitive oriented colorings with $\vec P_{2q}$-preserving oriented colorings. We also show that the directed strong coloring number at radius $2k-1$ bounds the density of every depth-$(k-1)$ shallow topological minor of $G$.
arxiv:2611.33681.authors: Wenwen Li, Jaroslav Nesetril, Daqing Yang

arxiv:2611.33685.title: The maximum number of triangles in a graph without pentagons
arxiv:2611.33685.summary: The generalized Tur\'an number $\ex(n,T,H)$ is the maximum number of $T$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no $H$. Inspired by a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s on the function $\ex(n,C_5,K_3)$, Bollob\'as and Gy\H ori proposed the problem of $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)$. In this paper, we prove that $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)=(1/(3\sqrt3)+o(1))n^{3/2}$, finally solved this problem.
arxiv:2611.33685.authors: Qing Cui, Ervin Gy\H{o}ri, Chenke Zhang, Xiutao Zhu

arxiv:2611.33694.title: Topological Clique Exclusion in Positively Curved Graphs
arxiv:2611.33694.summary: We study locally finite graphs of positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and minimum degree at least $t-1$ under two exclusions: a topological $K_t$, denoted $TK_t$, and its locally topological version $TK^{(\leq2)}_t$, in which every replacement path has length at most two. The ordinary exclusion gives an $O(t^{7})$ maximum-degree bound by combining the classical density theorem for topological cliques with a curvature-driven rainbow-clique argument. For $K_t$-minor-free graphs, a Hall-matching refinement improves the maximum-degree bound to $O(t^3(\log t)^{3/2})$ and, for connected graphs, the order bound to $O(t^{19}(\log t)^9)$.

arxiv:2611.33697.title: Singularities in global pluripotential theory
arxiv:2611.33697.summary: This book is an expanded version of the author's lecture notes at the Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (IASM) at Zhejiang University. We systematically develop the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities on compact K\"ahler manifolds and relate it to the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and toric pluripotential theory.

arxiv:2611.33701.title: Low treebandwidth colorings, $p$-centred colorings and generalized coloring numbers
arxiv:2611.33701.summary: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $p$, let $\chi^{tb}_p(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in a vertex coloring such that every subgraph induced by $i$ color classes has treebandwidth at most $i-1$, for $1\le i\le p$. We establish quantitative relationships between these coloring parameters and generalized coloring numbers. If $\operatorname{wcol}_{2p}(G)\le m$, then $G$ admits a $p$-centred coloring with at most $[(p+1)m]^m$ colors; in particular, $\chi^{tb}_p(G)\le[(p+1)m]^m$.

arxiv:2611.33753.title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
arxiv:2611.33753.summary: Ternary binding systems occur in signaling, scaffold-mediated assembly, and targeted protein degradation. A mediator brings two partners into a productive ternary complex, but excess mediator can hold them in separate binary complexes. Consequently, ternary complex formation can increase and then decrease as the mediator dose increases, producing the hook effect.

arxiv:2611.33771.title: Semiorthogonal decompositions of limit categories for symmetric stacks
arxiv:2611.33771.summary: In our earlier work with Tudor Padurariu, we introduced the notion of limit categories for derived stacks with self-dual cotangent complexes and used them to formulate the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture. In this paper, we generalize the notion of limit categories to a broader class of derived stacks, which we call symmetric stacks. One of the motivations for this generalization is to formulate Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type correspondences for a broader class of moduli stacks.

arxiv:2611.33778.title: The Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for smooth surfaces
arxiv:2611.33778.summary: Using a general theory of limit categories for symmetric stacks, we construct their semiorthogonal decompositions for moduli stacks of pure one-dimensional coherent sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors. The components of these semiorthogonal decompositions are quasi-BPS categories associated with the corresponding local Calabi--Yau threefolds. By comparing these semiorthogonal decompositions with those of dg-categories of coherent sheaves on moduli stacks of semistable sheaves, we propose a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for surfaces, generalizing the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture for $\GL_r$-Higgs bundles.

arxiv:2611.33780.title: Sections and Constant Fields of Postcritically Finite Rational Maps
arxiv:2611.33780.summary: We relate the constant fields of generic preimage towers to two invariants of geometric monodromy. Bounded section indices characterize branching of the closed action and imply a finite constant extension. Unbounded finite-level abelianization orders force an infinite cyclotomic subextension.

arxiv:2611.33804.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
arxiv:2611.33804.summary: The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, Gonz\'alez's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\le\rho(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $\rho(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary.

arxiv:2611.33825.title: On Grokking and the Dynamics of Generalization
arxiv:2611.33825.summary: We extend the signal-channel theory of grokking introduced by Litman and Guo by relating training dissipation and evaluation transfer to population risk. For preconditioned gradient flows with time-dependent kernels, we distinguish two sources of limited evaluation visibility, namely small cumulative dissipation and weak transfer. We obtain quantitative bounds for task visibility and establish their stability under signal filtering and changes of evaluation distribution.

arxiv:2611.33834.title: Size-preserving Cromwell equivalence for unknotted grid diagrams
arxiv:2611.33834.summary: We demonstrate that every grid diagram representing the unknot is equivalent, via Cromwell moves which preserve the grid number, to a grid diagram with no crossings, sharpening a monotonic-simplification result of Dynnikov. Moreover, we enumerate the equivalence classes of grid diagrams for the unknot, considered up to size-preserving Cromwell moves. As an application, we generate all grid diagrams for the unknot through grid number $8$ and identify the first examples of weakly Cromwell hard grid diagrams for the unknot.
arxiv:2611.33834.authors: Austin Christian, James Rea, Matthew Stark

arxiv:2611.33837.title: Decomposition algorithms for rational curves on real classical groups
arxiv:2611.33837.summary: This paper is devoted to an algorithmic investigation of the decomposition problem for rational curves on real classical groups. The main contributions are: (1) We present two Maple-implemented algorithms for decomposing rational curves on real classical groups. The first algorithm decomposes a curve with multiple poles into a unique product of curves with single poles.
arxiv:2611.33837.authors: Yifan Li, Zijia Li, Ke Ye

arxiv:2611.33838.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
arxiv:2611.33838.summary: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes.

arxiv:2611.33849.title: Data-driven framework for invariant manifold identification in multiscale systems
arxiv:2611.33849.summary: Multiscale dynamical systems often exhibit fast transient behavior followed by slow evolution on a low-dimensional attracting manifold, on which their long-term dynamics unfold. Identifying this structure directly from data remains challenging when the governing equations, Jacobians, and fast-slow variable partitions are unknown. In this work, we propose a fully data-driven framework for timescale decomposition, slow invariant manifold (SIM) approximation, and reduced-order model identification.
arxiv:2611.33849.authors: Dimitris M. Manias, Ismaila Muhammed, Dimitris A. Goussis, Haralampos Hatzikirou

arxiv:2611.33876.title: Fixed points for actions of automorphism groups of free products on ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces
arxiv:2611.33876.summary: We study fixed-point properties of automorphism groups of free products acting on complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces. Under the assumption of certain fixed-point properties of the free factors, we obtain lower bounds on the smallest dimension in which automorphism groups can act on a complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ space without a global fixed point.
arxiv:2611.33876.authors: Qian Chen, Qiang Zhang, Dongxiao Zhao

arxiv:2611.33908.title: The Brauer--Manin obstruction to weak approximation on a constant K3 surface
arxiv:2611.33908.summary: We construct a constant supersingular K3 surface over every global field of characteristic two for which rational points are Zariski dense but are not dense in the Brauer--Manin set. This shows that the analogue of Skorobogatov's conjecture over global function fields does not hold for supersingular K3 surfaces.

arxiv:2611.33921.title: A degree-stability method for the $p$-spectral Tur\'an-type problem for disjoint color-critical graphs
arxiv:2611.33921.summary: Let $F_1,\ldots,F_t$ be pairwise vertex-disjoint color-critical graphs with $\chi(F_i)=r+1$ for each $i\in[t]$. For $r\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits [Discrete Math. 7 (1974) 349--376] proved that the graph $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the number of edges among $n$-vertex graphs containing no copy of $\cup_{i=1}^tF_i$. In 2024, Lei and Li [Electron.
arxiv:2611.33921.authors: Jian Zheng, Ya-Lei Jin, Ming-Zhu Chen, Peng-Li Zhang

arxiv:2611.33966.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
arxiv:2611.33966.summary: There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets.
arxiv:2611.33966.authors: Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, Emily Xia Meng, Henry Kvinge

arxiv:2611.33969.title: Structure Preserving Iterative Solution of Linear Systems Arising in Gauss Collocation for port-Hamiltonian DAEs
arxiv:2611.33969.summary: This work presents structure-preserving computational techniques for the pencil Pad\'e approximation arising in the numerical integration of port-Hamiltonian differential-algebraic equations (pH-DAEs) via the Gauss-Legendre schemes. We first extend the concept of the diagonal Pad\'e approximation and introduce a generalized framework characterizing the $s$-stage Gauss method. We further examine its structural properties and the role of the full orthogonalization method (FOM) in approximating the discrete solution.
arxiv:2611.33969.authors: Malak Diab, Andreas Frommer, Karsten Kahl, Stefan Maier, Nicole Marheineke

arxiv:2611.33976.title: The irreducibility of tame character varieties
arxiv:2611.33976.summary: Tame character varieties are known to be irreducible when the parametrised local systems have monodromies lying in closures of generic conjugacy classes; we will establish their irreducibility without the genericity assumption. A combination of nonabelian Hodge correspondence and variation of parabolic weights reduces the problem to the case of almost generic semi-simple monodromies, which is then treated using a point-counting result of Scognamiglio for nongeneric character stacks. The connectedness result is then used to clarify a couple of facts concerning the symplectic leaves.

arxiv:2611.33994.title: Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings, with applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers
arxiv:2611.33994.summary: We study Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings and give applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers. We realize rational double points of ADE over $W(k)$ as invariant subrings $A^G$, where $A$ is a ramified two-dimensional complete regular local ring and $G$ is a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,W(k)}$. We also prove a general theorem on the existence of Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings: if a flat affine group scheme $G$ over $W(k)$ admits a functorial Reynolds operator and a relative Frobenius lift, then any formal power series ring equipped with a linear action of $G$ admits a Frobenius lift that restricts to a Frobenius lift on the…

arxiv:2611.33997.title: Milk-removal feedback shapes lactation sustainability and daily output in a model of human lactation
arxiv:2611.33997.summary: Milk production during lactation is dynamically regulated by milk removal, yet quantitative models linking feeding or pumping schedules to subsequent production remain scarce. We develop a minimal model describing milk accumulation and production between removal sessions, and the stimulation of subsequent production through milk removal. We compare different assumptions about how stimulation depends on the amount of milk removed or the duration of removal, and consider two removal protocols: prescribing either the removed amount or the removal duration.

arxiv:2611.34034.title: Stochastic extinction: convergence in distribution
arxiv:2611.34034.summary: We develop a general framework to show the convergence in distribution of non-irreducible Markov processes to invariant distributions supported on lower-dimensional subsets of the state space. In applications, these singular supports signal the emergence of distinctive long-time behaviours, such as the extinction of species in ecology and the concentration on laminar states in fluid dynamics. The proposed approach is made widely applicable by tailoring its assumptions so that they can be verified using the theory of stochastic persistence/extinction.
arxiv:2611.34034.authors: Michel Bena\"im, Leo Hahn, Oliver Tough

arxiv:2611.34041.title: The Exact Nef-Curve Cone Formula for dlt Pairs
arxiv:2611.34041.summary: We prove an exact rational-curve formula for the nef-curve cone of every complex projective dlt pair with effective real boundary, answering the related question proposed by Cascini. Every $(K_X+\Delta)$-negative extremal ray is generated by a movable rational curve whose normalization is free in the smooth locus. We reduce the klt case to known results and treat the remaining limiting rays with a new argument based on an orthogonal movable divisor and induction on dimension.

arxiv:2611.34052.title: The asymptotics of maximal rank of three-way tensors
arxiv:2611.34052.summary: We prove that the maximal rank of an $n\times n\times n$ tensor is $n^2/3+O(n^{3/2})$, over the real numbers and over every algebraically closed field. More generally, in format $\lfloor an\rfloor\times\lfloor bn\rfloor\times\lfloor cn\rfloor$, with $a,b,c>0$ fixed, the leading term is $\frac{abc}{a+b+c}n^2$. The argument starts with a criterion for rank with respect to an arbitrary projective variety: a decomposition of zero with surjective differential, from a smooth parameter space, bounds the rank of every point.

arxiv:2611.34086.title: On canonical projections of the bipartite graph $D(k,q)$
arxiv:2611.34086.summary: The bipartite graphs $D(k,q)$, constructed by Lazebnik et al. in 1995, are $q$-regular, edge-transitive, and of large girth. In this paper, we primarily instigate the canonical projections of $D(k,q)$. First, as a generalization of $D(k,q)$, we define a bipartite graph $\Gamma(\Omega,q)$, where $\Omega$, referred to as a rooted binary tree, is a finite subset of binary sequences closed under the deletion of any suffix.
arxiv:2611.34086.authors: Chen Zhang, Xiaoyan Cheng, Yuansheng Tang, Ming Xu

arxiv:2611.34103.title: From Limit Theorems to Mixing Limit Theorems
arxiv:2611.34103.summary: Following the work of Gou\"ezel, we give an alternative proof, under weaker assumptions, of a result of Arana-Herrera and Forni, which provides a general method for upgrading limit theorems for cocycles over dynamical systems to mixing limit theorems.

arxiv:2611.34110.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
arxiv:2611.34110.summary: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

arxiv:2611.34114.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gr\"obner elimination and graph combinatorics
arxiv:2611.34114.summary: Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gr\"obner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set.

arxiv:2611.34165.title: Entropic continuity of Lyapunov exponents in arbitrary dimension
arxiv:2611.34165.summary: We prove that the sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents is entropically continuous for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism, provided the entropy exceeds its second-largest exterior growth rate. We also establish stable strong positive recurrence and show that the topological entropy is continuous, and the number of ergodic measures of maximal entropy is upper semicontinuous. This extends the result of Buzzi, Crovisier, and Sarig to arbitrary dimensions.
arxiv:2611.34165.authors: David Burguet, Gang Liao, Yao Tong

arxiv:2611.34167.title: A general upper bound on broadcast function ${{B(n)}}$ using Kn{\"o}del graph
arxiv:2611.34167.summary: Broadcasting in a graph is the process of transmitting a message from one vertex, the originator, to all other vertices. We consider the classical model in which an informed vertex informs one of its uninformed neighbours during each time unit. A broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a graph in which broadcasting can finish in ${\lceil \log_{2} n \rceil}$ time units from any originator.
arxiv:2611.34167.authors: Sirma Cagil Altay, Mohammadhossein Fakharan, Hovhannes A. Harutyunyan

arxiv:2611.34174.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
arxiv:2611.34174.summary: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively.
arxiv:2611.34174.authors: Koushik Brahma, Takeshi Ikeda, Mark Shimozono

arxiv:2611.34180.title: A note on characterization of S4 x C2^n
arxiv:2611.34180.summary: For every non-negative integer n, we characterize S4 x C2^n by its poset of isomorphic classes of subgroups. This provides an infinite family of counterexamples to the conjectures posed by Tarnauceanu in [8] and [9].

arxiv:2611.34186.title: Independence of Thurston eigenvalues and Lyapunov exponents for quadratic rational maps
arxiv:2611.34186.summary: We study post-critically finite quadratic rational maps $f: \mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ where the two critical points lie in the same cycle. The Thurston eigenvalues of $f$ are those of the derivative of the Thurston pullback map $\sigma_f$ at its fixed point. Addressing questions of Buff--Epstein--Koch, we construct a sequence of real, bitransitive centres in the critical orbit relation curve $C_2$ which degenerates in moduli space, and whose Lyapunov exponents tend to infinity whilst the Thurston eigenvalues satisfy $\frac{1}{10}< |\lambda|<1$.

arxiv:2611.34200.title: Norm groups of orders and the algebraic unknotting number
arxiv:2611.34200.summary: We use number-theoretic tools to find an explicit and effective obstruction for a knot to have algebraic unknotting number equal to $1$. As an example, we show that the connected sum of $T(2,5)$ (the cinquefoil) and $-T(2,3)$ (the negative trefoil) has algebraic unknotting number $1$, even though $T(2,5)$ has algebraic unknotting number $2$.

arxiv:2611.34216.title: Ramification divisors and twisted Nambu brackets of Keller maps
arxiv:2611.34216.summary: For a polynomial map $\phi\colon\A^n\to\A^n$ we study the Yau twist of the Jacobian Nambu bracket by $\phi^*$. The Hamiltonian fields of pulled back functions span the image of the adjugate of $d\phi$, so the twist detects the ramification divisor of $\phi$. For a Keller map $F$ the twist is removable exactly when $F$ is an automorphism; otherwise $F$ is not proper, and every projective extension of $F$ has a non-zero effective ramification divisor supported on the boundary, whose image is the non-properness set.
arxiv:2611.34216.authors: Geoffrey Mboya, Stephen Mboya, Carringtone Kinyanjui

arxiv:2611.34231.title: Regularity Criteria for Ind-Sheaves
arxiv:2611.34231.summary: In this paper, we prove the Kashiwara-Schapira regularity conjecture [Conjecture 6.4, Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity, 2003] in arbitrary dimension. For this purpose, we show that under suitable finiteness and isotropic micro-support conditions, ind-sheaves which are regular on the zero section come from $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaves. Furthermore, we characterize the essential image of constructible sheaves under the natural embedding functor, and relate them to regular holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules via the regular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence.

arxiv:2611.34251.title: Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
arxiv:2611.34251.summary: We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals.
arxiv:2611.34251.authors: Vadim Kaloshin, Illya Koval, Daniel Tsodikovich

arxiv:2611.34253.title: Development of a GPU-accelerated numerical simulation model for liver infection in realistic domains
arxiv:2611.34253.summary: Viral hepatitis reduces the functionality of the liver and constitutes a major global health concern because it oftentimes evolves to chronic inflammation leading to long term liver damage. Mathematical models on a mesoscopic scale abstract from only partly known cell-scale processes while providing an in-silico tool for understanding tissue-scale development of the disease. In this work, we investigate the interactions between virus and immune cells in a realistic three-dimensional liver geometries by using a reaction-diffusion model that reproduces infection courses with cure and with chronic developments.
arxiv:2611.34253.authors: Eva Cirujeda, Adri\'an Navas-Montilla, Cordula Reisch

arxiv:2611.34269.title: Degree-respecting labellings with ordered neighbour sums
arxiv:2611.34269.summary: In an exhaustive enumeration of hydrocarbons with only single bonds, carbon skeletons are generated as adjacency matrices and pruned by two rules: a vertex of larger degree receives a smaller label, and among vertices of equal degree, a vertex whose adjacency row is the larger binary integer receives a smaller label. The pruning is sound only if every skeleton admits a labelling obeying both rules. We prove that such a labelling exists for every finite simple graph, connected or not and with no bound on the degrees, and that the same holds when the weights $2^i$ of the labels $i$ are replaced by any strictly increasing real weights.

arxiv:2611.34282.title: Irreducible trinomials over the binary field: an elliptic-curve criterion and explicit families
arxiv:2611.34282.summary: We study irreducible trinomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Using an elliptic curve and reciprocity laws, we prove that, for $k \ge 2$, $X^{(4^k+2)/3}+X+1$ is irreducible if and only if $4^k+3$ is prime and $2$ is a primitive root modulo that prime. By power substitution and linearization, we also assemble explicit infinite families of irreducible trinomials $X^m+X^n+1$ in fourteen distinct reduced exponent classes.
arxiv:2611.34282.authors: Siyuan Fu, Zhiming Li, Huaiqing Zuo

arxiv:2611.34289.title: A Short Proof of the Goldman--Parker Conjecture
arxiv:2611.34289.summary: Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres. We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction.

arxiv:2611.34295.title: The hitting time index: bounds, a sharp threshold, the proof of a conjecture and the disproof of another conjecture
arxiv:2611.34295.summary: We prove some new upper and lower bounds for the hitting time index ($HT$ index) of an $n$-vertex graph, showing along the way that the largest order of the index is $n^5$ and the smallest is $n^3$. More specifically, we prove the conjecture that the smallest value of the index is $\frac{n(n-1)^2}{2}$, which is attained by the complete graph. We also find a sharp threshold for the minimal degree $\delta$ so that the $HT$ index goes from an $n^4$ order to an $n^3$ order if the threshold is surpassed.
arxiv:2611.34295.authors: Jos\'e Luis Palacios, Shunya Tamura, Jason Wiberg, Aleksandar Petojevi\'c

arxiv:2611.34299.title: Cooperative colorings of cycles and uniform cycle factors
arxiv:2611.34299.summary: A cooperative coloring of graphs on a common vertex set is a choice of one independent set in each graph such that their union covers the vertex set. We give a combinatorial proof that three cycles on a common vertex set always have a cooperative coloring. We also prove that, for every $\ell\geq4$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$, there are three graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, with no cooperative coloring.
arxiv:2611.34299.authors: Xuqing Bai, Zhipeng Gao, Bi Li, Xin Zhang

arxiv:2611.34307.title: The $k$-disjoint paths problem for group-labelled graphs
arxiv:2611.34307.summary: A $\Gamma$-labelled graph is an oriented graph with edge labels in a group $\Gamma$. Fix a finite abelian group $\Gamma$ and a positive integer $k$. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that finds $k$ vertex-disjoint paths joining prescribed pairs with a prescribed gain on each path, or determines that none exist.

arxiv:2611.34308.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
arxiv:2611.34308.summary: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $\Gamma$ of affine isometries.

arxiv:2611.34315.title: The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality
arxiv:2611.34315.summary: Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincar\'e duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordstr\"om, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and L\^e, in [Ann.

arxiv:2611.34317.title: Generic bi-stochastic semigroups are flows
arxiv:2611.34317.summary: We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, \mu)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, \mu)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, \mu)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces.

arxiv:2611.34318.title: Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts

arxiv:2611.34333.title: Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
arxiv:2611.34333.summary: We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics.
arxiv:2611.34333.authors: Christopher Chalhoub, Jeroen S. W. Lamb, Martin Rasmussen

arxiv:2611.34336.title: Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree
arxiv:2611.34336.summary: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support of $N=n+k+1$ monomials, and we study the topological degree of $F$ on the positive orthant. In a previous paper we computed this topological degree in terms of signs of maximal minors, under a half-space condition which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. Here we use these formulas, together with their translation on the Gale dual side, to bound the topological degree.

arxiv:2611.34342.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds
arxiv:2611.34342.summary: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group.

arxiv:2611.34348.title: List coloring degenerate graphs with requests
arxiv:2611.34348.summary: We prove three results on the flexible list coloring of $d$-degenerate graphs. Following Dvo\v{r}\'{a}k, Norin and Postle [J. Graph Theory 2019], a graph $G$ is $(k,\epsilon)$-flexible if for any assignment $L$ of lists of size $k$ to its vertices and any choice of requested colors by a set $\widehat V$ of the vertices from their respective lists, there is an $L$-coloring satisfying at least $\epsilon|\widehat V|$ of the requests.
arxiv:2611.34348.authors: Rajat Adak, L. Sunil Chandran, Shiwali Gupta, Tom\'a\v{s} Kaiser, Subrahmanyam Kalyanasundaram, Rogers Mathew, Saraswati Girish Nanoti, Suraj Kumar Sahoo, Umesh Shankar, Joel M. Thomas

arxiv:2611.34353.title: Ergodicity of the mapping class group action on components with small nonzero Euler number
arxiv:2611.34353.summary: We study the action of the mapping class group on the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ character variety of a closed oriented surface of genus $g$. On the components considered here, the infimum of the translation lengths of essential simple closed curves is zero almost everywhere for every invariant positive Radon measure. For Goldman measure we show that almost every character sends some such curve to a non-hyperbolic element.

arxiv:2611.34357.title: Propagation failure for bistable differential equations on periodic trees
arxiv:2611.34357.summary: We study traveling fronts for bistable reaction-diffusion equations on periodic heterogeneous trees. We use comparison principles to estimate the pinning and propagation regions for both cubic and general bistabilities. Our analytical results and numerical simulations show that the interesting propagation reversal effects found in homogeneous trees become more pronounced in the heterogeneous setting, paving the way towards understanding more general graphs.
arxiv:2611.34357.authors: Hermen Jan Hupkes, Petr Stehl\'{\i}k, Vladim\'{\i}r \v{S}v\'{\i}gler, Jialing Yu

arxiv:2611.34386.title: Optimal bounds for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-constant-power error-correcting cooling codes
arxiv:2611.34386.summary: High temperatures have dramatic negative effects on interconnect performance. In a bus, whenever a wire changes its state from ``0'' to ``1'' or from ``1'' to ``0'', Joule heating causes the temperature to rise. Constant-power error-correcting cooling (CPECC) codes, introduced in [IEEE Trans.
arxiv:2611.34386.authors: Shuangqing Liu, Qianfei Zhang, Shikang Yu, Menglong Zhang, Lijun Ji

arxiv:2611.34425.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes I: Exact Enumeration and Generic Achiral Symmetry
arxiv:2611.34425.summary: We give an exact arithmetic formula for the number of classical fullerenes on $2m$ vertices. The oriented count is known; the new contribution counts achiral fullerenes, those admitting an orientation-reversing symmetry. We transport these symmetries to a lattice, classify eleven types, and express their contribution as seven weighted orbit counts.

arxiv:2611.34431.title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
arxiv:2611.34431.summary: We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains.

arxiv:2611.34434.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes VII: Arithmetic Unranking of Fullerene Isomers
arxiv:2611.34434.summary: Given a vertex number $2m$ and a rank, we construct the corresponding ordinary fullerene as a planar adjacency list. Choosing the rank uniformly therefore samples ordinary isomorphism classes exactly from the vertex number alone. We select an integral period by counting lattice points on a quadratic level in polytopes with fixed facet directions.

arxiv:2611.34437.title: Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
arxiv:2611.34437.summary: We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincar\'e maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections.
arxiv:2611.34437.authors: Miquel Barcelona, Joan Gimeno, Marc Jorba-Cusc\'o

arxiv:2611.34477.title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
arxiv:2611.34477.summary: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.

arxiv:2611.34498.title: On dual varieties of smooth projective varieties
arxiv:2611.34498.summary: For a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective variety $X\subsetneq\mathbb P^N$, we prove that its projective dual $X^\vee$ is a hypersurface whenever $\operatorname{dim} X\ge3\operatorname{codim}X-2$. This result may be regarded as further evidence for Hartshorne's complete intersection conjecture. We also prove the duality defect conjecture of Landman in codimension at most five.

arxiv:2611.34514.title: Limit laws for Siegel theta sums
arxiv:2611.34514.summary: Siegel theta sums are exponential sums over the integer lattice whose phases are determined by a quadratic form. For a random choice of quadratic form, we prove a limit law for the modulus of the normalised sum as the summation range tends to infinity. The limiting distribution depends on the space from which the quadratic form is sampled.
arxiv:2611.34514.authors: Jory Griffin, Jens Marklof, Tariq Osman

arxiv:2611.34537.title: Hall's condition between adjacent levels of the face lattice of the permutohedron
arxiv:2611.34537.summary: Let $\OP$ be the poset of ordered set partitions of $[n]$, ordered by merging adjacent blocks; with a bottom element adjoined it is the face lattice of the permutohedron. Whether it has the Sperner property is open. We show that for every pair of adjacent levels, the smaller one can be matched into the larger one by parent--child pairs, except possibly for the pairs $(j,j+1)$ with $(28n-36)/39<j<(13n+5)/18$ (for small $n$ the window is slightly smaller still).

arxiv:2611.34570.title: Cohomology of pseudo-reductive groups over local function fields
arxiv:2611.34570.summary: We give a pairing which describes the first Galois cohomology of a pseudo-reductive group $G$ over a local function field $K$ as the Pontryagin dual of the group $\Ext^1(G, \Gm)$ of translation-invariant line bundles on $G$. In order to accomplish this, we endow the Picard group of a scheme $X$ over a (Hausdorff) topological field with a topology, and prove that this topology enjoys favorable properties under certain mild conditions on $X$ and on the field.

arxiv:2611.34580.title: On the Gorenstein property of local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$
arxiv:2611.34580.summary: Local models are used to model, \'etale-locally, the singularities of integral models of Shimura varieties. They are defined in terms of linear algebra and admit explicit descriptions by matrix equations. We determine exactly which local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ are Gorenstein.

arxiv:2611.34594.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
arxiv:2611.34594.summary: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces.

arxiv:2611.34596.title: Higher rewriting for strong linearly distributive coherence
arxiv:2611.34596.summary: Rewriting is a computational method to solve word problems: deciding whether two compound expressions, or words, are equivalent with respect to a set of identities. Higher rewriting generalizes rewriting to higher-dimensional words, or cells, in higher categories. Following Guiraud and Malbos, we use higher rewriting to generalize Mac Lane's coherence theorem.
arxiv:2611.34596.authors: Max Demirdilek, Christian Reiher, Christoph Schweigert

arxiv:2611.34606.title: A Finite Automaton Translating Geometric Addresses into Dynamical Itineraries on the Basilica
arxiv:2611.34606.summary: Fractals are generally known for their self-similarity and repeating patterns. One way to produce fractals is via the dynamics of functions from the extended complex plane to itself. These fractals are known as Julia sets.

arxiv:2611.34609.title: The Brownian L\'evy transformation is exact
arxiv:2611.34609.summary: We prove that the L\'evy transformation of Brownian motion is exact. This settles the long-standing question of whether the transformation is ergodic. The proof combines an interval cutting argument with an estimate for the first entrance of the iterated paths into a small neighborhood of zero at an independent exponential time.

arxiv:2611.34620.title: Induced Independence Levels and Signed Enumeration in Powers of Cycles
arxiv:2611.34620.summary: For a graph $G$ we study the distribution of the independence numbers $\alpha(G[S])$ over its vertex-induced subgraphs, together with signed Boolean-lattice sums over fixed independence-number levels. For the $r$th power $C_n^r$ of a cycle, we establish, in the range $n\ge 2rk+r+1$, a unique representation of each subset $S$ with $\alpha(C_n^r[S])=k$ by an independent $k$-set and its forward neighborhood. The resulting Boolean-interval partition gives exact enumeration by subset cardinality.

arxiv:2611.34654.title: Connectedness Principle in the Complex Analytic Setting
arxiv:2611.34654.summary: We show that if $(X,B)$ is a normal compact K\"ahler pair and $f:X\to Z$ is a proper morphism with connected fibers to a normal compact K\"ahler variety $Z$ such that $(-K_X+B)$ is nef over $Z$, then $\mathrm{Nklt}(X,B)\cap f^{-1}(z)$ has at most two connected components for every $z\in Z$. More generally, we prove the result for generalized pairs whose nef part is allowed to be transcendental. Moreover, we record that the same result holds for projective morphism between analytic varieties (possibly non-compact).

arxiv:2611.34697.title: Symplectic bumpless pipe dreams
arxiv:2611.34697.summary: Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety.

arxiv:2611.34710.title: Toward a human-friendly proof of a polynomial bound for the Directed Grid Theorem
arxiv:2611.34710.summary: The Directed Grid Theorem of Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC 2015] states that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every digraph of directed treewidth at least $f(k)$ contains a cylindrical grid of order $k$ as a butterfly minor. Their function is not elementary, and Hatzel, Kreutzer, Garlet Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] improved it to a tower of exponentials of height $22$, by a proof in three stages through paths and cycles of well-linked sets. In this paper we prove each stage with a polynomial bound, so that $f$ can be chosen to be a polynomial of degree $20\,031\,568$.
arxiv:2611.34710.authors: Victor Campos, Allen Ibiapina, Raul Lopes, Rodrigo Nogueira, Ignasi Sau

arxiv:2611.34736.title: On the Density of Repeated Entries in Pascal's Triangle
arxiv:2611.34736.summary: Let $N(a)$ denote the number of occurrences of the integer $a>1$ in Pascal's triangle, and set ${\mathcal E}_H=\{a\geq3:N(a)>2H\}$, $A_H(x)=|{\mathcal E}_H\cap[1,x]|.$ For every fixed $K\geq2$ we prove the expansion $A_1(x)=\sum_{k=2}^{K}(k!x)^{1/k}+O_K\!\left(x^{1/(K+1)}\right).$ Consequently, the Dirichlet series ${D}_1(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_1}a^{-s}$ extends meromorphically to $\Re s>0$, with simple poles precisely at $s=1/k$, $k\geq2$, of residue $(k!)^{1/k}/k$. For every $H\geq2$, $x\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove $A_H(x)\le A_2(x)\leq\exp\left(\frac{2\log x}{(\log\log x)^{1/4}}\right)\ll_{\varepsilon} x^{\varepsilon}.$ Hence $D_H(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_H}a^{-s}$ is…

arxiv:2611.34737.title: Recursive Word Conditioning for Higher-Dimensional Partitions: Exact Enumeration and Complexity
arxiv:2611.34737.summary: Let $p_d(n)$ denote the number of $d$-dimensional partitions of weight $n$. We develop an exact enumeration method operating on recursively parsed partition words (which are shown to encode $d$-dimensional partitions), beginning with an elementary interior-part decomposition of ordinary partitions. Conditioning on an interior word block separates the preceding and succeeding nested blocks.

arxiv:2611.34744.title: Prevalence of the periodicity of maximizing measures
arxiv:2611.34744.summary: For a continuous map $T\colon X\rightarrow X$ on a compact metric space $(X,d)$, we say that a function $f\colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ has the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ if its time averages along forward orbits of $T$ are maximized at a periodic orbit. In this article, we establish the Hunt--Ott conjecture (cf.~\cite{HO96a,HO96b}), that is, the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ is prevalent (in the sense of Hunt--Sauer--Yorke) in the space of Lipschitz functions with respect to a standard metric for subshifts of finite type. This result is a strengthening of \cite[Theorem~A]{BZ16} and \cite[Theorem~1.1]{DLZ24}, confirms the prediction mentioned in the ICM proceeding contribution of Bochi…
arxiv:2611.34744.authors: Zelai Hao, Illya Koval, Zhiqiang Li

arxiv:2611.34749.title: Weitzenbeock's theorem in arbitrary characteristic
arxiv:2611.34749.summary: Let \(k\) be a field and \(V\) a finite-dimensional rational representation of the additive group \(\GG_{a,k}\). We show that the ring of invariants \(k[V]^{\GG_a}\) is finitely generated in every characteristic, extending Weitzenb\"ock's classical theorem beyond characteristic zero.

arxiv:2611.34768.title: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
arxiv:2611.34768.summary: We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts. Second, approximate the full evolution operator using a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki (LTS) decomposition of the desired approximation order in time step.
arxiv:2611.34768.authors: Ilon Joseph, Ivan Novikau, Michael R. Montgomery, Joanna Slawinska, Dimitrios Giannakis

arxiv:2611.34774.title: Zero-cycles and holomorphic forms in families
arxiv:2611.34774.summary: We establish parallel Chow and Hodge-theoretic rigidity theorems for dominant projective morphisms between smooth complex varieties. For instance, if the general fiber satisfies $CH_0(F) = \mathbb{Z}$, then the same is true of every fiber. Similarly, if the general fiber is connected with $H^0(F, \Omega_F^p) = 0$ for $p > 0$, then the same is true of every fiber.

arxiv:2611.34784.title: Territorial Conflict as a Cellular Automaton: Frozen Domains and Active Fronts in a Risk-Derived Local Rule
arxiv:2611.34784.summary: We formulate the attack and fortification rules of the game Risk as a synchronous cellular automaton on a graph, with battles resolved by exact dice odds. We prove, and verify in Lean, that for the default exchange ratio the rule has radius 6, or 5 for deterministic battles with a positive attack threshold, both attained; that its deterministic form is irreversible except at the highest attack thresholds without growth and with fortification absent or inactive; that without troop growth it freezes in finite time; and that the dynamics near an interface is locally determined. The coupling of the ownership field to a troop field separates frozen domains from active fronts: with a positive…

arxiv:2611.34787.title: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
arxiv:2611.34787.summary: We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property. By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the…

arxiv:2611.34794.title: Monoid Representation of the Determinants of the Adjacency Matrices of 1-joined Path Graphs
